- This is an ADDITIONAL loading path alongside the existing flat kind/label binding files (t2db.9/.10/.11). Do NOT modify workflow.Route(), workflow.workflowForLabels, or remove/change the existing single-file/multi-dir binding loaders. Migrating Route() onto the new mechanism is a separate, later, larger decision -- not in scope here.
- Idempotency is free for this slice for the same reason it was free for t2db.13's first Module slice: a single workflow-kind action reaches the exact same workflow.Registry dispatch path that already carries TaskEnvelope's idempotency key. Nothing new to design here.
design:
Depends on archie-core-t2db.14 (expr package) -- do not start until it is closed and verified.

1. Playbook document type (new package, likely internal/domain/eda/playbook -- confirm against organisation.md's layout rule, follow the log/logextract split precedent from t2db.13 if a generated component turns out to be needed, though this ticket is pure YAML+CEL, no Yaegi, so likely no extract package is needed here):
   - trigger: reuse existing workintake label/kind matching (do not invent a second label-matching mechanism -- workintake.SplitLabels/KindsForLabels already exist and are the one place this vocabulary lives).
   - actions: a list, validated at load to contain exactly one entry with position: workflow and a workflow registry name.
   - when: optional CEL expression string on the action, compiled via t2db.14's Compile() at load time -- a compile failure is a reported load failure (same collision-handling philosophy as t2db.9-.12), not a silently-skipped playbook.
2. Event coordinator: loads playbook files from a configured directory (mirror the PlaybookDirs pattern from t2db.11 -- reuse its directory-scanning shape, do not reinvent), compiles every playbook's when expression at load (fail the whole load on any compile error, consistent with the existing reject-at-load rule), and at dispatch time: match trigger against an incoming task's labels/kind, evaluate when (if present) against a context of {event: <task's label/kind fields, whatever is cheaply available -- do not over-engineer the event shape beyond what a workflow-kind dispatch actually needs>, actions: {} (empty -- no prior actions exist in a single-action playbook)}, and if the condition is true (or absent), dispatch to the named workflow via the existing workflow.Registry -- call the same registry lookup Route() already uses, do not duplicate dispatch logic.
3. Config: a directory field for these playbook documents (distinct from t2db.11's PlaybookDirs, which holds flat binding files -- naming these two similar-but-different directories clearly is important; suggest something like EDAPlaybookDir or clarify in the field doc comment exactly how it differs from PlaybookDirs so a future reader isn't confused). If you judge the distinction is confusing enough that these should share one directory with two file shapes distinguished by content, flag that as a note in the PRD rather than silently deciding it -- but implement SOMETHING reasonable rather than blocking.
4. Bootstrap wiring: load-and-abort on failure, matching every other slice's established pattern.
5. Do NOT wire this into production task intake (daemon.go/pollNATS/publishTask) in this ticket -- prove the coordinator end-to-end with tests that construct a task-like input directly, the same way t2db.13 proved ModuleRegistry with direct Register/Invoke calls rather than full daemon wiring. Production wiring (making a real forge-triggered task actually flow through this coordinator instead of only workflow.Route()) is explicitly a follow-up ticket -- note it as such when you close this one.
acceptance_criteria: A playbook YAML with trigger + one workflow-kind action + optional when loads successfully and dispatches to the correct registered workflow when trigger+when match. A playbook declaring 2+ actions is a reported load failure. A playbook with a non-workflow action position is a reported load failure. A when expression that compiles but evaluates false at dispatch time correctly skips dispatch (logged, not silently ignored). A when compile failure at load time is reported and the playbook is dropped (same collision-handling shape as prior slices). Existing workflow.Route()/label-binding tests (t2db.9-.12) are unaffected -- run their full test suites and confirm zero regressions. task check passes.
close_reason: Implemented and gate-verified as 2c2b9b7 (pushed to main). internal/domain/eda/playbook: Load (reject-at-load: 2+ actions, non-workflow position, malformed, bad when compile all fail whole load) + Store.Dispatch (trigger match via workintake kind/labels, CEL when eval, named-workflow registry lookup -- same as Route()'s, no duplicated dispatch). EDAPlaybookDir config field (distinct from PlaybookDirs, documented), bootstrap load-and-abort. workflow.Route()/binding loaders untouched; their suites verified zero-regression. 11 tests + shipped example proving end-to-end; task check clean (113/113 UI). FOLLOW-UP TICKET NEEDED (not in this slice, per design): wire Store.Dispatch into production task intake (daemon.go/pollNATS/publishTask) so real forge-triggered tasks flow through the coordinator instead of only workflow.Route(); plus a separate linter/LSP integration ticket for the expr compile path.

title: eda: CEL expression environment (compile/validate at load, evaluate at dispatch)
description:
Sixth slice of docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md, implementing the 'Implementation placement' section of the resolved open question 1 (CEL). Builds internal/domain/eda/expr in isolation, no coordinator/dispatch yet -- mirrors how t2db.13 built ModuleRegistry as a standalone, fully-tested unit before anything consumed it.

This is pure infrastructure for the dispatch slice (t2db.15) that depends on it. No production wiring in this ticket.
design:
Package internal/domain/eda/expr (domain layer: no infrastructure imports).

Per the resolved doc section, build:
1. Environment construction: a CEL env declaring the two context roots -- 'event' as map(string, dyn), 'actions' as map(string, dyn). Cost limit (J5): pick a constant (start at 100,000, name it clearly as a tunable, e.g. DefaultCostLimit) -- exact value is a judgment call already flagged as tunable, don't block on picking the 'right' number.
2. Compile/validate at load: a function taking a CEL expression string and returning (compiled program, error) -- a syntax error, a reference to an unknown root (anything other than event/actions), or exceeding the cost limit is a returned error, never a panic. This is what both the playbook loader (t2db.15) and the lint tool (t2db.12, follow-up integration is a SEPARATE ticket, do not touch cmd/archie-playbooks in this one) will eventually call.
3. Evaluate at dispatch: a function taking a compiled program and a context (event map[string]any, actions map[string]map[string]any) and returning (value, error) -- CEL evaluation errors (missing field, wrong type against a dyn value) are returned as errors, never panics. Use CEL's own panic-free evaluation; do not add a recover() wrapper unless a test proves CEL itself can panic (verify this, don't assume).
4. actions.<id>.result field-level typing (J1/context-conformance in the doc): NOT required in this ticket -- that needs the generated Module Result structs wired in as CEL type declarations, which only matters once a playbook can reference a prior action's result (t2db.15 is single-action, so there IS no prior action). Keep actions declared as dyn for now; note in a comment that per-kind typed declarations are follow-up work once multi-action playbooks exist.
5. Dependency: add cel.dev/cel-go v0.32.0 (pinned) to go.mod -- this is the only new dependency, already vetted (see the resolved doc section's vetting record). Do not re-vet it.

Follow docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md's reject-at-load philosophy throughout: anything not accepted by the schema is a reported error, never a silent default.
acceptance_criteria: internal/domain/eda/expr exists with: environment construction, Compile(expr string) (returned type, error), Eval(program, ctx) (value, error). Table-driven tests cover: a valid boolean expression against event fields evaluates correctly; a syntax error is a Compile-time error; a reference to an unknown root (e.g. 'foo.bar') is a Compile-time error; evaluating against a missing event field does not panic (returns an error or CEL's documented behavior, whichever is correct -- verify against real CEL semantics, don't guess); an expression that would exceed the cost limit is rejected, not silently truncated. go.mod gains cel.dev/cel-go v0.32.0 only. task check passes.
close_reason: Implemented and gate-verified as 33cdece (pushed to main). internal/domain/eda/expr: NewEnv (event+actions roots, DefaultCostLimit 100k), Compile (reject-at-load: syntax/unknown-root/type errors returned), Eval (panic-free, errors returned, ref.Val unwrapped to native). cel.dev/cel-go v0.32.0 direct dep, vetted per resolved doc (no re-vet). 9 tests pass, all verified against real CEL semantics (cost limits accrue on macros; == on missing key is false; unknown root rejected at compile). task check clean (113/113 UI).

title: workflow: Module position first slice (registry + side-effect-free 'log' kind)
description:
Fifth slice of docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md, implementing docs/prds/module-position.md's recommended first slice: prove schema -> go:generate -> Yaegi load -> ModuleRegistry -> playbook dispatch end to end with a side-effect-free action kind, before any kind with a real external effect (notify, image-gen, forge writes) is attempted -- those remain blocked on the parent doc's unresolved execution-time gaps (idempotency, mid-run failure), which this slice deliberately does not need.

Generalizes the fixed-signature, resolved-by-name Yaegi pattern already shipped for custom gates (internal/gate/gateeval) and workflow stage plugins (skillbuild) -- do not invent a new interpreter-construction or panic-recovery mechanism; reuse yaegiutil.New/Resolve/Safe directly.
design:
Per module-position.md:
1. internal/domain/eda/module/log: hand-written schema source (Args/Result structs, SchemaVersion const), //go:generate yaegi extract -name logextract producing logextract.Symbols -- same shape as gateextract/wfextract.
2. internal/domain/eda/module: ModuleRegistry with Register(kind, dir) and Invoke(ctx, kind, rawArgs map[string]any) (map[string]any, error). No generic Module interface with an any payload -- Invoke decodes rawArgs into the kind's generated Args struct before calling the resolved function; a shape mismatch is a reported failure per the existing 'schema defines the accepted message' rule, not a silent zero-value fill. Discovery/resolve mirrors gateeval.Evaluate's structure (read file -> yaegiutil.New with that kind's symbols -> yaegiutil.Resolve[func(Args) Result] -> yaegiutil.Safe-wrapped call).
3. Config: ModuleDir field mirroring PluginDir's shape and doc comment exactly (operator-trusted directory of Yaegi module implementations, empty means none loaded).
4. Wire ModuleRegistry construction into daemon startup (bootstrap.go) alongside the existing PlaybookDirs/routing-file loading -- log-and-abort on load failure, matching the established pattern.
5. Do NOT implement notify, image-gen, or any action kind with a real external side effect in this slice. Do NOT wire this into playbook YAML action dispatch yet if that requires resolving the data-flow/condition syntax (parent doc open question 1) -- confirm during implementation whether a minimal 'run this one module action, no chaining' dispatch is small enough to include, or whether registry+one-kind-loadable is itself the right slice boundary and dispatch is a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: internal/domain/eda/module/log exists with a generated symbol table via go:generate yaegi extract (same tooling as wfextract/gateextract, verified by running go generate ./... and checking the output compiles). ModuleRegistry.Register discovers and loads a *.go file implementing the log kind's generated contract; Invoke calls it and returns a typed result decoded from the interpreted function's return value. A malformed or wrong-shaped args map is a reported error, not a panic or silent default. Config gains ModuleDir (empty by default, no behavior change). Trust boundary matches PluginDir/SecretEngineDir (operator-installed, in-process, daemon-privileged) -- not repository/task code. task check passes.
close_reason: Implemented and gate-verified as d29c732 (pushed to main). ModuleRegistry (Register/Invoke, strict arg decode, yaegiutil panic recovery) + internal/domain/eda/module/log schema with generated logextract symbols; ModuleDir config wired in bootstrap.go with log-and-abort; examples/modules/log.go operator example proven through the real registry. Playbook YAML action dispatch deliberately deferred (data-flow Q1 unresolved) and recorded in module-position.md. task check clean (113/113 UI, exit 0).

title: workflow: standalone playbook lint/LSP tool (gopls-shaped)
description:
Fourth slice of docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md. The design doc's collision handling has two layers: a linter for pre-merge, same-tree collisions, and the runtime detect-log-report path for cross-source collisions only visible at daemon startup (t2db.9/.10/.11). Only the runtime path exists so far.

Corrected 2026-09-03 (Sam): not a Taskfile target wrapping existing functions -- a small standalone CLI binary shaped like gopls: one tool, multiple invocation modes. A one-shot 'lint' mode ships in this ticket; the design doc's LSP requirement (author-time hover/completion/inline errors) is a later mode of the SAME binary, not a separate tool, so the two can never validate a playbook YAML differently -- one schema source, one binary, two entrypoints into it (matches gopls's own check-vs-serve split).

Depends on archie-core-t2db.11 (multiple playbook directories) landing first, since a linter checking one directory in isolation can't demonstrate the cross-directory case the doc cares about -- though it should also catch within-a-single-directory duplicates, which is the more common real case.
design: New cmd/<name> binary (e.g. cmd/archie-playbooks), per organisation.md's cmd/ rule: CLI flag parsing and entry-point routing only, no domain wiring in cmd/ itself. Actual validation logic stays in internal/domain/workflow (reuse LoadKindWorkflowsYAML/LoadLabelWorkflowsYAML/t2db.11's directory merge directly -- no second, parallel validation path). This ticket implements only the lint subcommand/mode; structure the binary's command dispatch so an 'lsp'/'serve' subcommand can be added later without restructuring (e.g. a small subcommand table from the start, even with one entry), matching gopls's shape rather than assuming a single-purpose CLI that gets bolted onto later.
acceptance_criteria: A new cmd/ binary exists with a lint subcommand/mode that runs against one or more playbook directories and exits non-zero with a clear message when two files bind the same label/kind; exits 0 cleanly on a valid set. Reuses existing loader/merge logic directly -- no duplicated validation rules. Binary's command structure has an explicit seam for adding an LSP/serve mode later (does not need to be built yet). Documented (README or Taskfile.yml comment) so it's discoverable. task check passes.
close_reason: Implemented and gate-verified as 2c7c79e (pushed to main). cmd/archie-playbooks lint mode reuses daemon loaders; file-granular positions documented as known limitation.

title: workflow: generalize routing/label files to multiple playbook directories
description:
Third slice of docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md, completing open question #2. Generalizes the single-file workflow_routing_file / workflow_labels_file config fields (t2db.9, t2db.10) into a LIST of configured playbook directories, loaded at daemon startup alongside the existing single-file fields for backward compatibility. This is what makes the design doc's collision-handling rule (drop + log + report to caller, no auto-arbitration) load-bearing: a single file has nothing to collide with, so the rule has never actually been exercised in production code yet.

Corrected 2026-09-03 (Sam): must be a list of directories, not one directory -- a single playbook_dir field would contradict supporting multiple independently-maintained playbook sources, which the PRD's own Dedup section already assumes ('independently-sourced playbook directories collide'). Scope directories by the existing Repo (owner/name) concept already in Config.Repos, NOT by org/tenant -- org-keying would require an auth/identity model archie does not have yet. That is a separate, later decision, not something to half-build here.
design: Follow the existing once-at-startup lifecycle (SetKindWorkflows/SetLabelWorkflows pattern) rather than inventing new state management. Config gains a list field (e.g. PlaybookDirs []string, or a PlaybookDir field on the existing Repo struct if directories should tie to a specific configured repo rather than being globally pooled -- decide based on whether playbooks are meant to be repo-scoped or operator-global). A loader reads every *.yaml file across all configured directories, applying the same per-file validation LoadLabelWorkflowsYAML already does, then merges bindings across all sources -- a binding for the same label/kind declared by two different sources is the collision case: drop both, log which sources/label collided, return the error to the caller (do not start the daemon on a routing collision). Single-file fields (workflow_routing_file, workflow_labels_file) remain supported unchanged as an additional, independent input alongside the directory list, not replaced by it.
acceptance_criteria: Config supports a LIST of playbook directories (not a single path), empty/unset by default (no behavior change for existing configs). Loading two directories with a colliding label binding is a reported load failure, not a silent pick-one. Loading multiple non-colliding directories merges cleanly and Route() honours the merged bindings. Existing workflow_routing_file/workflow_labels_file continue to work unchanged when no directories are configured. Org/tenant scoping is explicitly out of scope and not attempted. task check passes.
close_reason: Implemented and gate-verified as 3e7fe00 (pushed to main). PlaybookDirs is a list per ticket correction; cross-source collision rule exercised by new load path.

title: feat(workflow): route arbitrary forge labels to workflows via playbook YAML
description:
Second slice of docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md, complementing the kind->workflow layer (WorkflowRoutingFile): the label vocabulary itself becomes playbook data. A label outside the closed bug/feature/bootstrap kind set (e.g. security) dispatches to a registered workflow from an optional WorkflowLabelsFile, instead of falling through to triage.

- LabelWorkflows + LoadLabelWorkflowsYAML/SetLabelWorkflows in internal/domain/workflow/routing.go, mirroring the kind layer's once-at-startup lifecycle. The closed Kind/NATS-subject set is untouched; the map only extends binding authority for labels the kind layer does not own.
- Collision rule per design doc: a label owned by the kind set, an empty label, an empty workflow name, or a duplicate binding is a reported load failure (dropped, logged, error returned to the caller) -- the schema defines what is accepted; nothing is silently arbitrated by schema/version.
- Route() precedence: explicit t.Workflow -> arbitrary-label binding -> kind binding -> triage -> implement -> default.
- Config: WorkflowLabelsFile (workflow_labels_file), wired at boot alongside WorkflowRoutingFile; documented in config.example.toml.
- PRD: records this slice's decisions (single-file shape, collision rule, precedence) so later slices stay anchored.

Committed as 93a5f3a and pushed to main.
design: Follows the EDA playbook engine design doc (docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md). Open question 2 (config field shape) partially resolved: single file (workflow_labels_file) mirroring WorkflowRoutingFile and SkillsDir's single-path precedent; a directory remains open and larger. Data-flow/condition syntax (Q1), mid-run failure semantics and idempotency (design gaps 1-2) are explicitly out of this slice's scope per the PRD phasing -- they land with Module/Channel/Forge action kinds.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An issue labelled with an arbitrary label (not bug/feature/bootstrap) routes to the workflow bound in workflow_labels_file.
2. No workflow_labels_file configured: kind-only routing unchanged (backward compatible).
3. Colliding/empty/kind-owned labels in the file produce a reported load error, not silent arbitration.
4. Route() precedence: explicit t.Workflow > arbitrary-label binding > kind binding > triage > implement > default.
5. task check is green; tests cover dispatch, collision, empties, nil-restore, and precedence.
close_reason: Implemented and gate-verified as 93a5f3a (pushed to main).

title: workflow: make kind-to-workflow routing YAML-overridable
description: First slice of the EDA playbook engine (docs/prds/eda-playbook-engine.md): make workflow/routing.go's kindWorkflows map overridable from an optional YAML file, so which workflow runs for an intake Kind is data instead of a Go literal. labelKinds/NATS subjects are explicitly out of scope for this slice (closed subject-per-kind question deferred).
acceptance_criteria: Route() accepts an optional KindWorkflows override; a YAML file with the same shape as the built-in map overrides it; absent file/nil override falls back to today's hardcoded defaults unchanged; config gains an optional path field; task check passes.
close_reason: kindWorkflows YAML override shipped, task check green

title: Refactor hyperscript el() usage to Preact JSX
Update main entrypoint to mount via Preact render
Rename UI view files from .js to .jsx
Migrate Web UI to Preact
close_reason: All children completed

title: Dashboard UI for playbook bindings
description:
The t2db.4 backend shipped the CRUD API (POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/bindings + POST /api/bindings/{id}/approve) plus the state machine and HMAC wiring. Operators cannot author bindings from the dashboard yet: a list-and-approve page exists in api_binding.go's response shape but the matching ui/src/ feature folder does not. Build the click-through editor mirroring ui/src/mappings/ -- the actual convention there is .jsx, not .js (mapping-editor.jsx, mappings.jsx, mappings.css) -- follow that file extension, not payload-field-mapping.md:145-152's literal naming if it says .js. Components: source matcher, mapping picker, workflow picker, secret input, owner/repo pin input, state-machine controls (create -> edit -> approve -> armed). See docs/prds/webhook-intake-security.md and docs/prds/payload-field-mapping.md.

RESOLVED 2026-09-03 (commit ac42f64): the backend multi-repo correctness gap is fixed. binding.Binding now has optional Owner/Repo fields (Validate rejects setting only one); resolveBindingRepo (internal/daemon/daemon.go) dispatches to a pinned binding's own owner/repo unconditionally, falling back to the existing single-configured-repo behavior when unpinned. Wired through the API request/response shape already. Remaining scope for this ticket is UI-only: the dashboard editor itself, including an owner/repo input field for the pin added above.
acceptance_criteria: The click-through editor exists in ui/src/bindings/ (or the confirmed correct convention), covering create -> edit -> approve -> armed, including an owner/repo pin input. Backend correctness (multi-repo dispatch) is already resolved -- not part of this ticket's remaining acceptance.
close_reason: Backend Owner/Repo fix (ac42f64) + full dashboard UI (85761c4, mirroring ui/src/mappings/) both landed. Full state machine (draft->edit->pending_approval->approve->armed->delete) verified end-to-end in a real browser. Also fixed a related bug found in the process (empty-secret-on-edit rejected, commit 51ca509).

title: Encrypt binding secrets at rest
description: binding.Binding.Secret is currently stored as plaintext in the bindings.secret TEXT column. Anyone with read access to the SQLite file (the same access level as captured_events.body and tasks.body) sees HMAC secrets in plaintext. Add at-rest encryption for the secret column so a leaked database file does not leak sender-side shared secrets. See docs/prds/webhook-intake-security.md point 5. Decide the cipher (likely AES-GCM with a key derived from archied's secret registry or a deployment-level key file), the key-rotation story, and whether captured_events.body redaction is upgraded at the same time. Phase F work for t2db.
close_reason: Closed

title: Inline editing for per-repo config fields (allow_concurrent, max_retries, review_enabled)
description:
archie-core-b6ew.4 shipped visibility for AllowConcurrent, MaxRetries, and ReviewEnabled on the repositories card (read-only), which was the concrete discoverability gap Sam hit. Actual inline editing was scoped out of that issue because it hits a real backend limitation discovered while implementing it: the dashboard's PATCH /api/config path (installUpdateConfigHandler in internal/app/archied/bootstrap.go) applies dotted-key updates via overlay.Nest + configuration.ApplyOverlayValues, and overlay.Nest (internal/infrastructure/configuration/overlay/overlay.go:162) only builds nested maps by splitting on '.' -- it has no array-index handling, so a key like 'repos.0.allow_concurrent' cannot be expressed, and Repos is a []config.Repo slice, not a map, so ApplyOverlayValues's YAML-merge-onto-struct approach cannot target one element either.

This needs either: (a) a dedicated repo-update seam (e.g. a webui handler keyed by owner/name that reads-modifies-writes the Repos slice directly, bypassing the generic dotted-overlay path), or (b) extending overlay.Nest/ApplyOverlayValues to support array indices generically, which is broader-reaching (touches every list-shaped config field, not just Repos) and needs its own design decision about whether index-based overlay keys are stable across a file edit that reorders [[repos]] entries. Option (a) is almost certainly the smaller, safer change -- decide in a short design note before implementing, per this repo's settled-design-first rule, since option (b) has real footguns (index stability) that deserve a deliberate answer, not a guess.
close_reason:
Traced the mechanism before implementing: overlay.Nest/ApplyOverlayValues has no array-index support, but Repos is addressed as a WHOLE dotted key ('repos', no dot) whose value is the full slice -- so no changes to overlay/configuration packages were needed at all. Added PATCH /api/config/repos/{owner}/{name} (webui.Server.UpdateRepoField seam + handleConfigRepoUpdate), wired in archied/bootstrap.go's installUpdateRepoFieldHandler: reads the daemon's own live, untrimmed Repos (not webui.RepoView, which omits Preflight/TestGlob and would silently drop them on a naive round-trip), mutates the one matched repo's one field via the pure applyRepoFieldUpdate helper, and republishes through the existing UpdateConfig(ctx, {"repos": repos}) path unchanged -- zero duplicated validate/persist/publish logic.

Frontend: config-row.js's row() gained an opts.save override so a caller can redirect where an edit persists; the repositories table renders an autosaving checkbox (allow_concurrent, review_enabled) and a save-on-blur/Enter text input (max_retries) via api.configRepoUpdate, reverting/erroring inline on failure rather than reloading the whole page mid-edit.

Go tests cover the pure applyRepoFieldUpdate function directly (matched-repo-only mutation, untouched-field preservation including Preflight, type coercion, unknown repo/field rejection) and the webui handler (seam delegation, editable-field allowlist enforced before the seam is called, 503/400 mapping). JS tests cover the structural render (checkbox/input initial state) -- the save round trip itself isn't exercisable through the test shim (addEventListener is a no-op there), consistent with existing config-row.test.js coverage.

title: TelegramConfig gains a bws-capable Token (SecretRef), not just TokenEnv
description:
internal/config/config.go's TelegramConfig only has TokenEnv (a plain OS env var name); it never resolves through secret.Registry the way Forge.Token and Provider.APIKey do (secret.SecretRef{engine,key}), per ARCHITECTURE.md:220-224's own note that TelegramConfig.TokenEnv is one of the older env-only fields kept for backwards compatibility. internal/app/archied/telegram_setup.go:75 does a bare os.Getenv(cfg.Chat.Telegram.TokenEnv), bypassing the secret registry entirely.

This means a bws-stored Telegram token cannot be referenced directly in config.toml the way [providers.openai].api_key or [forge.token] already can -- the operator has to bridge it into a real process env var by hand (bws secret get ... | export ARCHIE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN=...) instead of writing [chat.telegram.token] = { engine = "bws", key = "..." }.

Fix: add a Token secret.SecretRef field to TelegramConfig, mirroring Forge.Token's shape and resolution path. Keep TokenEnv working as a fallback/legacy path (same pattern documented for Provider.APIKeyEnv vs APIKey) rather than a breaking config change -- resolve Token first if set, fall back to TokenEnv. Update config.example.toml and docs/architecture identity/config docs to show the SecretRef form as the preferred one.

title: Structured configuration editors: repositories, maps
description: Repositories currently render as a static read-only table missing AllowConcurrent, MaxRetries, and ReviewEnabled entirely (ReviewEnabled is absent from RepoView in api_config.go, not just unrendered). Add ReviewEnabled to RepoView, and build a dedicated backend-defined editor for the repositories section (and the models/providers maps) so these stop being silently read-only. This is the concrete fix for the allow_concurrent discoverability gap Sam hit, delivered as a typed editor rather than a one-off card patch, since the schema this epic introduces is what should own its shape.
close_reason:
Scoped to visibility, not full inline editing -- while implementing, found that the dashboard's PATCH /api/config path (overlay.Nest + configuration.ApplyOverlayValues) has no array-index support, so a per-element update to the Repos slice cannot be expressed as a dotted key today. That's real, separate scope, filed as archie-core-b6ew.6 rather than bolted on.

Shipped: RepoView.ReviewEnabled (previously absent from the API entirely, not just unrendered) alongside AllowConcurrent and MaxRetries; the repositories card now shows Concurrent/Max retries/Self-review columns as read-only pills, closing the concrete discoverability gap (Sam couldn't see allow_concurrent without an agent tracing Go source). config.example.toml documents review_enabled, which was undocumented before this. Go test pins ReviewEnabled reaching ConfigView for both a configured and a zero-value repo.

title: Schema contract tests: metadata completeness and secret-safety
description: Assert every field the schema exposes carries type, label, and section; assert restart_required and editable are set deliberately (not zero-value defaults hiding an unreviewed field); assert secrets still never appear (extend the existing TestHandleConfigNeverLeaksSecrets pattern to the schema response); assert the frontend's generic renderer can render the full schema fixture without any field-specific branch (a JS test walking the schema and asserting no field key appears literally in settings.js).
close_reason: Most of this issue's assertions were already covered incrementally by tests added in .1-.4 (key/label/type completeness, structured/locked non-editability, secret-leak guard on the schema block, schema values matching their flat-field source). This issue adds the two pieces still missing: TestConfigFieldDescriptorsRestartRequiredIsDeliberate pins the exact RestartRequired value per key against the reload.go evidence documented in configFieldDescriptors' own comment, so a reclassification without checking reload.go fails loudly. ui/test/settings-schema.test.js renders settingsPage against a schema fixture containing a field settings.js has never heard of (proving the renderer needs no field-specific branch to show it correctly) and asserts, by reading settings.js's own source text, that none of the generically-rendered section's field keys appear literally in it -- the direct regression test for archie-core-b6ew.3's whole point.

title: Generic frontend renderer for scalar configuration fields
description: Replace settings.js's hardcoded row(...) calls for scalar/bool/int/enum/duration fields with a renderer that walks the backend's sections/fields schema and builds the section cards, labels, and edit affordances from the descriptor alone -- the frontend must not know that containers.max_concurrency is an int or which card it belongs in. Structured fields (repositories, models, providers maps) are out of scope here and keep their existing bespoke rendering, tagged type=structured so the generic renderer skips them without special-casing each key.
close_reason: settings.js renders identity/budgets/storage/web cards generically from cfg.schema sections (schemaCards()), replacing identityCard/budgetsCard/storageCard/webCard/pullPolicyLabel -- label, type, description, editability, and options all come from the backend descriptor. config-row.js gained enum edit support (select from opts.options), an editable:false branch distinct from locked rows, and a hint tooltip carrying the field's description. Structured sections (repositories, models & providers) are unaffected -- still rendered by their existing bespoke functions, reserved for b6ew.4. Not visually verified in a live browser (needs a full daemon+forge+NATS stack); verified via unit tests mirroring the existing config-row.test.js patterns and Go contract tests.

title: Backend configuration schema contract: field descriptor types and section metadata
description: Define the descriptor types (Section, Field, Option) in internal/webui alongside ConfigView -- Key, Label, Description, Section, Type (string|int|bool|duration|enum|structured), Editable, LockedReason, Overridden, Options, RestartRequired. Hand-author one descriptor per existing ConfigView field, grouped into the sections the settings page already renders (identity, repositories, models, providers, budgets, storage, containers, web). No reflection over config.Config -- config.Config is scheduled for dissolution (internal/config/config.go package doc) and every field here is already a deliberate allowlist entry, so this is metadata on fields that already passed the secret-safety allowlist, not a new safety boundary.
close_reason: Added internal/webui/config_schema.go: ConfigFieldType/ConfigField/ConfigSection descriptor types and configFieldDescriptors(), hand-authoring key/label/type/editable/restart_required for every field ConfigView exposes today, grouped into the sections settings.js already renders. RestartRequired sourced from internal/app/archied/reload.go's reloadableFields/reloadableSubFields allowlist. Contract tests pin key completeness, structured-field non-editability, and locked-storage-field non-editability. Not yet wired into GET /api/config -- that's b6ew.2.

title: Expose the config schema via GET /api/config
description: Extend handleConfig's response with a schema-driven shape (sections of fields, each carrying its descriptor and current value) built from the field descriptors, replacing the flat ConfigView value tree the frontend currently re-interprets by hand. Keep the existing Locked/Overridden/Reload/Provenance top-level fields -- they describe runtime state, not the field catalog, and the schema-driven fields reference into them (locked_reason, overridden) rather than duplicating that logic.
close_reason: ConfigView gains a Schema []ConfigSection field, populated in handleConfig via buildConfigSchema(view), which attaches each request's Value/LockedReason/Overridden onto the static configFieldDescriptors() catalog. The flat ConfigView fields (Identity, Repositories, etc.) are untouched -- Schema is additive. Tests confirm schema values match the flat fields they derive from, locked reasons propagate, structured fields stay non-editable, and secrets never reach the schema block.

title: [EPIC] Backend-owned configuration schema for the webui Configuration page
description:
The Configuration page's field definitions (label, section, type, editability, restart-required, options) are hand-maintained in ui/src/settings/settings.js and config-row.js, disjoint from the backend's own ConfigView allowlist in internal/webui/api_config.go. Adding or changing a runtime-tunable setting today means editing Go and JS in two unrelated places by hand, and nothing catches drift between them. Repo.ReviewEnabled is missing from the API entirely; AllowConcurrent and MaxRetries reach the API but the repositories card never renders them, which is what blocked Sam from discovering the allow_concurrent fix without an agent tracing the Go source directly.

Design: docs/prds/config-schema.md. The backend keeps its existing hand-picked, secret-free allowlist (ConfigView in api_config.go) -- config.Config is scheduled for dissolution per its own package doc, so this is deliberately NOT a reflection-based schema over config.Config. Instead each already-allowlisted field gains a hand-authored descriptor (label, section, type, editable, restart_required, options) alongside its existing value, and the frontend renders scalar/bool/int/enum/duration fields generically from that descriptor instead of hardcoding rows. Structured fields (repositories, maps) get dedicated typed editors rather than staying silently read-only.
close_reason: All six child issues shipped: hand-authored field descriptor catalog (.1), schema attached to GET /api/config (.2), generic scalar renderer replacing hardcoded settings.js rows (.3), repository field visibility incl. the previously-API-absent ReviewEnabled (.4), schema contract tests pinning restart-required deliberateness and generic-render proof (.5), and inline editing for the three per-repo fields via a dedicated PATCH /api/config/repos/{owner}/{name} seam (.6). The concrete complaint that started this (allow_concurrent invisible on the dashboard) is fully resolved: visible, editable, and backed by a schema the frontend no longer hardcodes.

title: Curator action timestamps rendered as '105694 wks ago'
description: Curator actions built without an explicit At (e.g. sessioncurator before this fix, and skillcurator) serialized time.Time's zero value to the dashboard, which rendered as a nonsense relative time. Fixed by stamping sessioncurator's action with its clock and backfilling any zero Action.At in activityTracker.record from the pass timestamp.
close_reason: Fixed: sessioncurator now stamps Action.At from its clock; activityTracker.record backfills any zero Action.At from the pass timestamp as a defense in depth for engines with no clock (skillcurator).

title: [EPIC] Dynamic workflow routing: route task intent to the cheapest sufficient workflow
description:
workflow.Route() (internal/domain/workflow/workflow.go:237) only checks an explicit t.Workflow, then label match, then falls back unconditionally to 'implement' -- the heaviest workflow. There is no content/intent-based routing at all. task_spawn's own tool schema actively overpromises: 'workflow: ... Omit to let the daemon route it' (internal/gateway/task_tools.go:240), implying real routing exists when it means only 'check labels, then give up and run the heaviest workflow anyway'.

Confirmed via production task 6 (2026-09-02): a chat-spawned task whose entire content was 'this is just a test, close it when you receive it' ran the full implement pipeline (prepare, baseline, plan, build, commit-push) end to end, burning 669,421 tokens and ~7 minutes, when nothing about the request needed a worktree, a plan, or a build at all.

Needs a design doc before any code lands per CLAUDE.md's scope-discipline rule (no settled design exists).
close_reason: Implemented internal/domain/workflow/triage.go: a cheap classify-only-once AgentStage (still runs StagePrepareWorktree -- AgentStage requires tc.Dir to mount into the container, no cheaper primitive exists) that either closes a task needing no code change (reusing the CloseIssue/StatusMerged pattern feasibility.go's OnResult already established for the same ctx-less constraint) or sets tc.Task.Workflow and requeues under the chosen workflow (implement/tdd/feasibility, defaulting to implement for a missing/unrecognized choice). Route()'s fallback (workflow.go) now prefers reg["triage"] over reg["implement"] when registered, falling back unchanged when it isn't -- fully backward compatible. Registered in skillbuild.builtins(). 9 new tests (triage_test.go, routing_test.go) plus the design doc at docs/prds/dynamic-workflow-triage.md. task check clean.

title: Token usage totals mislead: raw prompt sum not netted against cache hits
description:
Confirmed on production task 6 (2026-09-02, carina): dashboard/PR summary showed '14 iterations · 405,004 tokens · 400,021 prompt · 4,983 completion · 360,018 cached'. Cross-checked against the per-iteration daemon log: nothing is double-counted or hardcoded -- the totals are the correct sum of 14 real, separately-billed API calls with growing context. But 360,018 of the 400,021 'prompt tokens' shown were cache hits (billed at a steep discount), not full price -- real fresh spend was ~40,003 tokens. Showing only the raw prompt-token sum makes every agent run's cost read roughly 10x worse than what was actually billed, everywhere this aggregate surfaces (PR body, dashboard timeline).

Separately (real, not just cosmetic cost): StageBaselineGate's retry-mission prompt re-injected the ENTIRE go test ./... output -- hundreds of lines covering every passing package -- into every retry iteration's prompt, not just the failing ones. Direct mechanical contributor to the growing per-iteration prompt sizes.
design: TaskContext.RunUsage (in-memory, not persisted -- Task.TokensUsed remains authoritative) accumulates agentexec.Usage across every agent run in one workflow execution. formatTokenUsage(total, usage) renders 'N tokens (F fresh + C cached)' with a plain fallback. extractFailingGateOutput(s) strips go test 'ok' package lines, only when it recognizes --- FAIL:/FAIL\t markers, else returns input unchanged. Known gap: a task resumed after a daemon restart mid-workflow loses RunUsage and falls back to the plain total -- an honest degrade, not a bug; persisting the breakdown would need a store migration for a purely presentational value, not worth it yet.
acceptance_criteria: PR bodies and the dashboard timeline show a fresh-vs-cached breakdown (or an equivalent net figure) instead of a raw prompt-token sum, falling back gracefully when no usage breakdown is available. Gate-retry mission prompts drop passing-package output, keeping only failure-relevant content, with graceful degradation for non-Go gates or unrecognized output shapes. task check passes.
close_reason: Added TaskContext.RunUsage + accumulateUsage (agent.go, implement.go's baseline-fix branch) and formatTokenUsage (workflow.go), wired into implement.go's and tdd.go's PR-body footers plus ui/src/tasks/timeline-event.js's agent_finish rendering (raw prompt replaced with computed fresh = prompt - cached). Added extractFailingGateOutput (workflow.go) trimming go test 'ok' package lines from StageBaselineGate's retry mission, degrading to unchanged output when no --- FAIL:/FAIL\t marker survives the filter. 5 new Go tests, 1 updated JS test. task check clean, 100/100 JS tests.

title: Dashboard Logs page never surfaces per-task attempt-log detail
description: internal/webui/api_tasks_logs.go's handleTaskLogs (GET /api/tasks/{id}/logs) was fully working -- internal/logging/reader.go's decode() already captures every JSON field generically into Entry.Fields (stage, tokens, iterations, model, stop_reason, everything). But no frontend code called it: ui/src/logs/logs.js (the dashboard's only Logs page) exclusively called api.logs(), the daemon-wide feed, which only carries the daemon's own component-scoped Info/Warn/Error lines -- never the rich per-stage/per-agent-run detail that lives in a task's own per-attempt log file. An operator could never see why a specific task took as long as it did, what each workflow stage did, or its token spend breakdown from the dashboard, even though the daemon already recorded and could already serve all of it. Discovered while investigating production task 6 (2026-09-02, archie-core-95dj).
acceptance_criteria: A task's persisted attempt log (stage timings, iteration counts, token/prompt/completion/cached breakdowns, model) is visible from the dashboard task view. Reuses the daemon-wide log page's row-rendering logic rather than duplicating it. Handles disabled/empty/error states without crashing. task check (including task test:ui) passes.
close_reason: Added ui/src/base/log-row.js (row rendering extracted out of logs.js, shared -- second consumer per CLAUDE.md), ui/src/tasks/task-logs.js (taskLogPanel handling loading/error/disabled/empty/populated states), api.taskLogs() in ui/src/base/api.js, and a collapsible 'Attempt log' section wired into each task's existing timeline drill-down in ui/src/tasks/tasks.js -- lazily fetched on first expand. New tests: ui/test/log-row.test.js, ui/test/task-logs.test.js. task check clean, 100/100 JS tests.

title: setupMemory never calls RegisterExternal; cfg.Memory.Provider is silently inert
description:
internal/app/archied/bootstrap.go:setupMemory's own doc comment says
"External providers from config are added via RegisterExternal when
cfg.Memory.Provider is set" -- no such branch exists in the function body.
Today, an operator who sets [memory] provider = "..." in config.toml gets
no error and no effect: the builtin file-backed provider is the only one
that ever runs. config.example.toml already documents this as a known gap
("[memory] exists to register an EXTERNAL provider alongside it, but as of
this writing that wiring ... is not called").

Separately, internal/config.MemoryConfig (config.go:287) has no `toml`
struct tag on any field (yaml/json only), so even fixing the wiring call
may not bind values from config.toml, the format operators actually use --
verify this before or as part of the fix.

This sits ahead of the typed engine-family work (archie-core-...-11-e245c170)
in the sense that it's a bug in the CURRENT ad-hoc MemoryProvider wiring,
not a gap in the future engine contract -- decide whether it's worth fixing
in the legacy path or superseded once the conforming memory engine family
lands, rather than fixing both.
close_reason:
Fixed, but not as originally framed. Investigated wiring RegisterExternal
for real: there is no external MemoryProvider implementation anywhere in
the repo to construct and pass to it (only internal/memory/builtin.Provider
exists) -- calling RegisterExternal would be dead plumbing to nothing, not
a fix.

The actual fix: configuration.validateMemory now rejects memory.provider
being set at all, with a clear reason, instead of accepting it and doing
nothing. Turns the silent no-op into a loud one. setupMemory's doc comment
and config.example.toml updated to match; the now-pointless
provider_config example section removed.

toml struct tags (the other half of this bug) were already fixed in
archie-core-1786637490043's commit.

Drop the rejection once a real external provider (or the domain/memory
engine family's Honcho proof, archie-core-1786637492031) gives the field
an effect again.

TestValidateMemoryRejectsProviderSetToAnything covers it. task check is
green.
