title: Architecture decision record: scheduling destination matrix entry in migration-decisions.md
description:
`migration-decisions.md` section 1 explicitly names scheduling among the largest unreviewed areas needing a destination matrix entry: 'every current package MUST receive one explicit disposition' includes the cron/scheduling capability.

The ticker engine `scheduling.Engine` is already in `internal/domain/scheduling` (decided by being built there). The remaining slices — store, runner/router, blueprints, lifecycle guard — need their target paths, dependencies, contracts, and deletion criteria recorded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Section 1 (or a new section row) lists each scheduling slice — store, runner/router, blueprints, lifecycle guard, config, composition, ticker — with its target path, dependencies to remove, contracts preserved, and migration prerequisites.
- Names the existing `JobSource` / `Runner` / `Sink` / `Clock` interfaces as the contracts that bound the destination choices (so future maintainers see why no runner / store ended up under the engine package).
- Marks the recording as approved-by-position (the maintainer approved this placement implicitly by accepting the engine PR) so it is not re-litigated.

title: Wire cron engine: app/archied composition, sink adapter, Start/Stop lifecycle
description:
Composition slice that connects the four siblings: instantiates the ticker engine in `internal/app/archied/` over the job store and the router, with the configured `EngineConfig` from the translator; registers it with the daemon's existing Start/Stop lifecycle (Start on boot, bounded-during Stop) and wires the events-bus sink so emitted `KindJobRun` / `KindJobError` events reach the bus subjects the rest of the system already listens on.

This is the last bead before the epic's acceptance scenario — daily-status-summary cron, persists across restarts, dangerous commands refused — is end-to-end runnable by a fresh operator.
acceptance_criteria:
- `engine.Start` called during daemon boot, with the configured interval.
- `engine.Stop(ctx)` called during daemon shutdown, bounded by the same grace deadline the rest of the daemon uses (matches `taskrun`/workflow engine shutdown pattern).
- `scheduling.Sink` adapts to the events bus emitter so dashboard / dashboard timeline surfaces running and failed jobs with the same `Kind`/`Detail`/`Data` shape the rest of the system uses.
- With all four sibling slices landed, the parent epic acceptance ('a daily-status-summary cron job can be created, persists across restarts, dangerous commands are refused') is exercisable end-to-end.

title: Cron configuration block: [scheduling] in config.example.toml with EngineConfig translation
description:
Operator input for the cron/scheduling slice: a `[scheduling]` block in `config.example.toml` (`interval`, `max_parallel`, `job_timeout`, `events_sink`) plus a translation layer in `internal/infrastructure/configuration` that produces the `scheduling.EngineConfig`.

Without this, the engine has no path from operator input to runtime. The translator is the bridge the wiring slice then hands to `internal/app/archied/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `config.example.toml` shows a `[scheduling]` block with all four fields and their default behaviour on zero values (mirrors `scheduling.Default*` constants).
- Configuration translator yields a fully-resolved `scheduling.EngineConfig` with documented defaults applied; negative values are validated and surface as a startup error, not a panic.
- Sink plumbing produces a concrete `scheduling.Sink` from the events-bus emitter; absent sink leaves `Events` nil, which the engine already documents as a valid (unobservable) configuration.

title: Cron lifecycle guard: reject dangerous commands at job creation
description:
Slice 4 of the cron/scheduling epic (archie-core-1786637496320-249-be6d9a20). The epic's third acceptance criterion verbatim: 'Dangerous commands are rejected at creation time.'

Guards both runners from the previous slice: ChatCourier (whose body could include shell-shaped payloads) and WorkflowTask (whose shell-step is a documented footgun). Rejection happens at job creation, not at tick time, so a refused job is visible in the store with a refusal reason and never reaches the ticker engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rejects job specs whose target body includes any of: `archied` restart, `systemctl`, `launchctl`, `pkill`, `mkfs`, `dd`, `shutdown`, `reboot`.
- Rejection reason is recorded on the refused job and surfaced through the gateway / dashboard; the job is not written to the store.
- One named rejection function both the CLI and gateway paths call, so adding a new dangerous token does not require touching every UI surface.
- False positives are deliberate — the list over-broadens then narrows by operator feedback. Cost of accepting a dangerous command vastly exceeds the cost of a refused one.

title: Cron blueprints: parameterised templates with typed slots and form schemas
description:
Slice 3 of the cron/scheduling epic (archie-core-1786637496320-249-be6d9a20). The authoring surface: predefined templates with typed slots (time, enum, text, weekdays — each with their validators) that gate the gateway and CLI creation forms.

Daily status summary is the headline blueprint. An author without a blueprint can still create a job directly, but the gateway form is the recommended surface for non-trivial jobs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A small registry of built-in blueprints (daily-status-summary at minimum; weekday-pickable and time-pickable are sufficient for headline coverage) exposed to gateway and CLI form renderers.
- Typed slot definitions (`time`, `enum`, `text`, `weekdays`) with a generated form schema suitable for the gateway chat-form surface.
- Template renderer fills slots from a validated values map; missing or wrong-typed slots reject the job at creation, not at next tick.
- Adding a new blueprint is data, not code, and the gateway / CLI form reflect added blueprints without a rebuild.

title: Cron delivery runner + router: dispatch due jobs to chat/task targets
description:
Slice 2 of the cron/scheduling epic (archie-core-1786637496320-249-be6d9a20). Implements `scheduling.Runner` and the router that picks one runner per job kind.

Without this slice, the ticker engine has no work to dispatch. Concrete target types to ship: ChatCourier (sends a templated message through the existing channel-agnostic `channels.Channel` gateway, so the channel choice stays the operator's, not the cron's) and WorkflowTask (submits a `workintake` envelope so the existing task lifecycle owns scheduling, retries, gates, and PR opening).

Job store is a hard prerequisite. Composition wiring and lifecycle guard block the wiring slice, not this one.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least two `Runner` implementations: `ChatCourier` (renders the job's templated body through the channel layer) and `WorkflowTask` (submits a `workintake` envelope carrying the cron identity and body so the existing workflow domain runs the rest).
- A `Router` that maps `Job.Kind` to a Runner; an unrecognised kind emits `KindJobError` `phase="dispatch"` and is otherwise a no-op — refused at the gate, not silently dropped.
- Every Runner honours `ctx.Done()` so the engine's bounded shutdown actually drains in flight.
- The epic's headline scenario ('daily status summary') is exercisable end-to-end through the ChatCourier runner with a hard-coded template; the blueprints slice replaces this with parameterisation.

title: Cron job store: per-profile JSON with cross-process file locking
description:
Slice 1 of the cron/scheduling epic (archie-core-1786637496320-249-be6d9a20). Implements the durable job store: one JSON file per profile at the conventional path, CRUD operations, and cross-process file locking so a CLI edit and a daemon writer don't corrupt each other.

The ticker engine (internal/domain/scheduling) consumes this through its `JobSource` interface. The store's only contract with the engine is `Due(ctx, now) -> ([]Job, error)` — the engine applies no schedule arithmetic of its own, so the store owns cron expressions, fixed intervals, and catch-up windows.
acceptance_criteria:
- One JSON file at the conventional per-profile path (`<config_dir>/cron/jobs.json` or equivalent). Schema is durable and version-stamped for forward compatibility.
- Create / read / update / delete by job ID with merge semantics that preserve fields not in the patch.
- Cross-process file lock (`flock` or OS equivalent) makes concurrent CLI+daemon writers serial; last-writer-wins is documented as the conflict policy.
- Implements `scheduling.JobSource` so the ticker engine can poll it without knowing the file layout or format.
- A truncated/partial-write file is not a panic: open returns an explicit error the engine surfaces as `phase="source" KindJobError` rather than crashing the loop.
close_reason: Slice 1 of cron/scheduling epic landed: per-profile JSON store with cross-process flock, merge-semantic Update, version-stamped schema, ErrCorruptFile on truncated files, ErrUnsupportedSchema on forward versions. Implements scheduling.JobSource so the ticker engine can poll it without knowing the file layout. Adversarial review applied: deep-copy Get/List, pool validation in Create/Update, ErrScheduleUnsupported on Once MarkRun, 0o600 file mode, SetEscapeHTML(false) for operator-readable files, fsync before rename for durability, ErrClosed sentinel after Close, real cross-process flock test via os/exec. task check green.

title: Operator-triggered PR review with selectable reviewer model
description: Expose the reviewer as a channel-neutral application capability that can review an existing pull request on operator request. The Web UI should offer a Review PR action as one adapter; chat/Telegram and future channels must invoke the same command rather than duplicating review behavior. The operator can configure or select the reviewer model independently from planner/builder models. Reuse the reviewer epic's fresh-context, read-only snapshot, structured findings, calibration, and visibility contracts.
acceptance_criteria: A channel-neutral review command accepts a repository and PR identity, launches the approved isolated reviewer path, and returns/persists structured findings; Web UI exposes Review PR; at least one non-Web-UI channel can invoke the same command; reviewer model is configurable independently with a safe default; authorization and duplicate/concurrent review behavior are deterministic; findings and review status are visible without requiring raw logs.

title: liveReply fallback lines appended after finalize are never rendered
description:
A media delivery that fails AFTER doFinalize has run appends its fallback line to l.toolLines and calls requestRender(), but stopRendering() has already closed renderDone and the renderer goroutine has exited. requestRender is a non-blocking send into a cap-1 channel with no consumer, so the line is dropped and the finalized Telegram message stands unchanged.

Media is fire-and-forget with a 30s budget while the turn's text finishes far earlier, so this is the NORMAL case for a large upload: a 40MB document that 400s or times out reports 'could not send x' into a slice nothing reads. Pre-dates the local-file work (URL fallbacks have the same hole) but archie-core-absb's guarantee that non-delivery is always visible depends on it.

Found by adversarial review of 9a45fbb. internal/channels/telegram/live.go:419-437 with :498-532.

## Acceptance Criteria
A media failure occurring after the live reply has finalized still reaches the user -- e.g. as its own follow-up message rather than an edit to a message nothing re-renders. Covered by a test that finalizes first and fails the send second.
close_reason: Fixed: stopRendering now marks the reply finalized, and appendFallbackLine sends a standalone follow-up message instead of writing into a dead render buffer. Covered by TestLiveReplyMediaFallbackAfterFinalizeSendsFollowUp.

title: Dashboard swallows failed operator actions, showing nothing in the UI
description:
When an operator action fails, the dashboard surfaces nothing. Pressing Stop on a running task issued POST /api/tasks/3/action, received 403, and the only evidence anywhere was a browser console line: "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 403". The page itself showed no error, no toast, no change of state -- the button simply appeared to do nothing.

This is how archie-core-440c (every dashboard mutation 403s behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy) went unnoticed: the operator pressed Stop, saw nothing happen, and reasonably concluded the task was unstoppable rather than that the request had been refused. The bug was only found by opening devtools.

Confirmed live 2026-08-25 while signed in to the production dashboard.

## Why this is its own bead

440c fixes the 403. This bead fixes the fact that ANY failed action is invisible -- a 500, a store failure, a refused state transition, an expired session -- and each of those has its own way of going wrong. Fixing only 440c leaves the next failure equally silent.

Note internal/webui/api_tasks.go already returns distinguishable, human-readable failures ("missing CSRF header", "cross-origin mutation refused", "runtime task control is unavailable"). The server side is doing its job; the client discards it.

## What is needed

- A failed action tells the operator it failed, in the UI, with the server's reason where one is given.
- The distinction that matters most: refused (403, bad state, not permitted) versus broken (5xx, network). The operator's next move differs -- the first is "you cannot do that", the second is "try again or check the daemon".
- A 401 or an expired forward-auth session should prompt re-authentication rather than reading as a generic failure, since the deployment sits behind Authelia.
- The optimistic UI must not show an action as applied when it was refused.

Per CLAUDE.md the frontend is one folder per feature under ui/src/<feature> with shared primitives in ui/src/base -- error surfacing used by more than one feature belongs in base, extracted on the SECOND real consumer, not in anticipation. Remember ui/dist is committed: run `task ui` and commit the rebuilt output in the same change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load the dashboard in a deployment where mutations fail (any 440c-affected proxied deployment reproduces it directly).
2. Press Stop, Retry, Abandon or Archive on a task.
3. Observe the request fails in devtools while the page reports nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

A failed operator action is reported in the dashboard with the server's reason where supplied; refused and broken failures are distinguishable to the operator; an authentication failure prompts re-auth rather than a generic error; no optimistic state change survives a failed request; dashboard tests cover a refused action, a server error and a network failure; ui/dist is rebuilt and committed.

title: No byte-for-byte conversation replay: transcripts cannot be exported or examined
description:
Asked to save a complete transcript -- "everything. My messages, yours, tools everything. Also save the agents logs" -- the agent could not. It produced a summary archive and honestly documented the limitation: no chat export exists, and the task-log responses were clipped at the tool's 50 KB cap.

Sam's requirement: "we should be able to receive and view and examine byte-for-byte replays of an entire transcript. exactly the commands run, the results received for those commands, the user messages, agent responses, EVERYTHING."

## What exists and what does not

internal/gateway has session tooling -- session_list, session_resume, session_title, session_delete -- so sessions are already first-class and persisted (the turn ledger backs /gateway's replay of completed-duplicate turns, and archie-core-ippu made tool activity part of that record). What is missing is retrieval: nothing exposes a session's full contents for export or examination.

Establish first exactly what is persisted per turn today, because the answer determines whether this is an export feature or a capture feature. If tool ARGUMENTS and full tool RESULTS are not currently retained -- only rendered summaries -- then byte-for-byte replay requires changing what is written, not just adding a reader. That distinction is the main open question and should be settled before design.

## Requirements

- Fidelity: user messages, agent responses, every tool call with its arguments, and every tool result, in order, with timestamps. Not a rendered summary, and not the truncated preview the chat UI shows.
- Retrieval: usable for a whole session, not capped at a tool-result size limit. Bulk delivery almost certainly belongs on the send_file path (archie-core-absb) rather than in a tool result -- write the file, deliver the file.
- Examination, not just download: an operator should be able to inspect a replay in the dashboard, which is where the event inspector already lives.
- Honesty: if anything is unavailable (rotated, compacted, never captured), the export must say so explicitly rather than presenting a partial record as complete. The agent got this right by hand; the mechanism should guarantee it.

## Constraints

- Transcripts contain secrets by nature -- tool arguments carry tokens, results carry file contents. internal/memory/scrubber and gateway/stream.go's sensitiveParameterKey are existing prior art for redaction and should be reused rather than reimplemented. Decide explicitly whether an export is redacted, raw, or offers both, and who may request one.
- Retention: a full-fidelity record is large. Decide what is kept and for how long, consistent with the 7-day payload retention already decided for captured events.

## Acceptance Criteria

An operator can export a complete session transcript containing user messages, agent responses, tool calls with arguments and tool results with content, in order and timestamped; the export is delivered as a file rather than clipped into a tool result; a replay can be examined in the dashboard; anything missing from the record is stated explicitly in the export; redaction policy is decided, documented and applied; tests cover a session larger than any tool-result cap and assert no gaps or reordering.

title: /status and /tasks have the wrong division of labour
description:
Sam's words: "/status is fucking annoying. I'm invoking an actual status update, receiving minor information as well as shit I can get elsewhere. What's worse is that the /tasks command is meant to be for viewing the running agents, not /status."

Observed 2026-08-24, the entire output of /status was:

  Tasks  Parked: 2
  Runtime  Provider: OpenAI  Model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna

Two problems in one screen. It answers the question /tasks should own (what work is in flight), and it answers it thinly -- a count, with no task identity, no stage, no age, nothing actionable. Everything else it shows is static configuration available elsewhere. Later in the same session /status reported "Running: 1" for a task that was stuck in a failure loop and going nowhere, which is the specific case where a bare count actively misleads.

## The division of labour to restore

- `/tasks` owns WORK: what is running, what is parked and why, what needs the operator. This is the live view of the agents, and it is where task identity, workflow, stage, attempt and age belong.
- `/status` owns HEALTH: is the daemon well. Broker connectivity, provider reachability, channel state, container pool, queue depth, last poll, version. The things an operator checks when something feels wrong and which are NOT visible elsewhere in chat.

Neither should be a thin duplicate of the other, and neither should pad itself with static config the operator already knows.

## Related, decide together

archie-core-624 (task_action chat tool) adds operator verbs for tasks. /tasks is the natural surface for discovering the ids those verbs act on, so the two should be designed as one flow: see the work, then act on it. Check what internal/gateway/task_tools.go already returns before adding a new query path -- ChatTaskSummary may already carry most of what /tasks should show.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run /status in chat with tasks parked and one running.
2. Observe a parked/running COUNT plus provider and model, with no way to identify or act on any task.
3. Run /tasks and observe the overlap.

## Acceptance Criteria

/tasks shows the live work with enough identity and state to act on it (id, title, status, workflow/stage, age) and is the documented way to view running agents; /status reports daemon health that is not obtainable elsewhere in chat and does not duplicate the task list; a task that is running but not progressing is distinguishable from one making progress; the command descriptions registered with the platform match what each actually does.

title: Chat agent does not know its own repository or workspace, wasting turns rediscovering them
description:
Asked to raise a GitHub issue, the agent spent roughly eight tool calls working out where it lives: `pwd`, a `find` over /home/sam/projects returning 139 lines, `git remote -v`, a grep over RELEASING.md returning 92 lines, and a failed `read` of a README that does not exist. It eventually located the repository and filed the issue correctly, but every one of those calls was rediscovering a fact the daemon already knows.

Sam's words: "Yep, thats frustrating AF!"

## Why this is worth fixing structurally

It is not only slow and expensive. It is a correctness risk: an agent that has to guess which checkout it is looking at can act on the wrong one, and on this host more than one archie-core checkout exists. It also degrades every task that begins with orientation rather than work.

## What to do

internal/gateway/BuildSystemPrompt renders templates/archie.md.tpl, which already carries an `<env>` block. Per CLAUDE.md that template is the single place instruction precedence, core rules and the `<tools>`/`<env>` blocks live -- personas are the STYLE layer only, so this belongs in the template, never in a persona string.

Put the facts the daemon already holds into `<env>`: the configured workspace path, the repositories under management with their forge and default branch, and the identity in use. Configuration is the source of truth ([repos] entries, chat.workspace); do not have the prompt claim anything the daemon cannot confirm, and do not hardcode paths.

Note the same rule that governs `<tools>` applies here: the block must be built from what the daemon actually has, because a prompt that names a repository the agent cannot reach is worse than silence -- the model will confidently act on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

The chat agent knows its workspace path, managed repositories and identity without probing the filesystem; the block is rendered from live configuration rather than hardcoded; an empty or unconfigured value renders as explicitly unknown rather than as a plausible-looking default; a task that previously required filesystem archaeology to orient completes without it; tests assert the block reflects configuration and omits nothing the daemon knows.

title: [EPIC] Intercom: let the chat agent talk to running agents, the curator, and peers
description:
Today the chat agent can only observe autonomous work -- list tasks, read logs -- and act on it as an outsider through coarse verbs (spawn, stop). It cannot TALK to a running agent. An operator who can see a task going wrong has no way to say "stop guessing, the config lives at X" without killing the task and starting over, losing everything the agent had already worked out. Archie should behave like a living system whose parts can address each other, not a set of isolated processes with a dashboard bolted on.

## Prior art: pi-intercom

Pi ships `pi-intercom`, which solves this shape for Pi sessions on one machine and is worth reading before designing (/home/sam/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-intercom; skills/pi-intercom/SKILL.md is the usage guide). Its model:

- Sessions take names (`/name planner`, `/name worker-backend`) and address each other by name.
- `send` -- fire-and-forget notification. Task assignment, status, notice.
- `ask` -- BLOCKS until the target replies, with a timeout. The blocking form is the interesting one: it lets a worker stop and get a decision instead of guessing.
- `reply` -- answers an inbound ask, threaded automatically.
- `pending` -- lists unresolved inbound asks, i.e. who is waiting on you.
- `list` -- connected sessions and their state (idle / thinking / tool), for discovering targets.
- Its use cases map directly onto archie: planner-to-worker delegation, context and findings handoff, blocking clarification, subagent escalation (`need_decision`, `interview_request`), cross-project coordination.

## What is genuinely different here

Do NOT copy pi-intercom's transport. It ships its own local IPC broker (broker/broker.ts, a socket server with framing, spawn and runtime-claim logic) because Pi has no message bus. **Archie already has one**: NATS, with per-task subjects already defined in internal/agentexec/subjects.go (archie.agent.<id>.system and .events) and a request/reply pattern already used by taskrun, forgerpc, storerpc and worktreerpc. Building a second broker alongside it would be the "two parallel abstractions" mistake this repo already made once with gateway.BasePlatformAdapter.

So the real design questions are:
1. Does agent-directed messaging ride the existing per-task subjects, or does it need its own contract and subject family? Note CLAUDE.md's recorded NATS traps -- work-queue retention forbids overlapping consumers, and reply inboxes are core-NATS-only and are not stream subjects.
2. What is addressable? Running tasks have ids. The curator, channels and the daemon itself do not have a uniform identity for this purpose. An address space has to be decided before verbs are.
3. How does a BLOCKING ask work against an agent that is mid-model-call? A worker is not sitting in a receive loop; it is inside an agentloop turn. Delivering a message it will actually notice, without corrupting the turn, is the hard part -- and is where this stops being a transport problem.
4. Authorization: an operator messaging their own task is fine. Cross-identity messaging is not, and multi-identity deployments are supported (deployments/multi-forge-github-gitea.toml). Whatever the gateway's task tools enforce for identity scoping, this must enforce too.
5. Does an inbound operator message become part of the agent's context permanently, or a one-shot injection? This decides whether it can be used to steer a task or only to interrupt it.

## Relationship to existing work

- Overlaps archie-core-absb (agent cannot send local files) only in spirit: both are about the agent being able to communicate outward.
- The curator (internal/domain/curator) is a natural second participant after running tasks.
- Any design here should be checked against docs/architecture/organisation.md: the domain declares the contract it needs; the transport implements it.

## Success Criteria

An operator can address a running agent from chat and have it receive the message without the task being killed and restarted; a blocking ask returns the agent's answer or times out cleanly; participants are discoverable with their current state; messaging is identity-scoped so one identity cannot address another's work; the mechanism reuses the existing NATS transport rather than introducing a second broker; a design decision is recorded in docs/prds/ before implementation, per CLAUDE.md's scope discipline.
notes: Provenance correction 2026-08-25: this bead's description says 'Pi ships pi-intercom'. That is WRONG and Sam corrected it -- pi-intercom is a THIRD-PARTY PLUGIN written by a different developer solving their own problem, not a Pi feature and not endorsed by Pi. Weigh it accordingly: it is one developer's solution worth reading for its verb vocabulary (send/ask/reply/pending/list) and for the blocking-ask idea, not a reference implementation carrying Pi's design authority. The architectural judgement in this bead stands unchanged: do NOT adopt its broker, because archie already has NATS.

title: Agent cannot send local files: Telegram delivery is URL-fetch only
description:
The agent can produce a file on the host -- a log dump, a screenshot, a written archive, a diff -- and has no way to deliver it to the operator. Asked to send a saved transcript, it replied with a "Download the archive" link twice; nothing arrived either time, and it had no signal that anything had failed.

## Why video works and files do not

`telegramMediaSender.dispatch` (internal/channels/telegram/media.go:97) builds every attachment as:

    file := &models.InputFileString{Data: att.URL}

`InputFileString` tells Telegram to FETCH the given URL itself. That works for the existing media path because those attachments are remote-hosted -- MiniMax returns a public URL for a generated video, which is what `MultimodalResult.URLs` was added for. It cannot work for anything produced locally: a daemon-host path like /home/sam/archive.md is not a URL Telegram can fetch, so the send silently does nothing useful.

The `case "document"` branch (media.go:124-127) already calls `bot.SendDocument`, so the routing exists. Only the file SOURCE is wrong.

## What is needed

A way for the agent to send a LOCAL file as an attachment -- documents, logs, screenshots, images, any media -- not a link. The go-telegram/bot SDK supports upload via a reader (`models.InputFileUpload` with an io.Reader) as an alternative to `InputFileString`; the sender needs to choose between fetch-by-URL and upload-by-reader based on whether the attachment is remote or local.

Explicitly NOT the fix: exposing an external/public URL for local files. That trades a missing feature for a hosting and access-control problem.

## Constraints to respect

- Telegram enforces upload size limits (50 MB for documents via the Bot API at time of writing); exceeding them must produce a clear error to the operator, not a silent drop.
- The file tools are workspace-confined unless `[chat] unrestricted_filesystem = true`. Sending must not become a way around whatever confinement is configured -- resolve and check the path under the same policy the read tool applies.
- A failed send must surface as a failure the agent can see and report. The current defect is not that the agent lied; it is that success and silent non-delivery are indistinguishable to it.

## Acceptance Criteria

The agent can send a local file through Telegram and the operator receives it as an attachment; local and remote attachments both work, choosing upload-by-reader or fetch-by-URL as appropriate; a send that fails (too large, unreadable, outside the configured confinement) returns an error the agent surfaces rather than reporting success; existing remote-URL media delivery is unchanged and still covered by tests.
close_reason: send_file tool plus upload-by-reader delivery; commit 9a45fbb

title: Allow parked agent jobs to be closed or archived
description:
## Problem
Parked agent jobs remain visible indefinitely, but the task-management interface currently exposes no action to close or archive them. This leaves stale jobs in the active job history and requires manual cleanup outside the normal workflow.

## Observed behavior
The following old jobs are parked and cannot be closed through the available task-management actions:

- Job #1 — `daemon: label dispatch trigger with empty label matches every open issue`
- Job #2 — `archied: [[repos]] entries can't span more than one forge`

The interface can list and inspect parked jobs, but provides no close/archive operation.

## Expected behavior
Provide an explicit operation for a parked job, such as:

- `close` when the job is definitively finished or no longer actionable;
- `archive` when it should be removed from the active job list while retaining history;
- optionally `reopen` if a parked job needs to be resumed.

The operation should persist the state, be reflected in task listings, and retain the job logs and audit history.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user can close or archive a parked job from the supported task-management interface/API.
- The operation is idempotent and reports a clear error for invalid state transitions.
- Closed/archived jobs no longer appear among active or parked jobs by default, while remaining queryable.
- Existing logs, attempts, and failure details remain accessible.
- Tests cover closing, archiving, reopening (if supported), and repeated operations.
close_reason: Already implemented and in use: parked tasks expose Retry/Abandon/Reject — Abandon/Reject transition to terminal Won't-do and close the forge issue; terminal tasks then expose Archive (removes the row, keeps the durable audit event); Retry reopens parked work. Landed in de60802 (archive+retry controls) and 52bb018 (reject from every non-terminal state incl. parked); covered by TestLifecycleSpecificTaskActions, TestTaskListExposesLifecycleActions, TestArchiveRemovesOnlyOneTerminalTask.

title: Rollback the managed agent image when a runtime update fails health checks
description: The runtime update path rebuilds the Docker image, but scripts/archie-update-watchdog only restores the unused host archie-agent binary. A failed health check can report a rollback while the task-container image remains on the failed runtime. Design and implement image-reference preservation/restoration for the configured managed worker image, with tests for runtime-only and combined updates.
acceptance_criteria: A failed runtime-only update restores the prior worker image before restarting archied; a combined update restores both daemon and worker image atomically; update tests prove the configured managed image, not a host worker binary, is the rollback target.
close_reason: Completed; reconciled with the already-closed GitHub issue.

title: Make native archied embedded NATS and managed containers the default deployment
description: Supported examples and install.sh currently generate agent.mode=inprocess and treat external Compose NATS as the container path. Migrate the default operator experience to native archied plus embedded NATS plus managed task containers, while keeping external NATS as the advanced broker option.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh install produces the supported NATS-only container topology; systemd runs native archied; interactive host chat authority is unchanged; no Compose NATS service is required for embedded mode; external NATS profile remains documented and load-tested.
close_reason: Implemented in c978f10 (feat(deployment): default to managed NATS workers). Verified: no agent.mode/inprocess remains in install.sh, deployments/*.toml or config.example.toml; deployment_contract_test.go added to enforce it.

title: Recover workflow agents that omit the required finish tool
description: An analyse-stage agent can end normally without invoking the finish tool, producing agent idle and parking otherwise recoverable work. Add a bounded, deterministic recovery path that preserves explicit workflow completion and does not accept an unverified model final response.
notes: Follow-up: the recovery wiring is correct inside archie-agent, but a separate architecture bug remains: embedded NATS still falls back to daemon-local execution. Tracked by the new NATS-only execution issue.
close_reason: SDK v0.1.22 provides one bounded forced-finish recovery; Archie opts in through InProcessRunner. Focused test, task check, module verification, and independent adversarial review passed. Re-verified 2026-08-24: the opt-in moved from the deleted InProcessRunner to agentexec.NewLoopRunner (loop_runner.go:106 CompletionForceFinish), which is what the archie-agent worker constructs; ai-sdk still v0.1.22. [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-24, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: fix(update): install only approved changed components
description:
## Bug Description
A gateway-only `/update` (archied/v1.13.0 while runtime remains archie/v1.9.9) fetches and builds both binaries, backs up and installs both, and rebuilds the agent image. The image build does not receive `RUNTIME_VERSION`, so the released runtime is stamped `dev`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `/update` with only the `daemon` component available.
2. Approve the displayed snapshot.
3. Observe `archie-update-install` build/install both components and run `docker compose build agent`.

## Expected Behavior
The approved snapshot flows into `CommandInstaller`; only changed components are fetched/built/backed up/installed. Rebuild the agent image only for a runtime update and stamp it with the released runtime version. Preserve phase-1 result and phase-2 rollback/report metadata for gateway-only, runtime-only, both, and no-op plans.

## Actual Behavior
The installer receives only chat/report metadata, so the script independently rebuilds everything after `git pull` and Docker uses its default `RUNTIME_VERSION=dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Regression harness proves a gateway-only update never builds/installs the runtime or image.
- Tests cover gateway-only, runtime-only, both, and no-op.
- Released runtime images are stamped with the release version, never `dev`.
- Rollback/report metadata remains component-aware and correct.
- `task check` passes.

title: fix: make tool progress readable and preserve project context
description:
## Problem

Telegram tool progress is currently displayed as a stream of raw inline entries, for example:

- tool names followed by JSON schema placeholders such as `[string]`
- raw JSON arguments and oversized output
- repeated output without readable grouping
- full error dumps and turn-budget failures

Agents also search broad locations such as `/home/sam` instead of staying focused on the active project/worktree, read directories as files, and emit malformed shell commands. Useful project context is not being retained cleanly across the turn.

## Scope

- Render tool progress as compact, readable streaming fenced code blocks (Telegram-safe).
- Remove schema placeholders and redundant raw invocation JSON from user-visible output.
- Truncate or offload oversized results without consuming the entire turn context.
- Preserve concise success/failure status and actionable errors.
- Default agent discovery and file operations to the actual project/worktree context where task context provides one.
- Improve context retention across tool calls.
- Add validation or guardrails for malformed shell commands where practical.

## Acceptance criteria

- A normal tool call is shown as a readable streaming status block, not raw JSON.
- Tool failures remain visible but are concise and actionable.
- Large results are bounded/offloaded and do not exhaust the turn budget.
- Project-scoped tasks do not begin by searching unrelated home-directory data.
- Regression tests cover rendering, failure output, truncation/offload, and project-root selection.
- Telegram output is verified against a live deployed instance.

title: Add InstallType/Reference fields to releaseupdate.Component, populate from daemon/agent/deployment profile
description: Part 2/3 of point 4 in archie-core-1786751948782-3-837a8fd0's design. releaseupdate.Component (internal/releaseupdate/service.go:35-41) has ID/Label/Installed/Available/Changelog but no InstallType or Reference fields. Add both, and populate: archied reads its own compiled-in installtype.Type(); archie-agent reports its own over the NATS status round-trip (depends on the sibling issue that adds that round-trip); third-party dependencies Archie doesn't build (e.g. NATS) can't self-report, so their InstallType/Reference should come from the deployment profile (deployments/*.toml) rather than detection -- add the relevant fields there. Reference is something like 'container' + 'ghcr.io/samcharles93/archie-agent:1.9.0@sha256:...', not just a bare install-type string.
close_reason: Fixed: Component gained InstallType/Reference, populated via Service.Enrich from installtype.Type() (daemon), observed AgentStatus (agent), and [nats] config (third-party). Adversarial review clean (one lint-consistency nit fixed: use config.NATSMode* constants instead of raw strings). [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-23, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: Surface per-component update status on Configuration page and /version
description: Part 3/3, point 5 of archie-core-1786751948782-3-837a8fd0's design. Depends on the InstallType/Reference issue landing first -- there's nothing to surface otherwise. Add a /version endpoint and a per-component block on the Configuration page (internal/webui/api_config.go, ui/src/settings/), structured as {install_type, running_version, reference, latest_available, status} per component, where status is an enum (ok / update_available / drift / unknown) rather than a bare color. The actual comparison basis (e.g. running digest vs latest digest) should be visible on hover/expand, modeled on docker version's Client/Server nested-block convention per the original design doc.
close_reason: Fixed: GET /api/version + Configuration-page 'Update status' card, sourced from the InstallType/Reference/RunningVersions plumbing landed in .1/.2. Adversarial review found one real bug (Installed=='' with Available set incorrectly returned update_available instead of unknown) and one test gap (present-but-empty running-version map entry) -- both fixed, tests added, all green. [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-23, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: Stamp archie-agent's install type and add NATS status round-trip
description: Part 1/3 of point 4 in archie-core-1786751948782-3-837a8fd0's design. archied's own build is stamped with internal/installtype via -ldflags (Taskfile.yml:65, Dockerfile.archied:48-49), but archie-agent's build has no equivalent stamp -- Dockerfile:14 and Taskfile.yml:170 (agent build target) pass no -X installtype flag. Without it, an agent worker has nothing to self-report even once the daemon asks. Also add the NATS-side status/version request the daemon can send a running agentworker to get its install type + running version back (agentworker already has a NATS channel for logs; extend it for a status response rather than inventing a new transport). This is the prerequisite for archie-core-1786751948782-3-837a8fd0 point 4's 'archie-agent reports its own the same way' clause.
close_reason: Fixed: archie-agent's build is now stamped (installtype + agentworker.Version), and it reports both back to the daemon in every taskrun.Response. daemon.AgentStatus records the latest observation; daemonRunningVersions includes the agent component once one lands. Adversarial review clean (one nice-to-have comment added). [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-23, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: Workflows page 'Start work' form inputs unstyled (white boxes in dark theme)
description: The Start work card on the Workflows dashboard page (ui/src/workflows/workflows.js renderStartWork) creates raw <input>/<select>/<textarea> elements with no CSS class, so they fall back to browser default styling -- white background, black text -- against the rest of the dark-themed app. Every other form control in the app (e.g. Configuration's .kv-input in ui/src/settings/config-row.js) uses a themed class. Fix: style these form controls to match the app theme, either by reusing an existing input class or adding scoped rules in ui/src/workflows/workflows.css.
close_reason: Fixed: themed .wf-form input/select/textarea in workflows.css to match the dark theme. [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-23, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: Docs: promote the shipped review stage into docs/architecture and reconcile CLAUDE.md
description:
Under the scope-discipline rule merged as PR #533, a design is promoted into docs/architecture/ only once it is built and true. This is that promotion, and it is deliberately a separate bead so it is not lost when the feature lands and attention moves on.

Do three things once the stage ships:

1. Promote the docs/prds/ decision into docs/architecture/, describing the review stage as it actually works -- not as designed. Cut anything a reader could learn from the code.
2. Update ARCHITECTURE.md's task lifecycle: queued -> running(workflow:stage) -> pr_open -> merged|rejected gains a review stage that can divert to waiting_human before pr_open. The current text does not mention it.
3. Reconcile CLAUDE.md's Development Protocol. It currently tells a human or agent contributor to run the adversarial pass by hand. Once archied does this for the PRs it opens, that section needs to say which path applies to whom, or it will read as describing a manual step that is now automatic.

CLAUDE.md's own rule: a comment or doc that contradicts its code is worse than none, because the next reader trusts it.
close_reason: Duplicate; work tracked under canonical epic

title: Surface findings on the PR body and the dashboard
description:
The output has to land where the operator already looks, or the review is invisible work.

On the PR archie opens: a findings section stating what was checked, what was found, what was fixed, and what survived. A PR with zero findings should say the review ran and found nothing -- silence is indistinguishable from the review not running, which is the same unverified-claim problem the update-verification work (PR #530) was about.

On the dashboard and /api/tasks: a parked-for-findings task must show why, the same way a park reason is already surfaced today. An operator seeing waiting_human needs the findings without digging through logs.
close_reason: Duplicate; work tracked under canonical epic

title: Calibration: confirm findings adversarially before surfacing them
description:
The risk that kills this feature is a reviewer that cries wolf. A findings list padded with speculation trains the operator to skim past it, and then the feature is worse than nothing because it consumes attention while lowering trust.

Before a finding is surfaced, it must be independently checked and marked CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, with only CONFIRMED able to block. The reviewer must also be able to return zero findings, and to state which properties it checked and cleared -- a review that reports nothing is a valid and welcome result, and saying so explicitly is what distinguishes 'I checked and it is fine' from 'I did not look'.

title: Wire generate_video (MiniMax) tool end-to-end
description:
Implemented the MiniMax text-to-video generation tool and wired it through the media-delivery pipeline built for this: tool -> tools.MultimodalResult -> drainChatStream detection -> gateway.TurnStream.Media -> gateway.MediaSender (Telegram delivers inline; webui falls back to a link).

## What shipped
- internal/tools/minimax: API client (create+poll against MiniMax's v2/video_generation and v2/query/video_generation/{id}), a builtin tools.ToolEntry (generate_video), fully test-first with an injected-clock poll loop (no real sleep in tests).
- internal/tools: extended tools.MultimodalResult with a URLs []MediaRef field, for tool results whose media lives at a remote hosted URL rather than local bytes (the existing Files field).
- cmd/archied/telegram_setup.go: drainChatStream now detects a MultimodalResult in a tool result's Output and calls turn.Media(...) per URL, alongside the existing turn.ToolCall(...) reporting.
- internal/config: MinimaxConfig (off by default, unlike web_fetch -- this spends real API credits per call), api_key via the existing secret.SecretRef pattern.
- cmd/archied/bootstrap.go: registerMinimaxTool -- only registers the tool once an API key actually resolves, matching the 'do not advertise a broken capability' pattern web_fetch already uses.
- config.example.toml: documented [tools.minimax].

## Scope deliberately left out (by explicit instruction: URL-only, get it working first)
- Image-to-video (image_url content items) -- text-to-video only.
- Local byte/file upload delivery path -- URL-only, matches gateway.MediaSender's current URL-only design.
- Email/webhook channel delivery -- only Telegram implements gateway.MediaSender today; other channels have no inline media path, and webui falls back to a text link (see archie-core-1786748942243-6-f109697e for the still-open 'deliver generated images through channel and web abstractions' work).
- No OpenAI video provider -- only MiniMax implemented, per this issue's scope. A second provider should follow the same tool-package shape (internal/tools/<provider>) if wanted.
- No spend guard / approval gate on the tool despite it costing real credits per call (classified ClassMutating, not RequiresApproval) -- flagged in tool.go's doc comment as a candidate follow-up if usage shows it's needed.

title: Remove dead BasePlatformAdapter interface from internal/gateway
description:
`gateway.BasePlatformAdapter` (internal/gateway/adapter.go, Connect/Disconnect/Send/ChatInfo) is implemented by nothing outside its own test stub. It landed in commit bc1caf6 alongside the Session types and was never wired.

Every live channel instead implements `channels.Channel` (= `gateway.Gateway`: Name/Start/Stop, plus ConfigSchema/ValidateConfig) -- asserted at internal/channels/telegram/telegram.go:1229, internal/channels/email/email.go:389, internal/channels/webhook/webhook.go:224. So the repo carries two parallel channel abstractions and the newer one is inert.

It also has an internal contradiction that is likely why it was never implemented: the doc comment says the daemon instantiates 'one adapter per active bot identity x platform' (adapter.go:59) but `ChatInfo(ctx) (ChatInfo, error)` is documented as 'static metadata about the conversation a platform adapter is connected to' (adapter.go:36-38) with no chat argument. Telegram's Gateway is a single instance serving many chats, so ChatInfo(ctx) has no single answer. Send(ctx, MessageEvent) is fine for both models since MessageEvent carries ChannelID; ChatInfo is the part that only makes sense per-conversation.

Outbound delivery is assigned to the not-yet-built `internal/domain/messaging` by docs/architecture/migration-decisions.md section 2, so this interface should not be revived in place -- it should be deleted and its intent re-expressed there.

## Scope

- Delete BasePlatformAdapter and its test stub from internal/gateway/adapter.go / adapter_test.go.
- Keep SendResult and ChatInfo structs if domain/messaging or the media work still wants them; they are separable from the interface.
- Decouple gateway.CapabilitiesOf from BasePlatformAdapter (it currently takes one) so the capability mechanism survives the removal.

## Acceptance criteria

- BasePlatformAdapter no longer exists; `task check` passes.
- No behaviour change: nothing implemented it, so nothing should need rewiring.
- Any type retained from adapter.go has at least one live consumer, or is removed too.
notes: Discovery confirmed CapabilitiesOf is absent from the current checkout and gateway history. SendResult and ChatInfo have no live consumers, so all three legacy declarations are removed. Red test: TestLegacyPlatformAdapterTypesAreRemoved failed on BasePlatformAdapter, ChatInfo, and SendResult before deletion; gateway package suite passes after deletion. Full task check currently reaches one unrelated pre-existing failure: internal/app/agentworker TestApplicationOwnsNoTransportWireMechanics reports persistent_runner.go imports JSON wire encoding.

Gateway and worktree tests pass. task check passes all packages except the pre-existing tracked agentworker architecture failure archie-core-hqst. title: Align branch naming behavior, API, tests, and documentation
description:
branchPrefix ignores title and body despite the documented title-prefix contract, and branchSlug documents 40 characters while implementing 60.

Re-verified against main (internal/worktree/worktree.go). Three of the four original defects remain; the checked-in FIXME is already gone.

- `archieBranch` (line 610-612) documents "conventional commit prefix from the issue title when possible, falls back to labels", but `branchPrefix(title, body, labels)` (line 632) switches only on `labels` and returns "feat" otherwise. `title` and `body` are dead parameters.
- `strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, "")` (line 616) is a no-op: TrimSuffix with an empty suffix always returns its input, so the guard it appears to express does nothing.
- `branchSlug`'s doc comment (line 652-653) says "max 40 chars"; the implementation breaks at `b.Len() >= 60` (line 662).
- No FIXME or TODO remains in the file.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `archieBranch(12, "fix: crash on empty payload", "", "")` with no labels.
2. Expected per the doc comment: prefix `fix` derived from the title. Actual: `feat/12-fix-crash-on-empty-payload` — the title prefix is ignored and also left duplicated in the slug, because the strip branch only fires when `prefix` already matches the title.
3. Call `archieBranch(12, "<title of 80+ characters>", "", "bug")` and observe the slug runs to 60 characters, not the 40 the doc comment promises.

## Acceptance Criteria

The chosen title/label precedence is explicit and tested for unlabeled and conflicting inputs; dead parameters and the TrimSuffix no-op are removed; slug documentation and boundary tests agree with the implemented limit; scoped lint passes.
acceptance_criteria: The chosen title/label precedence is explicit and tested for unlabeled and conflicting inputs; dead parameters and no-op residue are removed; slug documentation and boundary tests agree with 60; scoped lint passes.
close_reason: Fixed: precedence is now title-first via parseTitlePrefix with a labels fallback and 'feat' default; the strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, "") no-op is gone; the dead body parameter is removed from archieBranch and its call site (worktree.go:131); branchSlug's doc now says 60, matching the implementation. go fix later modernised parseTitlePrefix to strings.Cut -- verified equivalent (Cut splits on the first separator; ok mirrors idx != -1). Verified by inspection rather than a red run, since the signature change prevents compiling the tests against pre-fix code. task check green; fresh adversarial review zero findings.

title: Clean no-change worktrees at terminal completion
description:
BuildNoChanges transitions directly to merged without a PR, bypassing the only production worktree cleanup path and leaking a full clone.

Confirmed still present on main. `closeNoChangesIssue` (internal/domain/workflow/steps.go:67-77) sets `Outcome{Status: store.StatusMerged}` directly, with no worktree removal. The only two production callers of `worktree.Manager.Cleanup` are internal/daemon/daemon.go:769 and :788, both inside the PR-state polling loop that transitions out of `StatusPROpen`. A task that reaches `merged` without ever opening a PR never enters that loop, so its clone is never removed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a task whose builder stage completes with `StatusPassed` but produces no diff, so `implement.go:166` sets `tc.BuildNoChanges = true`.
2. Let `StageCommitPush` run: it takes the `BuildNoChanges` branch, closes the issue, and sets the outcome to `merged`.
3. Observe the task row reaches `merged` with no PR number, so the daemon's `PRState` polling loop never sees it.
4. Inspect the workspace root: `<work_dir>/<base64(owner)>/<base64(repo)>/issue-<n>/` still contains the full clone.
5. Repeat for further no-change tasks and watch the directory count grow unbounded — nothing else removes them.

## Acceptance Criteria

Both direct and container no-change completion remove the identity-correct worktree while parked worktrees remain available; lifecycle regression tests cover the terminal path.
acceptance_criteria: Both direct and container no-change completion remove the identity-correct worktree while parked worktrees remain available; lifecycle regression tests cover the terminal path.

title: Preserve three-dot failure semantics without a merge base
description: patch silently computes a direct tree diff when base and HEAD have no merge base, contradicting its three-dot contract and corrupting diff-cap and gate inputs.

title: Do not report push failure after successful publication
description:
Push publishes the remote ref before writing unused local upstream metadata, then returns local config errors as if publication failed.

Confirmed still present on main: `Manager.Push` (internal/worktree/worktree.go:414-449) completes `r.PushContext` successfully, then calls `r.Config()` / `r.SetConfig(cfg)` to record branch upstream. Either of those returns `read repo config: %w` or `record branch upstream: %w` from `Push`, so a caller sees a push failure for a branch that is already published on the forge.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Prepare a task worktree and commit a change so there is a branch to publish.
2. Make the local repository config unwritable or unreadable after the remote is reachable (e.g. `chmod 000 <worktree>/.git/config`, or a `.git/config` the go-git config parser rejects).
3. Call `Manager.Push(ctx, dir, branch)`.
4. Observe the remote branch exists on the forge, but `Push` returns `record branch upstream: ...` (or `read repo config: ...`).
5. The daemon treats that error as a failed publication and parks the task, even though the PR branch is live.

## Acceptance Criteria

A post-publication metadata failure cannot park the task as an unsuccessful push; tests verify the remote ref and returned result remain consistent.
acceptance_criteria: A post-publication metadata failure cannot park the task as an unsuccessful push; tests verify the remote ref and returned result remain consistent.
close_reason: Fixed: recordUpstream extracted from Push (worktree.go:465); a post-publication config failure is now a logged warning and Push returns success once the remote ref is published. Manager gained an optional Log field with a slog.Default() fallback. Verified by inspection rather than a red run -- the test uses the new Log field so it cannot compile against the pre-fix code. task check green; fresh adversarial review (independent, did not write the code) zero findings.

title: Calibration: confirm findings adversarially before surfacing them
description:
The risk that kills this feature is a reviewer that cries wolf. A findings list padded with speculation trains the operator to skim past it, and then the feature is worse than nothing because it consumes attention while lowering trust.

Before a finding is surfaced, it must be independently checked and marked CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, with only CONFIRMED able to block. The reviewer must also be able to return zero findings, and to state which properties it checked and cleared -- a review that reports nothing is a valid and welcome result, and saying so explicitly is what distinguishes 'I checked and it is fine' from 'I did not look'.

Prior art from the 2026-08-20/21 sessions on PR #530: three passes each separated confirmed from plausible, one explicitly listed properties it had verified clean, and the confirmed findings were reproduced by mutation before being trusted. That calibration is the feature, not the finding count.
acceptance_criteria: Only CONFIRMED findings block PR creation; a zero-finding review is representable and reported as such; the reviewer records which properties it checked and cleared; padding with style nits is explicitly out of contract.

title: Surface findings on the PR body and the dashboard
description:
The output has to land where the operator already looks, or the review is invisible work.

On the PR archie opens: a findings section stating what was checked, what was found, what was fixed, and what survived. A PR with zero findings should say the review ran and found nothing -- silence is indistinguishable from the review not running, which is the same unverified-claim problem the update-verification work (PR #530) was about.

On the dashboard and /api/tasks: a parked-for-findings task must show why, the same way a park reason is already surfaced today. An operator seeing waiting_human needs the findings without digging through logs.
acceptance_criteria: PR body carries a findings section including the zero-finding case; a task parked on a surviving finding shows the findings as its park reason in the dashboard and /api/tasks; nothing requires reading task logs to learn why a PR was withheld.

title: Dashboard-initiated updates get no phase-2 report, so they are never verified
description:
internal/webui/api_chat.go:497 starts an install with releaseupdate.InstallMeta{Channel: "webui"} and leaves ReportPath empty. CommandInstaller passes that through as ARCHIE_UPDATE_REPORT_PATH, and scripts/archie-update-watchdog's write_report() returns early when it is empty.

Consequences: an operator who approves an update from the dashboard gets only the synchronous phase-1 result (build/install succeeded, restart queued) and never learns whether the daemon actually came back up, whether it was rolled back, or - since c25799e - whether the installed version is the one now running. Telegram gets all of that; the dashboard silently gets none of it.

The verification added in c25799e (releaseupdate.Report.Verify) is reached only from internal/channels/telegram/update.go, so this path is unverified regardless.

Fix needs two parts: give the webui install a ReportPath (updateReportPath in cmd/archied), and give the dashboard somewhere to relay a pending report on boot the way telegram's reportPendingUpdate does - today ReadPendingReport has exactly one caller, and a single report file shared by two relayers would race to clear it.
acceptance_criteria: A dashboard-approved update produces a phase-2 report; the dashboard surfaces its outcome including version verification; two relayers cannot double-report or lose a report.
close_reason: Fixed: dashboard installs now get a ReportPath, and Server.Run relays/verifies/clears the phase-2 report on boot via a new KindUpdateReport SSE event. Adversarial review clean.

title: MCP npm servers re-fetched from npm on every task container start
description:
## Problem

d4bb914b/#64 fixed the daemon-side case: cmd/archied/main.go's
configuredMCPProvider now points npx-launched MCP servers at a persistent
NPM_CONFIG_CACHE under the daemon's own work_dir, so a daemon restart
reuses a warm cache instead of re-resolving/re-downloading from the npm
registry.

internal/app/agentworker/mcp_providers.go builds the identical
StdioTransportConfig for archie-agent's own per-task MCP servers, but was
deliberately left untouched -- it's not a separate code path, the exact
same cfg.Tools.MCPServers list (including any npx entries) is threaded
through to every per-task NATS agent worker (bootstrap.go -> NATSRunner.MCPServers
-> taskrun.Request -> task_execution.go's startMCPProviders). Since each
task runs in a fresh ephemeral container, an npx-based MCP server
configured for task use re-resolves/re-downloads on every task, not
just every daemon restart -- more frequent, and thus a worse amplifier of
a registry outage than the bug already fixed.

## Why this needs its own issue

Unlike the daemon case, a bare NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=<path> pointed at a host
directory is meaningless inside an ephemeral container unless a
persistent Docker volume is actually bind-mounted at that path. No such
volume currently exists for this purpose -- internal/container/pool.go's
mounts are caller-provided, and nothing wires an npm-cache volume in.
That's real new infrastructure (a shared, persistent volume across
per-task containers), not a parameter-threading fix like d4bb914b was.

## Acceptance criteria

- Task containers reuse a persistent npm cache across tasks, the same
  way the daemon now does across restarts.
- The cache volume/mount is wired through internal/container/pool.go's
  Acquire (or equivalent) without weakening per-task filesystem isolation
  for anything other than the npm cache path itself.
- Startup time for a task's npx-based MCP server no longer scales with
  package size once the cache is warm.
close_reason: Fixed: MCP npm servers for per-task containers now reuse a persistent npm cache. Added mcp.NpmCacheEnv (shared with the daemon-side fix), an always-on archie-cache-mcp-npm Docker volume mounted at /data/cache/mcp-npm on every task container regardless of ecosystem, and wired it into internal/app/agentworker/mcp_providers.go's stdio transport construction. Adversarial review found zero surviving findings. [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-22, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]
