title: dashboard: turn_completed events carry no task correlation and drown real activity in the Live Activity feed
description:
## Problem, two compounding parts

**1. `turn_completed` events carry no useful, correlatable content.**
`internal/gateway/turn.go:306-311` publishes:
```go
r.Bus.Publish(events.Event{
    Kind:   events.KindTurnCompleted,
    Detail: sessionID,
    Data:   map[string]any{"session": sessionID, "channel": r.Channel},
})
```
No `TaskID` is set, and `Detail` is a raw internal session identifier (e.g. `1312197967`) with no formatting. On the dashboard's "Live activity" table this renders as `Task: —`, `Detail: 1312197967` — meaningless to anyone reading it, and impossible to correlate to a task. This event fires on every chat turn, so it dominates the feed: in a sample of the 30 most-recent Live Activity rows, only 3 were real task-lifecycle events (`task_queued`); the other 27 were content-free `turn_completed` rows.

**2. The `/logs` page has no filtering, search, or level control at all** — just Pause/Refresh. Confirmed live: during the redelivery storm in #517, `handle failed` alone produced 996 near-identical lines, and there is no way to filter by task, by level, or search text to find anything else in the stream. During exactly the situation an operator needs the log page most (an active incident), it is unusable.

## Fix

- Give `turn_completed` (and any other cross-cutting event shown in this feed) a human-meaningful `Detail` — e.g. the channel name plus a short session label — and drop it from the feed entirely if it isn't task-correlated, since a feed titled "Live activity" that is 90% non-actionable chat-turn noise defeats its own purpose.
- Add basic filtering to `/logs`: at minimum a level filter and a task/session search, so a single noisy source can be excluded without losing everything else.

title: Dashboard: Token outlook is blank because token usage is not reaching daily accounting
description:
## Problem

The dashboard's **Token outlook** card is blank instead of showing token usage/spend. The screenshot shows the card present but with no usable content.

## Investigation

The live dashboard API currently returns:

```json
{
  "workflows": [
    {"workflow":"tdd","total_tokens":904901,"avg_tokens":301633},
    {"workflow":"implement","total_tokens":0}
  ],
  "tokens_by_day": null
}
```

The dashboard frontend expects `tokens_by_day` and renders the empty state when it is missing/empty (`ui/src/dashboard/dashboard.js:405-418`). The runtime therefore has token totals in the `tasks` table but no daily token series for the card.

The persistence path is inconsistent:

- `internal/domain/workflow/agent.go:171-176` records `res.TokensUsed` on the task and emits an `agent_finish` event with `data.tokens`.
- `internal/store/events.go:231-251` calculates the card data exclusively from persisted `agent_finish` events.
- The live task event database currently contains `task_queued` and `turn_completed` events but no `agent_finish` rows, while workflow statistics still contain 904,901 tokens.
- `handleSummary` serializes the nil result from `TokensByDay` as JSON `null`, rather than a stable empty array or a meaningful unavailable state.

This means the dashboard cannot truthfully show spend even though token usage is already tracked elsewhere.

## Expected behaviour

- Completed agent runs contribute to the Token outlook series and the Tokens used statistic.
- The API returns `tokens_by_day: []` rather than `null` when no data exists.
- The UI distinguishes "no usage recorded yet" from "usage tracking is unavailable/broken".
- Token totals and daily totals come from one authoritative accounting path and do not diverge.
- The card never renders blank.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a regression test reproducing the current state: tasks have non-zero `tokens_used`, but no `agent_finish` rows; the summary must still have a defined, truthful token state.
- Trace and repair the event persistence path so successful and failed agent runs produce the data required by `TokensByDay`, including NATS/container execution.
- Add store/API tests asserting daily aggregation, timezone/day semantics, empty data, malformed/missing token fields, and multiple stages per task.
- Return an empty JSON array for an empty series, not `null`.
- Add a UI test for populated data, no data, and unavailable/error states; verify the card cannot be visually blank.
- Verify against a running daemon with real task data and run the normal project gate.

## Scope

This issue is about truthful token accounting and the Token outlook dashboard. It does not attempt to add provider billing APIs or dollar pricing unless required to make the existing token accounting correct.

title: Telegram: response formatting concatenates URLs with following text
description:
## Problem

Telegram responses can concatenate a bare URL with the sentence that follows it, which breaks the clickable/direct link and makes the message look malformed.

This has occurred at least twice. Example:

```text
https://github.com/samcharles93/archie-core/issues/513It includes model-independent safeguards...
```

The expected output is:

```text
https://github.com/samcharles93/archie-core/issues/513

It includes model-independent safeguards...
```

## Desired behavior

- Preserve paragraph/newline boundaries between links and subsequent text.
- Ensure a bare URL remains independently clickable in Telegram.
- Do not concatenate separately streamed/rendered response segments.
- Apply the fix consistently whether the response is sent once, edited while streaming, or split into multiple Telegram messages.

## Acceptance criteria

- A URL followed by prose is rendered with at least one newline separating them.
- Bare GitHub issue URLs remain clickable and contain no trailing prose.
- Regression coverage includes the exact example above.
- Coverage exercises the relevant Telegram streaming/editing and message-splitting paths.
close_reason: Fixed Telegram URL/prose boundary normalization across one-shot, live, and split delivery paths; added Markdown/code safety, newline preservation, and regression coverage.

title: Agent falsely claims GitHub issue creation succeeded without verification
description:
## Problem

During a Telegram chat using `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, the agent stated that it had created GitHub issue #512 and supplied a URL even though no issue had been created. When challenged, it acknowledged the false claim and said it lacked a GitHub token; after being asked to retry, the issue creation succeeded.

This is a serious trust and UX problem: users must be able to rely on claims about external side effects such as creating issues, pushing branches, opening PRs, deploying, or restarting services.

## Expected behavior

- Never report an external action as successful unless the corresponding tool/plugin call completed successfully and returned verifiable output.
- Include the issue number and URL from the forge response, not values inferred or fabricated by the model.
- If the tool is unavailable or fails, report the actual failure clearly.
- Allow a retry when the capability may be temporarily unavailable.

## Suggested safeguards

- Require successful structured tool results before permitting success language for side-effecting actions.
- Track pending/completed/failed action state in the turn runner.
- Add a postcondition check for issue creation, such as validating the returned issue ID/URL.
- Add regression tests using a model response that falsely claims an issue was created without invoking the forge tool.
- Consider a gateway warning or telemetry event when a final response claims an unverified side effect.

## Reproduction

1. Ask the agent to create an issue.
2. The model responds with an issue number and URL without a successful forge invocation.
3. Check GitHub and observe that the issue does not exist.

## Context

Observed with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` through the Telegram gateway. This should be enforced independently of model/provider because any model can make an unsupported action claim.

## Frequency

This has been observed twice in the same conversation, so it is a recurring failure rather than a one-off hallucination. Regression coverage should include repeated side-effect claims across turns, including claims that reuse a plausible issue number and URL.
close_reason: Deprioritized: prompt-level fix landed in fba80e3 (archie-core-3jag/GH#524) covers the general overconfidence pattern. Not worth mechanical enforcement (postcondition checks, tool-result verification) unless this recurs — revisit with stronger prompting first if it does. [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-23, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: Polish the /status command response
description:
## Problem

The `/status` command response is functional but lacks polish and is difficult to scan. The current output looks like:

```text
Task status: parked:2
Provider: deepseek Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

The information is compressed into raw key/value text, and task state, provider, and model details are not clearly separated.

## Desired behaviour

Present status information in a compact, polished, mobile-friendly format suitable for Telegram. It should make the most important state immediately obvious and visually separate task and runtime/model information.

For example:

```text
📊 Archie status

Tasks
⏸ Parked:2

Runtime
Provider: OpenAI
Model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna
```

The exact wording and icons can follow existing Telegram UI conventions.

## Acceptance criteria

- `/status` has a clear heading and grouped sections.
- Task states are shown on separate, readable lines.
- Provider and model are clearly separated.
- The response remains concise and readable on mobile.
- Empty and unavailable values have a graceful fallback.
- Tests cover the formatted response, including multiple task states and missing runtime details.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add end-to-end image generation test matrix and operational safeguards
description:
## Scope
Build the cross-cutting test and verification layer for the image capability. Exercise the clarification flow, hosted fake provider, local fake backend, real local recipe smoke test where available, delivery, and failure paths.

Add safeguards for cost, resource use, prompt/input limits, concurrency, cancellation, and observability consistent with Archie''s existing operational style.

## Acceptance criteria
- Automated tests cover both mechanisms, generation and editing, routing, provider failures, delivery failures, cancellation, and cleanup.
- Tests assert no provider call occurs before mechanism clarification.
- Resource and input/output limits are enforced in code and tested.
- A documented local smoke command verifies at least one GPU recipe without requiring hosted credentials.
- The normal project gate passes, and the epic's acceptance criteria can be verified from real command output.

title: Write image capability documentation and agent assistance examples
description:
## Scope
Document the user-facing `/image` flow, hosted-provider setup, local GPU setup, supported model/backend recipes, troubleshooting, resource requirements, and security/cost implications.

Provide concise code/config examples an agent can use to help users call both hosted and local paths. Examples must show how to inspect hardware/backend availability, choose a tested model, submit a generation/edit request, and collect the resulting image.

## Acceptance criteria
- Documentation explicitly says mechanism selection happens first by default.
- Hosted API baseline fields and provider deviations are documented.
- Every local model recipe names its tested backend/version, model source, VRAM/RAM expectations, supported sizes/operations, and failure modes.
- Examples are runnable or tested in CI with mocked services; no secrets or huge weights are included.
- Docs distinguish tested support from illustrative/untested possibilities.

title: Deliver generated images through channel and web abstractions
description:
## Scope
Extend the existing message/result delivery abstraction so generated images can reach users safely through supported channels and the web UI. Preserve useful metadata such as prompt/provider/model and errors without exposing credentials or internal filesystem paths.

Use bounded temporary storage/cleanup and a clear policy for formats, dimensions, compression, and maximum response size. Ensure a failed upload does not leave the user with a success-looking text response.

## Acceptance criteria
- A provider result can be delivered as an image through each currently supported delivery path, or unsupported paths report a clear limitation.
- Temporary files and downloaded inputs have bounded size and deterministic cleanup.
- MIME/format handling, alt text/caption, and metadata are tested.
- Delivery failures, retries/cancellation, and partial-success behavior are tested.
- Existing text and file delivery behavior remains unchanged.

title: Implement /image mechanism clarification and routing flow
description:
## Scope
Make the default `/image` workflow ask the user for their preferred generation mechanism before running a request when no mechanism is already selected: hosted API or local GPU. Present the choices and relevant constraints concisely, then collect only the options needed for the selected mechanism.

Support an explicit per-request override and a clearly scoped remembered preference only where existing session/config conventions support it. Never silently fall back from hosted to local or local to hosted.

## Acceptance criteria
- `/image` with no mechanism produces a clarification prompt and does not invoke a provider.
- Hosted and local selections route to the correct provider with the selected options.
- The flow supports generation and edit requests, including input-image validation.
- Invalid choices, missing credentials, unavailable GPU backends, and cancellation produce actionable replies.
- Channel-neutral tests cover the state machine; Telegram/web behavior is covered at the adapter boundary where applicable.

title: Add local GPU image generation backend and tested model recipes
description:
## Scope
Add a local GPU path that can execute image generation on an existing user GPU through a supported local backend/API. Prefer integration with an established server/workflow interface over embedding model runtimes or downloading weights from Archie.

Ship a tested initial recipe set for common models appropriate to consumer GPUs, with the exact model files, backend versions, VRAM/RAM expectations, supported operations, and known limitations recorded. Include runnable code/config examples that Archie can use to assist a user in setting up and calling the backend.

The implementation must report unavailable hardware/backend/model conditions clearly and must not pretend an untested model is supported.

## Acceptance criteria
- At least one local GPU recipe is exercised end-to-end on real hardware or a reproducible maintained test harness.
- Additional recipes are included only with evidence, covering model/backend/version, VRAM, image sizes, and speed/quality trade-offs.
- Backend URL/auth/timeout and model selection are configurable.
- Local generation returns the same provider-neutral result shape as hosted generation.
- Tests cover backend unavailable, malformed response, timeout, cancellation, and model-not-found paths.
- No model weights are committed or downloaded into the repository/home partition.

title: Implement hosted gpt-image-2-compatible image provider
description:
## Scope
Implement the hosted image provider behind the image capability contract, targeting the practical baseline of the OpenAI `gpt-image-2` API.

Cover text-to-image and image editing where supported by the API, prompt and image inputs, size/quality/background/output-format/compression-style options exposed by the baseline, response decoding, and provider error mapping. Do not claim unsupported parity: document exact API version/endpoint assumptions and any deliberate differences.

## Acceptance criteria
- Uses the existing HTTP/auth/configuration patterns rather than a one-off client.
- Request serialization and response decoding are covered with httptest fixtures.
- Provider failures, malformed responses, timeouts, oversized inputs, and cancellation are handled without panics or leaked secrets.
- No live API key is needed for tests.
- A small runnable example shows the request shape and configuration.
notes: Leverage github.com/samcharles93/ai-sdk's existing image.Provider/core.GenerateImage/registry.RegisterImage for the generate path (azure/togetherai/xai already implement it; OpenAI does not yet) instead of writing a raw HTTP client -- same adapter pattern curatorLLMRunner uses for chat. Gap: ai-sdk's GenerateImageRequest has no input-image/mask fields, so editing needs either an upstream ai-sdk change or a separate direct client for the edit endpoint. Decide which at this bead's own design step. See docs/prds/image-capability-contract.md's closing note.

title: Define provider-neutral image capability contract and configuration
description:
## Scope
Define the internal image-generation capability boundary used by hosted and local providers. Keep it narrow and provider-neutral: generation, editing with input images, prompt/options, output metadata, cancellation/timeouts, and capability discovery.

Add configuration and provider selection that fit the existing model/provider conventions. A missing credential or unavailable backend must make the capability unavailable with a useful user-facing error, not prevent Archie from starting or break text chat.

## Acceptance criteria
- Typed request/result/options contract covers the agreed gpt-image-2 baseline without baking in OpenAI types.
- Provider registry/resolution and capability discovery are testable with fakes.
- Hosted vs local selection is explicit and cannot silently incur cost.
- Timeouts, maximum input/output sizes, cancellation, and error taxonomy are defined and tested.
- Configuration validation rejects unsafe/ambiguous settings and preserves existing config behavior.
close_reason: Shipped docs/prds/image-capability-contract.md plus internal/domain/image (Provider contract, Registry — no Lifecycle, provider is call-scoped) and config.ImageConfig/validateImage. Provider-neutral, tested with fakes, hosted+local both gated by explicit enabled=true. Also linked all 7 orphaned epic children (found unlinked again, same pattern as the curator/memory epics).

title: [EPIC] Image generation capability: hosted API baseline plus local GPU workflows
description:
## Goal
Add first-class image generation to Archie, with a capability surface targeting the practical baseline of the OpenAI `gpt-image-2` API while also supporting image generation on a user's existing GPU.

The capability must not assume one backend. A user asking for `/image` is first asked which generation mechanism they prefer:
- hosted API (starting with an OpenAI-compatible `gpt-image-2` provider), or
- local GPU generation using one of Archie's tested model/backend recipes.

## Scope
- A provider-neutral image capability contract and routing/configuration.
- Hosted generation/editing with an OpenAI `gpt-image-2`-class API baseline.
- Local GPU generation through tested, documented model/backend recipes suitable for common consumer GPUs.
- `/image` clarification and execution flow across supported channels.
- Returned image delivery, bounded inputs/outputs, errors, and tests.

## Non-goals
- Training or fine-tuning image models.
- Bundling multi-gigabyte model weights in Archie.
- Pretending every GPU/model combination is supported; local support must be explicit and evidence-backed.
- Replacing the existing text-chat capability or silently selecting a paid hosted provider.

## Definition of done
- `/image` asks for the preferred mechanism before generation when no mechanism is already selected for the request/session.
- Hosted generation and editing cover the documented gpt-image-2 baseline, with provider-specific differences exposed rather than hidden.
- Local GPU generation works end-to-end with at least one tested recipe, and additional tested common models are documented with VRAM/backend requirements and runnable examples.
- Images can be delivered through the existing channel abstractions without leaking temporary files or unbounded data.
- Unit, integration, and failure-path tests cover routing, provider errors, clarification, local execution, and delivery.
- Configuration, security, and operational documentation are complete.

Subtasks below are dependency-ordered where practical; each must link back to this epic and state any deliberate deviations from the hosted API baseline.

title: telegram: a tool-use turn ending with no answer posts the tool line alone as the finished message
description:
finalText returns the tool block alone when the reply is empty, and finalize sends it as the authoritative finished message — content == '' is the only silence path, so an empty-reply turn with completed tools permanently delivers '🔧 shell — exit 0' with no answer. The old path guarded 'if reply != ""'. Telegram messages are immutable, so it can never be corrected. Gated on show_tool_calls (off by default), so it bites opt-in deployments. No test covers finalize with an empty reply and tools.

Failure: the model ends a tool-use loop without a final summary (empty ResponseText); the finished message shows only the tool line, looking like a completed answer that said nothing.
design: When the reply is empty, do not post the tool block as the answer — either skip the final send (leave the cursor-cleaned live message) or emit an explicit 'no reply' marker. Add a test for finalize(empty, tools).
acceptance_criteria: A turn that ends with tools but no answer text does not post a bare tool line as the final message.
close_reason: Fixed in internal/channels/telegram/live.go: framedText keeps tool lines whole ahead of the clamped answer tail (fixes wpq6); finalText appends a '(no response)' marker when tools ran but the reply is empty (fixes hlxd); abandonFailed marks a provider-error partial distinctly from a clean /stop abandon (fixes c3w2). Regression tests verified red-then-green; adversarial review found no blocking issues (added one more test for the degenerate oversized-tool-block case it flagged). task check clean, committed as 587b9b9.

title: webui: the dashboard narrates tool calls with no opt-out; show_tool_calls only gates Telegram
description:
show_tool_calls gates only the Telegram adapter. The web dashboard's chatStreamSink forwards every ToolCallEvent unconditionally (api_chat.go:228) — no config key exists anywhere in webui — so an operator following the documented intent (show_tool_calls off means no tool narration) still gets full per-tool narration in the web dashboard with no way to disable it. The ToolCallEvent contract comment (stream.go:18-20) delegates 'whether to show it at all' to the channel adapter, but only the Telegram adapter exercises the knob.

Failure: an operator with the default show_tool_calls=false opens the web dashboard; every internal tool step of every web chat is narrated in full, exposing tool inventory and parameter shapes to anyone with dashboard access.
design: Either add a webui-equivalent config key and gate the sink on it, or make show_tool_calls a cross-channel setting. Decide and document the intent, then wire the webui sink to honor it.
acceptance_criteria: With the setting off, the web dashboard does not emit tool frames; with it on, it does — controlled by one documented knob.
close_reason: Fixed: ShowToolCalls moved from TelegramConfig to ChatConfig (one cross-channel setting), webui's chatStreamSink gated on it (off by default, matching Telegram). Adversarial review clean aside from cosmetic/doc notes, both addressed. Breaking config-key move flagged explicitly in the commit body since it's a silent TOML drop, not an error. Committed f7590a6.

title: gateway: replay and redelivery lose tool activity, showing duplicate answers without tools
description:
The replay paths (TurnClaimCompleted, prior-reply) emit stream.Delta(ResponseText) only — never stream.ToolCall — and neither the ledger (TurnRecord) nor the session store persists tool activity. A completed-duplicate delivery (NATS redelivery, restart RecoverTurns re-delivery) finalizes a fresh liveReply with empty toolLines and sends the bare reply as a new message: the transcript shows the original (with tools) and the duplicate (without) side by side, disagreeing about what ran. Web history has the same gap — stored assistant messages render text only.

Failure: a chat message is redelivered or re-queued after restart; the user sees the same answer twice, the second copy lacking the tool block that explains it.
design: Decide whether tool activity should be persisted (ledger/session store) and replayed, or whether replays simply should not re-narrate tools. If persisting, add a tool-activity record to the turn/message and replay it; if not, make the replay path explicitly consistent and document the choice.
acceptance_criteria: A redelivered/restarted turn does not show a tool-less duplicate disagreeing with the original; the behavior is explicitly decided and tested.
close_reason: Fixed: TurnRecord now persists tool-call activity alongside ResponseText; the completed-duplicate replay path replays it via stream.ToolCall before the text. Prior-reply fallback documented as deliberately text-only (crash race with no persisted tool record). Commit 86a9731, task check clean, adversarial review clean (0 findings). [Closure restored 2026-08-24: originally closed 2026-08-22, lost when the beads DB was rebuilt (.beads.backup-pre-recovery).]

title: webui: derive tool failure from a structured field, not a 'failed:' string prefix
description:
The web UI derives failure styling with summary.startsWith('failed:') on the rendered string (chat-tools.js:25), while chatStreamEvent (api_chat.go) carries no structured error/ok field — the doc comment says the intent was structured precisely so the browser could style the two apart instead of parsing a rendered string, but the bit was dropped. False positives are concrete: a successful tool whose first output line begins with 'failed: ' is styled as a failure. Nothing pins the Go 'failed: ' prefix to the client sniff (the UI test feeds the literal string), so a future rewording silently breaks failure styling.

Failure: a successful shell command printing 'failed: no such file' to stdout exits 0; the web chat renders it red as an error step.
design: Add an explicit error/ok field to ToolCallEvent and chatStreamEvent (e.g. a bool or the raw Err), thread it through the sink, and style on that instead of the rendered string. Update the UI test to feed the structured field.
acceptance_criteria: A successful tool printing 'failed: …' is not styled as a failure; failure styling is driven by a structured signal, not string matching.
close_reason: Fixed in internal/webui/api_chat.go + ui/src/chat/chat-tools.js: chatStreamEvent now carries a structured Failed bool (from ToolCallEvent.Err != ""); JS reads event.failed instead of sniffing the summary text. Adversarial review found zero issues. Committed a99a770.

title: telegram: tool lines disappear from the live frame once the answer exceeds ~3900 runes
description:
Mid-turn frames keep only the tail (clampToOneMessage keeps the last 3900 runes with a leading ellipsis). Tool lines are written inline near the start of the buffer — before the answer, since tools run before the answer in agentic turns — so once the answer exceeds ~3900 runes, every early tool line vanishes from the live frame (the buffer only grows; nothing re-inserts them mid-turn). They reappear at the top at finalize. The visible message changes shape three times (tool-inline, gone behind the ellipsis, tools-on-top) and the user watching mid-turn sees the tool activity silently disappear.

Failure: a turn with an early web_fetch followed by a 4000-rune answer shows only '...' + tail with no tool line for the bulk of the turn.
design: Keep tool lines outside the clamped tail — render the tool block above the truncated answer tail in the live frame — so tool activity stays visible for the whole turn.
acceptance_criteria: In a turn with an early tool call and a >3900-rune answer, the live frame still shows the tool line(s) at the top rather than hiding them behind the ellipsis.
close_reason: Fixed in internal/channels/telegram/live.go: framedText keeps tool lines whole ahead of the clamped answer tail (fixes wpq6); finalText appends a '(no response)' marker when tools ran but the reply is empty (fixes hlxd); abandonFailed marks a provider-error partial distinctly from a clean /stop abandon (fixes c3w2). Regression tests verified red-then-green; adversarial review found no blocking issues (added one more test for the degenerate oversized-tool-block case it flagged). task check clean, committed as 587b9b9.

title: telegram: a restart mid-turn strands a permanent message ending in the ▌ cursor
description:
The live reply is a real, permanent Telegram message (SendRichMessage) whose messageID lives only in the in-memory liveReply struct. No shutdown path — supervisor restart in Start, daemon stop, launch() rebuilding Turns — edits or deletes it. A restart mid-turn strands a permanent message ending in ▌ that nothing will ever finish. The old draft path self-deleted (ephemeral 30-second previews); this is a new class of leftover introduced by the live-edit design.

Failure: the operator restarts the daemon or deploys a new build while a turn is streaming; the partial reply with the cursor persists in the chat indefinitely, implying the bot is still writing.
design: On gateway Stop/restart, track in-flight liveReply instances (a registry keyed by chat/thread) and edit them to drop the cursor and/or append a cancelled/restarted marker — or delete them. Decide the desired end state for an interrupted turn.
acceptance_criteria: A daemon restart during a streamed turn leaves no ▌-terminated message; the partial reply is either completed, marked, or removed.
close_reason: Fixed: Gateway tracks in-flight liveReply instances in a registry Stop drains, marking each interrupted. Adversarial review found a critical race (concurrent finalize/abandon on the same reply could corrupt the message) plus two lesser issues (unbounded blocking Stop, a narrow post-snapshot registration gap) -- all three fixed: sync.Once serializes finalize/abandon, the drain is time-bounded (default 5s, entries left running in background past that), and registerLive checks a stopped flag to immediately abandon a straggler. Re-reviewed via targeted regression tests including a 20-iteration concurrent race test. task check clean, -race clean across repeated runs. Committed 09ea210.

title: telegram: mark a failed turn instead of leaving an indistinguishable partial
description:
Both /stop and a genuine provider error funnel into live.abandon() (telegram.go:573), which trims the buffer, drops the cursor, and leaves the partial text as a permanent message with no failure marker — indistinguishable from a finished reply. /stop at least acks via stopReport; the provider-error branch sends nothing to the user, so a failed turn reads as complete and the user may act on incomplete information. The codebase's own error pattern (the ❌ session-resolution failure message) is unused here.

Failure: the model stream errors (provider 5xx, timeout) after three paragraphs; the bot's last message is the truncated text with no cursor and no error note; the user treats it as the final answer.
design: On provider error (not /stop), append or prepend an error marker to the abandoned message (e.g. a ❌ … failed line), or send a follow-up error message, so a truncated turn is visibly not the answer.
acceptance_criteria: A provider-error turn leaves a message that visibly signals failure; /stop still leaves a clean partial without a spurious error.
close_reason: Fixed in internal/channels/telegram/live.go: framedText keeps tool lines whole ahead of the clamped answer tail (fixes wpq6); finalText appends a '(no response)' marker when tools ran but the reply is empty (fixes hlxd); abandonFailed marks a provider-error partial distinctly from a clean /stop abandon (fixes c3w2). Regression tests verified red-then-green; adversarial review found no blocking issues (added one more test for the degenerate oversized-tool-block case it flagged). task check clean, committed as 587b9b9.

title: Clear cmd/archie-agent golangci-lint baseline
description:
## Problem
Full-package golangci-lint currently reports findings in cmd/archie-agent, including noctx in taskrun_test.go. This prevents using a clean package lint gate while refactoring main.go.

## Scope
Fix evidence-backed golangci-lint findings in cmd/archie-agent without weakening lint configuration or changing runtime behavior. Coordinate with the MCP extraction where that extraction removes the startMCPProviders complexity finding.

## Acceptance
- golangci-lint run ./cmd/archie-agent/... reports zero findings
- focused tests, vet, build, formatting, and task check pass
- no lint suppressions or configuration exclusions are added
acceptance_criteria: cmd/archie-agent full-package lint is zero with no suppressions; tests, vet, build and task check pass
notes:
Implementation and validation are complete in /tmp/archie-core-agent-cleanup on branch refactor/archie-agent-main-cleanup, but delivery is pending: changes are uncommitted, not integrated into the target branch, and not pushed. Do not close until those delivery steps are complete.
 Validation completed: golangci-lint run ./cmd/archie-agent/... reports zero issues without suppressions.
Delivered on review branch refactor/archie-agent-main-cleanup at de242f8; pending PR review/merge.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #480 at 52738f5; implementation commit de242f8 passed task check, race tests, lint, and independent review

title: Extract archie-agent task subscription concern
description:
## Problem
main.go owns boot task discovery and taskrun subscription selection in addition to process composition.

## Scope
Move bootTaskID and subscribeTaskRuns into a concern-named cmd/archie-agent source file, preserving dedicated-container versus shared-queue behavior and existing tests.

## Acceptance
- boot brief parsing and taskrun subscription selection are outside main.go
- behavior and logging remain unchanged
- focused tests and task check pass

title: agent containers: git dubious-ownership causes all gates to fail
description:
## Problem

Agent containers bind-mount the worktree from the host at `/data/worktree`, where the owning UID differs from the container user's UID. Git refuses to operate in such directories ("fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository"), and the Go toolchain calls git for VCS status during `go build`/`go test`/`go vet`.

This means every gate — baseline gate, build gate, TDD repro gate — fails immediately, before any real work begins. Agents burn tokens trying to fix the environment instead of working on the assigned issue.

## Evidence

- Task for issue #441 burned 557K tokens across 29 iterations and parked with `gate_failed_final` — the agent never reached the actual multi-forge fix
- `go build` within the container fails with `error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128`
- The agent's uncommitted `build_test.go` recognized the real cause: "A pre-existing git dubious-ownership issue causes the build to fail"

## Fix

Add `git config --global --add safe.directory /data/worktree` at archie-agent startup. The worktree mount path is always `/data/worktree` (storage.WorktreeMountDir). The command is best-effort: if git isn't installed, the agent logs a warning and continues — it remains usable for repos without gate commands.

## Files

- `cmd/archie-agent/main.go`: run git safe.directory config after logger init
close_reason: Fixed: internal/infrastructure/agentgit/safety.go's MarkSafe adds the mounted worktree to git's global safe.directory list, and it is wired into the actual agent-container startup path -- internal/app/agentworker/worker.go:63,84 calls dependencies.markSafe(ctx, workDir, log) unconditionally in run(), before NATS connect and before any gate executes. Confirmed by grep this is the only non-test call site (worker.go), so it isn't dead/unwired code. go test ./internal/infrastructure/agentgit/... and ./internal/app/agentworker/... -race -count=1 both pass, including worker_test.go coverage that exercises the run() path with markSafe wired in. This matches the exact fix archie-core-1786749700606-6-bf6aa32d already describes as done ('#468 ... resolved by safe.directory').

title: Telegram gateway: show tool calls inline during chat turns
description:
The Telegram chat agent returns only the final answer. The user cannot see which tools are being called, their parameters, or their results. This makes debugging agent behavior (hallucinations, wrong tool choices, footguns like `systemctl stop` vs `restart`) impossible from the chat side.

## Desired behavior

After each tool call completes, the gateway sends a compact inline message showing the tool name and a one-line summary of the result, before the next tool call or final answer. Similar to how Hermes surfaces tool calls in Telegram.

Example format:
```
🔧 memory_edit — added entry
🔧 terminal — systemctl --user stop archied (exit 0)
🔧 terminal — systemctl --user start archied (exit 0)
```

Then the final answer.

## Scope

`internal/channels/telegram/` only. Behind a config flag `[chat.telegram] show_tool_calls = true` so it can be toggled.

## Technical approach

Currently the call chain is:

```
submitTurn → router.RouteStream(turnCtx, gm, draft.onDelta)
           → r.LLMStream(ctx, msg, onDelta)
           → TurnRunner.Run(ctx, msg, onDelta)
           → prepared.Generate(ctx, req, onDelta)
```

Only `onDelta` (text streaming) is threaded through. Tool calls happen inside `Generate` but there's no callback back to the gateway.

### What needs to change

1. **Add a tool-call observer callback** — either extend `LLMStreamResponder` signature or add a separate `OnToolCall` field to `gateway.Router` struct, plumbing it through `TurnRunner` → `TurnModel`/`PreparedTurnModel.Generate` so model providers can report tool invocations

2. **Model provider integration** — the chat turn model (`cmd/archied/chat_turn_model.go`) and any provider-specific `Generate` implementations need to call the observer when a tool is executed, passing tool name + result summary

3. **Telegram gateway wiring** — in `submitTurn` (`internal/channels/telegram/telegram.go`), if `show_tool_calls` config is true, wire the observer to send a compact inline message via `sendMessage` before the final reply

4. **Config plumbing** — add `ShowToolCalls bool` to the Telegram gateway config struct and read it from `[chat.telegram] show_tool_calls` in `telegram_setup.go`

### Key files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `internal/gateway/gateway.go` | `RouteStream`, `Router` struct (add observer field) |
| `internal/gateway/turn.go` | `TurnRunner.Run`, `PreparedTurnModel.Generate` signature |
| `cmd/archied/chat_turn_model.go` | Model provider `Generate` — where tool calls execute |
| `internal/channels/telegram/telegram.go` | `submitTurn` — wire observer + send messages |
| `cmd/archied/telegram_setup.go` | Config reading + gateway construction |

title: webui/chat: surface per-task logs via API and a chat tool
description:
Part of #450. Depends on #453 (daemon subscriber).

Add `/api/tasks/{id}/logs`, built on `logging.Reader` the same way
`/api/logs` is today (`internal/webui/api_logs.go`).

Add a chat tool so Archie can answer "why did task N park?" directly from
Telegram or the webui chat, without an operator needing to open the
dashboard. This is the surface that matters most for the deployment model
in `CLAUDE.md`, where an operator may not be watching a dashboard at all.

title: daemon: subscribe agent system logs and route to task sink + dashboard feed
description:
Part of #450. Depends on #451 (task log sink) and #452 (agent publisher).

Subscribe `agentexec.SubjectAgentWildcard` ("archie.agent.>") for the
`.system` suffix once at daemon startup. This is composition — wiring the
domain's log sink to the NATS subscription — so it belongs in `internal/app/`,
not in `internal/domain/workflow` or `internal/nats` directly.

Demux by task ID, append each entry to that task's sink, and also publish it
into the existing `logging.Feed` so live task/container output appears on
the dashboard exactly like daemon output does today.

Also: prune a task's log directory when `nell.ArchiveTask`
(`internal/nell/adapter.go`) archives it, so task logs share the task's own
lifecycle instead of growing unbounded.

title: agentexec: publish agent logs to SubjectForSystem
description:
Part of #450. Depends on #451 (task log sink).

`agentexec.SubjectForSystem` is documented as the return channel for "log
dumps, health, and PII warnings" but has no publisher anywhere in the
codebase.

In `cmd/archie-agent/main.go`, replace the stderr-only `slog.Handler` with
one that tees to stderr (kept for operator debugging when a shell is
attached to a live container) and publishes each record to
`agentexec.SubjectForSystem(taskID)`. The agent already has its NATS client
and task ID (`bootTaskID`, read from `<worktree>/.git/task.json`).

Publishing must be fire-and-forget with a bounded local buffer — log
shipping must never block or fail the run it's reporting on. A full buffer
drops the oldest entry, not the newest, and should log (locally, stderr
only) that it dropped something, once, not per-entry.

title: logging: add a task-scoped log sink
description:
Part of #450.

Extend `internal/logging` (it already owns its on-disk format end to end —
see `docs/architecture/organisation.md`) with a task-scoped writer producing
the same `logging.Entry` JSONL shape at
`<state_dir>/logs/tasks/<task_id>/attempt-<n>.jsonl`, reusing the existing
rotation (`MaxSizeMB`/`Keep`) semantics per task directory.

`logging.Tail`, `logging.Query`, and `logging.Components` should operate on
a task's sink unchanged. No new package — this stays inside `internal/logging`
per the "no ceremonial layers" rule.

Confirm with the maintainer whether `internal/domain/workflow` importing
`internal/logging` directly is acceptable for a domain package, or whether
the domain should declare its own sink interface with `internal/app` wiring
the concrete `internal/logging` implementation in. Default to the interface
if in doubt — see `docs/architecture/organisation.md` dependency direction.

title: gate output: stop discarding it, put the real error in the park reason
description:
Part of #450.

`StageBaselineGate` in `internal/domain/workflow/implement.go` runs each
`[[repos.gate]]` command via `cmd.CombinedOutput()`, clips the output to
200 characters into a `tc.Log.Warn` call, and discards the rest. The
eventual park error (`baseline red -- %s fails and builder could not
auto-fix (status: %s)`) is built from `res.Status` alone.

Write the full `CombinedOutput()` to the task's log sink (see #451 for the
sink itself; this can land first using a plain file write if the sink isn't
ready yet, then be migrated) and put a bounded tail (~2KB, not 200 bytes) of
it into the returned error so it reaches the park reason.

Red-then-green: write a test against `StageBaselineGate` that asserts the
returned error contains gate output beyond 200 characters when the gate
command fails with a long message, confirm it fails today, then fix.

title: epic: task observability — capture and surface agent/gate output
description:
Design doc: `docs/architecture/observability.md` (this branch/PR).

## Problem

A task's real work happens in an ephemeral `archie-agent` container over
NATS. Four things currently destroy the evidence of what it did:

1. `cmd/archie-agent/main.go` logs to stderr only, and
   `internal/container/pool.go` creates containers with `AutoRemove: true` —
   the log dies with the container.
2. `StageBaselineGate` (`internal/domain/workflow/implement.go`) captures
   full gate output via `CombinedOutput()`, clips it to 200 chars into a
   `Warn` log, and discards the rest — the park reason carries only a status
   string.
3. `agentexec.Result` has no step-level transcript (tool calls, durations,
   errors).
4. `agentexec.SubjectForSystem` is documented as the return channel for
   exactly this ("log dumps, health... the daemon reads these for
   observability") but has zero publishers and zero consumers anywhere in
   the codebase.

Consequence: a task parked today with
`stage baseline: baseline red -- go build ./... fails and builder could not
auto-fix (status: parked)` and there was no way, from the dashboard or from
chat, to see the actual `go build` error — the container that had it was
already gone.

This matters beyond convenience: archied is meant to run unattended for
weeks (`CLAUDE.md` deployment model) and potentially for users other than
its original operator. A system only debuggable by someone watching
`docker ps` live doesn't meet that bar.

## Decision

NATS is the only transport this targets. `[agent] mode = "nats"` is the
supported deployment and the agent must already reach NATS to report any
stage result — a container that can't reach NATS is a distinct, narrower
failure (connectivity) than this epic addresses (a connected container's own
output being unrecoverable). No new functionality goes into the in-process
runner, which is being migrated away.

## Subtasks

See linked sub-issues.

title: webui(chat): Send button passes the click event as sendMessage's retry arg, throws and no-ops
description:
`ui/src/chat/chat.js` line 283:

```js
send.onclick = sendMessage;
```

`sendMessage(retry = null)` is assigned directly as a DOM `onclick` handler. The browser invokes `onclick` handlers with the triggering `MouseEvent` as the first argument, so every click calls `sendMessage(event)` -- the click event becomes `retry`. It's truthy and has no `.turn` property, so the very first line of the function:

```js
const text = retry?.turn.text || composer.value.trim();
```

throws `TypeError: can't access property "text", t.turn is undefined` (`t` being the minified param name) immediately, before any state changes (the disable/status-update code runs after this line). The click is silently swallowed -- no message sent, no visible error, Send just does nothing.

Reported live on carina 2026-08-09: clicking Send in the dashboard chat had no effect; browser console showed the above uncaught promise rejection at `index.js:77`.

### Fix

`send.onclick = () => sendMessage();` (matching the pattern already used for `newChat.onclick` a few lines up), so no arguments reach `sendMessage` from the click event.

title: channels: MarkRunning is never called, dashboard shows working channels stuck on 'Starting'
close_reason: MarkRunning now fires for telegram/email/webhook via a gateway.Lifecycle{Starting,Running} callback threaded through Gateway.Start: email/webhook report Running after their listener actually binds (webhook moved off ListenAndServe's internal bind to explicit net.Listen so this is observable), telegram reports Running after StartWebhook launch (webhook mode) or after the first successful getUpdates response via a pollReadinessClient http.Client wrapper (long-poll mode). Restart re-reports Starting/Running each cycle. task check clean, race-clean on the new tests.

title: daemon: label dispatch trigger with empty label matches every open issue
description:
`internal/daemon/daemon.go` `pollIssuesWithConfig()`, the `"label"` (and `"either"`) trigger branch calls:

```go
issues, err := fg.IssuesWithLabel(ctx, repo.Owner, repo.Name, cfg.Label)
```

`cfg.Label` is a top-level `Config.Label` field (`internal/config/config.go:364`) -- a different field from `[dispatch.labels]`, which maps task *states* (queued/working/waiting/pr/parked) to their forge labels for a different purpose. It's easy to configure `[dispatch.labels]` and reasonably assume the label-trigger match target is covered, while leaving the actual `label` field that controls trigger matching unset.

`GitHubClient.IssuesWithLabel` (`internal/forge/github.go:103`) passes that straight through as `Labels: []string{label}` to the GitHub issues-list API. With `label == ""`, GitHub does not filter by label at all -- it returns every open issue in the repo.

### Impact (live incident, 2026-08-09)

Deployed `dispatch.trigger = "label"` on carina without setting `label`. The daemon queued 124 unrelated open issues in one poll cycle (everything from epics to unrelated feature requests), and one reached a running agent container before it was caught and stopped manually.

### Expected

`pollIssuesWithConfig`'s `"label"` branch should refuse to poll (log an error and return, same as any other misconfiguration) when `cfg.Label` is empty, rather than silently falling through to an unfiltered API call. Ideally this is also caught at config-validation time (`internal/infrastructure/configuration/validate.go`) when `dispatch.trigger` is `"label"` or `"either"` and `label` is blank.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/label-dispatch-empty-label (31efdcf): pollIssuesWithConfig/pollEitherWithConfig now refuse the label poll when cfg.Label is empty, and validateDispatch rejects the misconfiguration at load time. Adversarially reviewed; one weak test strengthened to actually verify assignee matches survive.

title: webui(chat): dynamic header content breaks the fixed no-scroll chat layout
description:
The Chat page's layout (`ui/src/chat/chat.css`) is built for a fixed, no-scroll chat window: `.chat-workspace` uses `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto` with `overflow: hidden`, and only `.chat-transcript` (the message list) is meant to scroll. `.chat-page` only sets `min-height: calc(100vh - 5rem)`, not a fixed height.

Any dynamic content injected above `.chat-layout` -- the status/error banner (see #443), extra status pills, a long "Reload Telegram"/"Check updates" row wrapping on a narrower viewport -- has no height budget accounted for, so it just pushes the whole grid down and grows total page height past the viewport. That breaks the intended design: the page itself scrolls instead of just the transcript.

Screenshot: Chat page with the 501 error banner (see #443) visibly adding an extra row that isn't accounted for in the fixed layout.

### Expected

The top status/banner region should have a bounded height (or the page should reserve space for it) so injecting a banner or wrapping the status pills never causes page-level scroll -- only `.chat-transcript` should ever scroll.

title: webui(chat): raw 501 error banner when update-check is unconfigured
webui: Gate pulse card content should top-align with Finish setting up card
description:
On the dashboard's HEALTH section, the "Gate pulse" card doesn't visually align with the "Finish setting up" card next to it. "Finish setting up" is top-aligned (title, progress bar, checklist all stacked from the top), while "Gate pulse"'s empty-state content ("No completed runs yet" / "Once Archie finishes a task...") is vertically centered in the card, leaving large uneven whitespace above and below relative to its sibling.

Screenshot: dashboard HEALTH row, two cards side by side -- left card ("Finish setting up") content flows from the top; right card ("Gate pulse") content floats centered.

### Expected

The "Gate pulse" card's content (including its empty state) should top-align the same way "Finish setting up" does, so the two HEALTH cards read as one consistent row rather than two different layout patterns.
close_reason: Fixed in ui/src/dashboard/dashboard.css: .dash-top > div now flexes and .card grows to fill it, scoped to the HEALTH row only. Verified via a static HTML repro using the real project CSS (Playwright, computed geometry before/after) -- card heights and bottom edges now match. task check green, ui/dist rebuilt. Commit a9a056c.

title: archied: [[repos]] entries can't span more than one forge
description:
`[forge]` is a single top-level block resolved once (`resolveForge` in `cmd/archied/main.go:332`) into one `forge.Forge` client, shared by every entry in `[[repos]]`. The `Repo` struct (`internal/config/config.go:56`) has no per-repo `type`/`host`/`token` override -- `owner`/`name` are the only identity fields, so every repo is assumed to live on whatever single forge the daemon is configured for.

This blocks a `[[repos]]` list spanning more than one forge (e.g. one repo on GitHub, another on a Gitea instance) under a single archied identity. Discovered live on carina 2026-08-09: switching `[forge]` to `type = "github"` for `archie-core` made the daemon start querying the `tau` repo entry (still Gitea-hosted) against `api.github.com`, producing repeated 404s (`get repo sam/tau: GET https://api.github.com/repos/sam/tau: 404 Not Found`) until the `tau` entry was removed as a workaround.

### Expected

Each `[[repos]]` entry should be able to declare (or inherit a default) its own forge type/host/token, and the daemon should resolve a forge client per repo rather than one globally, so repos on different forges can be dispatched from the same archied instance.

### Workaround in place

`tau`'s `[[repos]]` entry was removed from carina's `config.toml` so `archie-core` (now GitHub) doesn't try to poll it against the wrong forge. `tau` gets no automated dispatch from this instance until this is fixed or it gets a separate identity.

title: fix(webui): open redirect in dashboard token-exchange handler
description:
CodeQL alert (`go/unvalidated-url-redirection`, medium severity): the dashboard token-exchange handler in `internal/webui/auth.go` redirected to a Location built directly from the incoming request's path and query, with no validation.

A request whose path starts with `//` (e.g. `GET //evil.example/x?t=<token>`) causes `clean.RequestURI()` to reproduce `//evil.example/x` verbatim. Browsers treat a Location header starting with `//` as protocol-relative, so this redirects the client off-host after a legitimate token exchange -- a classic open-redirect via the Go `net/url` double-slash gotcha.

### Fix

Added `sameOriginPath()` in `internal/webui/auth.go`, which collapses any leading `//` down to a single `/` before the value ever reaches `http.Redirect`. Covered by a red-then-green test in `internal/webui/auth_test.go` (`TestRequireToken_RedirectRejectsProtocolRelativePath`) that reproduces the exploit path and asserts the Location header is never protocol-relative.

Ref: [code-scanning alert #4](https://github.com/samcharles93/archie-core/security/code-scanning/4) (dismissed alerts #1-3 on that same scan were false positives -- allocations already bounded by `min()`, see their dismissal comments).

title: SOUL loader with per-turn reload and default fallback
description:
Load the SOUL file from the config dir into the identity slot of the rendered prompt, re-reading it per turn so an edit takes effect on the next message with no restart.

### Acceptance Criteria

SOUL content is rendered into the identity slot ahead of the invariant sections. An absent, empty or unreadable SOUL falls back to the shipped default identity rather than rendering nothing. Editing the file changes the next turn's prompt with no restart. A read error is logged once and degrades to the default; it never fails the turn. Size is bounded so an oversized SOUL cannot crowd out the rules.

title: Regression tests: Container pool — volume lifecycle, error paths, concurrent pool access
description: internal/container/pool_test.go has 3 tests (grace period, JSON output, volume file). Missing: volume cleanup on error, concurrent pool access, container timeout during task, invalid task payload handling, Docker daemon unavailable error path.

title: Surprisal sampling: embedding-backed strategies
description:
Implement the embedding-backed surprisal strategy behind the Sampler seam that wave 1 of the curator epic ships (cheap strategies: recency, random, all, staleness proxy). Surprisal scores memories by how surprising they are so the sampled reasoner's agentic budget is spent on the memories most likely to matter. DEFERRED by design: gated behind the embeddings capability (sibling issue 'Embeddings capability (prerequisite for surprisal sampling)') — pick up only after that lands.

### Acceptance Criteria

A Sampler implementation behind the same interface as the cheap strategies; selection is deterministic given fixed inputs. Algorithm: sample up to a candidate cap; build a k-NN graph over embedding vectors; row-normalize the adjacency with self-loops; power-iterate to the stationary distribution; surprisal = -log(stationary probability of the nearest point); select the highest-surprisal items. Degradation: content with no embedding is skipped; an embedding failure aborts sampling and falls back to free exploration - a sampling failure must never fail or crash a curator pass. Cost: the graph build is quadratic in the candidate cap; the cap is a named constant with a documented bound. Tests use synthetic vectors via httptest, never a live embedding service.

title: Embeddings capability (prerequisite for surprisal sampling)
description:
Surprisal-based sampling (curator epic DESIGN) requires computing vector embeddings of memory content so memories can be scored by how surprising they are. Archie has no embedding capability today; the epic gates any surprisal-style sampling behind adding one. This issue tracks that prerequisite so it can be picked up independently of the curator epic's main work. The consumer is the embedding-backed surprisal sampler (sibling issue 'Surprisal sampling: embedding-backed strategies'). Embedding consumers must degrade gracefully: content with no embedding is skipped, and an embedding failure aborts sampling in favour of free exploration rather than crashing the pass.

### Acceptance Criteria

An embedding client exists behind a narrow typed interface usable by in-process daemon components (curators first, other consumers later). Provider/model is config-driven (providers table + a role in [models]). A missing credential degrades per the credential-missing-degrades-not-fatal rule: capability reports unavailable, daemon still starts. Network calls carry timeouts; failures surface as reported errors, never a crash or a failed chat turn. Tests use httptest and never require a live embedding service.
close_reason: Closed

title: [EPIC] Curator engine: persistent memory-reasoning agent loops
description:
Introduce curators as their own engine family: long-running agent loops that reason over memory and perform small maintenance tasks, rather than one hardcoded background job. A curator is defined by a check-in interval, a tool set, and (once the memory engine family lands) an attached memory engine. It runs persistently while there is input and backs off to a cooldown when idle. Ship two reference curators -- a skill curator and a persistent-session-memory curator -- so the interface is proven against two consumers rather than designed around one.

### Design

The design splits a cheap hot-path extractor from an expensive sampled reasoner, so agentic cost is never paid per message. Sampling chooses which memories deserve attention via surprisal-based scoring, implemented over embeddings through interchangeable strategies including a k-NN graph random walk. Archie has no embedding capability today, so any surprisal-style sampling is gated behind adding one.

### Acceptance Criteria

Curator is a conforming engine family per ARCHITECTURE.md 'Plugin engine rule (strict)': typed contract, owning registry/manager, start/health/stop, narrow typed host access. Curators are registered and configured declaratively, not hardcoded. The runtime supports persistent operation under load and cooldown when idle, with intervals configurable per curator. Both reference curators run against the shipped defaults. Curator activity is observable: what ran, when, what it changed, and why. A curator failure is isolated and never takes down the daemon or a chat turn.

title: Regression tests: Yaegi extract packages smoke tests (wfextract, gateextract, pluginextract)
description: Four extract packages have zero tests: internal/workflow/wfextract, internal/gate/gateextract, internal/plugin/pluginextract, and internal/workflow/wfextract. These are Yaegi symbol extractors that generate Go source exposing package symbols to Yaegi scripts. They fail loudly at build time if broken, but minimal smoke tests would catch regressions in the export format (correct symbol names, expected types, no missing exports).

title: generalize Provider.APIKeyEnv / NATS.TokenEnv / Telegram.TokenEnv to SecretRef
description:
Follow-up to archie-core-xec, which only migrated Forge.TokenEnv (self-contained call site). Provider.APIKeyEnv is forwarded THREE different ways that all assume the secret is reachable by name in the daemon's own env, not resolved centrally:
1. agentexec.NewRuntime -> passes the env-var NAME into ai-sdk/runtime's AuthConfig.APIKeyEnv, which lazily os.Getenv's it later (external module, cannot change its contract).
2. agentexec.WorkerEnvironment / subprocess.go WorkerEnvironment() -> allowlist-forwards the NAME into a subprocess's environment for archie-agent to read itself.
3. daemon.containerEnv() -> already eagerly resolves via os.Getenv and injects NAME=value into a container env (this one generalizes cleanly).

Migrating Provider.APIKeyEnv to SecretRef requires switching cases 1 and 2 from name-forwarding to eager-resolve-via-secret.Registry-then-inject-value (ai-sdk/runtime.AuthConfig.APIKey literal field already supports this per its ResolveAPIKey fallback chain -- no ai-sdk/runtime changes needed, just stop relying on its lazy os.Getenv path for non-env engines). Also migrate NATSConfig.TokenEnv and TelegramConfig.TokenEnv (each has a single simple os.Getenv call site, lower risk than Provider).

### Design

secret.Registry must be threaded into agentexec.NewRuntime, WorkerEnvironment, and daemon.containerEnv (or a shared secret-resolution helper) so eager-resolve-then-inject replaces name-forwarding for engines other than the built-in env engine.

### Acceptance Criteria

Provider.APIKeyEnv, NATSConfig.TokenEnv, TelegramConfig.TokenEnv replaced with SecretRef; all three consumption paths (in-process runtime, subprocess worker env, container env) resolve via secret.Registry; task check passes; adversarial review finds zero surviving findings; explicit test proving a non-env engine (e.g. a fake test engine) correctly delivers a provider API key to agentexec.NewRuntime via the AuthConfig.APIKey literal field, not APIKeyEnv.

title: secret engine plugin: vault/openbao
description: Ship a yaegi-loaded secrets engine plugin talking to Vault/OpenBao's HTTP KV API (net/http), following the internal/secret Engine interface from archie-core-xec.
close_reason: Shipped vault/openbao engine plugin in examples/secret-engines/vault.go (commit 24faf53): CLI-based, VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_TOKEN, key 'path/field' or VAULT_SECRET_PATH prefix.

title: secret engine plugin: bws (Bitwarden Secrets Manager)
description: Ship a yaegi-loaded secrets engine plugin wrapping the bws CLI (os/exec), following the internal/secret Engine interface from archie-core-xec.
close_reason: Already delivered as a compiled-in engine, not a plugin. internal/secret/bws.go implements secret.Engine and shells out to the bws CLI via os/exec (commit 3ae59c9, 2026-07-31); NewRegistry/DefaultRegistry register it under the name "bws" alongside "env". It is documented in config.example.toml and ARCHITECTURE.md:208, and config.example.toml:64 uses it as the worked example. Shipping a second yaegi implementation under examples/secret-engines/ would register the same name "bws", and Registry.Register is last-write-wins over LoadDir, so the plugin would silently shadow the compiled-in engine -- two authoritative paths for one behaviour, which the architecture contract prohibits. Reopen only if the intent is to REPLACE the compiled-in engine with a plugin (which would also need bws removed from NewRegistry and the docs updated).

title: secret engine plugin: sops
description: Ship a yaegi-loaded secrets engine plugin wrapping the sops CLI (os/exec), following the internal/secret Engine interface from archie-core-xec. Lives under the shipped engines directory, loaded the same way as custom engines to prove the extension point.

title: internal/secret: secrets-engine registry with yaegi extension interface
description:
Add a secret-management package that avoids hard-coding secrets backends. Defines an Engine interface (Name, Version, Resolve(ref string) (map[string]string, error)) that custom secrets engines implement as yaegi-interpreted .go plugins, loaded the same way internal/plugin.LoadDir already loads daemon plugins (main.Engine export, resolved via yaegiutil.Resolve). Includes a built-in compiled-in 'env' engine, a Registry type, and a config.SecretRef type ({Engine, Ref string}) that directly REPLACES the existing TokenEnv/APIKeyEnv string fields across config.go (Forge, Provider, NATSConfig, TelegramConfig, etc) -- no backwards-compatibility shim, this is a clean cutover since the end user is the repo owner, not an external customer base. Ships no third-party engines yet (sops/bws/vault-openbao are follow-up beads) but proves the extension point with the env engine and a directory-loaded custom engine in tests.

### Design

Mirrors internal/plugin's Plugin interface (Name/Version) + one Resolve method. Built-in env engine is native Go (trivial, no yaegi needed) registered by default. Custom/shipped engines are yaegi .go files loaded from a configurable directory via yaegiutil.Resolve[Engine](i, src, "main.Engine").

### Acceptance Criteria

internal/secret package exists with Engine interface, Registry, LoadDir (yaegi-based, mirrors internal/plugin conventions) -- DONE. config.Forge.Token (SecretRef) replaces Forge.TokenEnv end-to-end including per-identity validation -- DONE. Provider/NATS/Telegram migration deferred to archie-core-xec.4 (scope narrowed mid-implementation after discovering the name-forwarding architecture fork). task check passes -- DONE. Adversarial review found zero surviving findings after fix pass -- DONE.

title: Discovery session: interview to produce agent personas PRD
description:
Sam has no implementation approach in mind yet for agent personas. Run a structured discovery interview (an agent grilling Sam with scoped questions, one round at a time) to extract: what a persona means concretely for this project, how it should relate to (or reuse) the existing skill/workflow system, whether personas are a prerequisite for or dependent on the multi-agent collaboration work, and what's explicitly out of scope. Write the findings up as docs/prds/agent-personas.md.

### Acceptance Criteria

docs/prds/agent-personas.md exists, reflects Sam's actual answers (not assumptions), and is detailed enough that a future implementation session could break it into scoped, dependency-ordered beads issues the way the 5zh epic was.

title: Agent personas: specialized agents for specific task types
description:
Build on multi-agent collaboration with the concept of agent personas — agents with distinct roles/specializations (e.g. a reviewer persona, a security-focused persona, a specific-language expert persona) that perform specific kinds of tasks rather than one generic agent handling everything. Related to but separable from the multi-agent collaboration epic — personas could exist for single-agent-at-a-time dispatch too (picking the right persona for a task), or become one of the participants in multi-agent collaboration.

### Acceptance Criteria

A PRD exists (docs/prds/) covering: what a persona is (system prompt variant? skill-bundle variant? separate model/config?), how a task gets routed to the right persona, how personas relate to the existing skill/workflow system (internal/skill, internal/workflow), and whether personas need to exist before or after multi-agent collaboration lands. No code changes required to close this epic — the PRD is the deliverable.

title: fix(gateway): resolve() orphans a session when it loses the double-check race
description:
CONFIRMED by execution with a blocking store decorator. sessionTracker.resolve calls sessions.Save BEFORE cacheActive, which may then discard the ID in favour of a racing caller's. The write is not rolled back.

Interleaving: goroutine A misses the cache and GetByChannel returns empty; meanwhile /new saves a UUID session and setActives it; A resumes, saves the deterministic session 'chat-y', then cacheActive returns the UUID. Store holds 2 sessions; 'chat-y' is unreachable, shows up in /sessions and /topic listings as '(untitled)', and per the newest-first bug can be silently resurrected on restart.

Applies equally to a racing /resume, /branch or /topic <id> -- the daemon genuinely runs commands on lane goroutines while submitTurn resolves on the bot worker.

Note the synchronization itself is correct: all four accesses to sessionTracker.active are guarded, and stripping the locks produces 12 race-detector reports plus an assertion failure, so the test is load-bearing. This is a logic bug inside the guarded code, not a race.

title: feat(container): pass registry auth on image pull
description:
internal/container/pool.go:305 calls p.cli.ImagePull(ctx, ref, client.ImagePullOptions{}) with RegistryAuth never set, so the daemon talks to the Docker Engine API with no credentials. Against a private registry (git.catlow.cloud) every pull answers 401 regardless of pull_policy.

docker login does NOT help: it writes ~/.docker/config.json, which only the CLI reads. The operator has to pull by hand with the CLI so the daemon's pull_policy=missing check finds the image already present. That workaround is currently documented in CLAUDE.md as a hard constraint rather than fixed.

Fix: populate ImagePullOptions.RegistryAuth with a base64-encoded registry.AuthConfig, sourced from ~/.docker/config.json or an explicit [containers] credential. Removes a documented footgun and makes pull_policy actually mean what it says against private registries.

title: infrastructure/configuration: external input boundary
description:
Read docs/architecture/configuration.md. Create internal/infrastructure/configuration as the external config input boundary. It owns TOML/YAML decoding, env and secret references, base/overlay precedence, compatibility aliases, input validation, and provenance. It must NOT own domain behaviour. Preserve current LoadOverlay behaviour exactly and keep every existing TOML field name working. Translate the decoded input into the current internal/config.Config shape at the composition boundary as an explicitly-marked temporary adapter, so runtime behaviour is unchanged. Do not migrate consumers in this bead.

### Acceptance Criteria

internal/infrastructure/configuration exists and is the loader used by cmd/archied. Old config files still load with identical effective values. task check clean. No consumer outside cmd/archied changed. The temporary adapter carries a comment naming its deletion condition.

title: SetupPrompter interface and UI-agnostic setup flow
description:
Port tau's split: setup logic lives in a package that takes a SetupPrompter interface; the command layer supplies the terminal implementation. This is what makes setup testable without a TTY.

### Acceptance Criteria

Setup logic has no direct terminal dependency and is driven end to end in tests by a fake prompter. The terminal implementation provides a numbered Select and a non-echoing ReadSecret via golang.org/x/term, both cancellable on Ctrl+C via context. No TUI framework is introduced.

title: Unify Telegram provider and model selection around SDK catalog
description:
Replace the separate /provider and static configured-model surfaces with one /model provider-to-model wizard. Build the usable provider catalog from the local ai-sdk models.dev catalog plus environment credentials and explicit overrides, cache the filtered tool-capable catalog under the active config directory, and use the same resolved provider/model state across chat and execution paths. Remove the handwritten WellKnown table and remove external-framework references from the Archie tree.

### Acceptance Criteria

/model first shows usable providers, then paginated tool-capable models, then atomically switches provider/model and reports model metadata and scope. /provider is absent from executable/menu/help surfaces. Catalog refresh is downloaded at daemon startup and cached beside configuration with safe cached fallback. Environment discovery and explicit overrides flow through chat, identities, subprocess and container/taskrun paths. Focused and composition tests cover discovery, pagination, callbacks and execution parity. A case-insensitive repository scan outside the explicit .references source tree finds no forbidden external-framework name.

title: gateway: restore /whoami /profile /sessions /resume /agents handlers
description:
These five command handlers were lost during parallel merges of the Telegram
workers. The Router fields they need (Identity, Models, Sessions, Agents)
already exist; the handlers and their Route cases do not.

18 tests in internal/gateway/gateway_test.go already specify the exact
behaviour. They are currently failing. Run them and make them pass:

  go test ./internal/gateway/...

Failing: TestRouteWhoami, TestRouteWhoamiNoIdentity, TestRouteWhoamiWithModel,
TestRouteProfile, TestRouteProfileNoIdentity, TestRouteSessionsEmpty,
TestRouteSessionsNotConfigured, TestRouteSessionsError, TestRouteResumeNoArg,

TestRouteResumeExactMatch, TestRouteAgentsEmpty, TestRouteAgentsNotConfigured,
TestRouteAgentsWithTasks, TestRouteAgentsError, TestLocalCommandsIncludesNewCommands

Scope:
- ONLY internal/gateway/. Do not touch any other package.
- Read the tests first; they define the exact reply text fragments expected
  ("not configured", "No sessions", "Usage", etc). Do not invent wording.
- Follow the shape of the existing handlers in gateway.go and
  session_commands.go: handleX methods on *Router returning (string, error).
- A nil dependency means "not configured" and returns a reply, not an error.
  A dependency that returns an error must propagate it (see TestRouteSessionsError).
- Add the new commands to the Route switch and to LocalCommands.

Constraints:
