- Do NOT write architecture docs, ledgers, plans or new beads. Just the code.
- Do NOT modify the tests to make them pass. The tests are correct.

Done when: go build ./... , go vet ./... , gofmt -l . clean, and
go test ./internal/gateway/... passes with zero failures.

title: install.sh: linger detection claims success it did not verify
description:
install.sh greps 'loginctl show-user $USER' for 'Linger=no'. When show-user fails or prints nothing -- no logind session, a container, USER unset -- the grep fails and control falls to the else branch, which prints '[OK] User linger is already enabled.' Nothing was verified and linger is never enabled, so systemd --user dies at logout. Worst for someone installing on a remote box over SSH: Archie works while they are connected and stops when they disconnect. Discussed 2026-07-30, fix agreed but not applied.

### Acceptance Criteria

Detection tests for the positive (Linger=yes) and attempts enable-linger in every other case, including when show-user fails. Uses $(id -un) rather than $USER, which is unset in some container and cron contexts and would abort under set -u. enable-linger is idempotent so a redundant call is harmless. No branch claims linger is enabled without having observed it.

title: Durable scheduled agent tasks backed by Archie's task queue
description:
Add first-class one-shot, interval, and cron scheduling for Telegram agents. The scheduler decides when work is due but never executes an LLM or shell inline: it atomically enqueues a normal durable Archie task under the originating identity, and existing workers execute it with the usual tool, sandbox, lifecycle, and observability policies. Expose typed agent tools and Telegram management surfaces for create/list/status/pause/resume/delete/run-now, with delivery back to the originating chat.

### Acceptance Criteria

Schedules support one-shot timestamps, fixed intervals, and cron expressions with explicit timezone. Definitions and execution history survive daemon restarts. Due firing uses an atomic lease/idempotency key so concurrent daemons and crash recovery do not duplicate a scheduled occurrence. Scheduler callbacks only enqueue normal tasks; they never run agents or shell commands inline. Each schedule records owner identity, origin chat/thread, prompt/task payload, enabled capability policy, overlap policy, next run, last result, and delivery state. Authorized users can create/list/status/pause/resume/delete/run-now from chat and equivalent typed agent tools. Missed-run, long-running overlap, clock/DST, cancellation, queue failure, execution failure, and delivery failure semantics are explicit and tested with a fake clock. Cron-spawned tasks cannot recursively create schedules unless explicitly authorized. Library selection is documented and does not replace Archie's durable queue semantics.

title: Daemon: process multiple tasks concurrently (max_concurrency enforcement)
description:
Daemon currently processes one task at a time (docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md Phase 2). This is the core blocker between current state and any multi-agent scaling mode — needed before container max_concurrency or same-repo concurrency can matter. Wire the daemon's dispatch loop to run N tasks in parallel, respecting a configurable max_concurrency.

### Design

internal/container/pool.go already enforces max_concurrency for container lifecycle — reuse that limit/pattern in the daemon's task dispatch rather than inventing a second concurrency control.

### Acceptance Criteria

Daemon dispatch loop runs multiple tasks concurrently up to a configured max_concurrency limit; single-task-at-a-time behavior is gone.

title: Wire secret engines into provider discovery and execution
description:
Production creates only the env registry, never loads secret-engine plugins, and Provider lacks the documented api_key SecretRef. Implement startup plugin loading, backwards-compatible provider secret references, resolved provider discovery/runtime/container propagation, tests, release, and Carina deployment.

### Acceptance Criteria

Provider api_key SecretRefs resolve through loaded engines at startup; existing api_key_env remains compatible; discovered providers, chat runtime, taskrun and containers receive resolved credentials without logging or serializing secret values; production composition tests and task check pass.

title: [BUG] find fallback reports a cancelled walk as 'no matches found'
description:
runFindGoFallback's walk callback swallows every per-entry error (returns nil to skip inaccessible entries), so the only error that can escape filepath.WalkDir is ctx.Err() from the cancellation select. The guard 'if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ctx.Err())' therefore never fires: on timeout or /stop the function falls through and returns whatever it had collected, or 'no matches found' when it had collected nothing. This is the same failure the grep exit-code bug had -- the model is told a search found nothing when the search did not finish. Behaviour predates 6d4e0be; the errors.Is autofix in that commit is behaviour-neutral here (errors.Is(err, nil) is false for non-nil err, matching the old err != ctx.Err() when the context is live).

### Acceptance Criteria

A find whose context is cancelled mid-walk returns an error result naming the cancellation, not 'no matches found' and not a silently partial list. Regression test in the style of TestGrepReportsSearchFailureRatherThanNoMatches.

title: Reconcile SOUL with PersonaRegistry and the six built-in personas
description:
Decide what happens to DefaultPersonas() (archie, helpful, concise, technical, creative, teacher) and the /personality command once SOUL owns identity. Options: SOUL replaces the default archie persona and the rest remain selectable style modifiers; or personas become seed templates a user copies into their SOUL; or personas are retired. Currently GetActive composes the baseline archie prompt with the selected persona, so the interaction with SOUL must be explicit rather than emergent.

### Acceptance Criteria

Precedence between SOUL and a selected persona is defined and documented. /personality either keeps working with stated semantics or is removed deliberately. No path lets a persona selection blank out the user's SOUL without them asking.
notes: Not resolved yet. docs/architecture/identity.md (Three-layer identity model, agreed 2026-07-30) documents SOUL as Layer 2 and explains why SOUL comes first, but does not state the specific precedence rule between SOUL and a /personality selection that this issue's acceptance criteria requires. /personality is still fully live and unmodified: internal/channels/telegram/personality.go, internal/gateway/gateway.go:375,472,507. DefaultPersonas() still lives in internal/gateway/persona.go with no SOUL reference. This is a real open design decision, not a documentation-only task -- read docs/architecture/identity.md's three-layer model first, then decide (and document) precedence.

title: Chat: real system prompt template for Archie (identity, tools, env)
description:
The chat agent's system prompt is the four-sentence static string in gateway.DefaultPersonas(). It carries no tool inventory, no environment/date block, and no instruction precedence, so the model invents its own capabilities -- it told Sam it 'only has the memory editing tool' and then offered to walk him through installing software it cannot install.

Take the shape from tau: /work/apps/tau/internal/agent/templates/agent.md.tpl renders an agent body plus <tools>, <guidelines>, <project_context> and <env> blocks, and /work/apps/tau/internal/agent/spec/templates/tau.agent.md supplies identity, instruction precedence, core rules, communication rules and confirmation boundaries.

Keep the existing PersonaRegistry as the style layer; the template is the substrate it renders into.

title: Fix forge test fakes after adding LinkBranch
description:
The forge.Forge interface gained LinkBranch, but several hand-written test doubles were not updated.

Affected fakes include stubForge, prCapturingForge, testForge, and fakeForge. This caused go vet ./... and go test ./... to fail because the test doubles no longer satisfied forge.Forge.

Acceptance criteria:
- All forge test doubles implement the current forge.Forge interface.
- go vet ./... passes.
- go test ./... passes.

title: Decide and implement the TOML write strategy
description:
Settle how setup persists config before any prompting code is written; everything else depends on it. BurntSushi/toml loses comments on re-marshal, and config.example.toml carries substantial inline documentation users are meant to read and edit by hand. Options: (a) generate a fresh commented config from a template on first run and only line-patch specific keys on re-run; (b) full re-marshal and accept losing comments; (c) adopt a comment-preserving TOML editor.

### Design

Decision: text-based line patching, not decode/re-marshal, not a comment-preserving TOML AST library (none exist for Go that are safe to depend on).

New package internal/infrastructure/configuration/tomlwrite:
- Apply(src []byte, edits []Edit) ([]byte, error): for each {Table, Key, Value} edit, finds an active "key = value" line in that table and replaces just the value (preserving indent + trailing inline comment); else finds a commented "# key = value" line in that table, uncomments the table header and the line; else appends the key at the end of the table's content (or appends a brand new [table] section at EOF if the table doesn't exist at all, active or commented). Lines not named by an edit are copied through byte-for-byte.
- Generate(template, edits) is Apply against configtemplate.Example (config.example.toml embedded at the module root via configtemplate.go, since go:embed can't reach outside its own directory tree -- this keeps config.example.toml the single source of truth instead of a second copy, which is exactly the drift bug this epic exists to fix).
- Value callers pre-render TOML literals; String() and Ref(engine,key) helpers cover the two shapes setup needs (quoted strings, secret.SecretRef inline tables). Deliberately does not import internal/secret -- it edits text, not Go values.

Trade-off: only understands single-line scalar/inline-table values. Does not handle multi-line arrays or [[array-of-tables]] (e.g. [[repos]]) -- those aren't setup's targets and must not be routed through this patcher.

Tests (internal/infrastructure/configuration/tomlwrite/tomlwrite_test.go) cover: active-key replace preserving trailing comment, active inline-table replace, commented-table uncomment-one-key-leave-siblings-commented, append into existing active table, append brand-new table, byte-identical-elsewhere on a single edit, byte-identical-elsewhere across two sequential runs (the rs9 acceptance criterion), and a full run against the real config.example.toml verified to decode via BurntSushi/toml and round-trip bot_user/forge.token correctly.

`go build ./...` and `task check` pass clean; no other files touched.

### Acceptance Criteria

The chosen strategy is documented with its trade-off. A first run produces a config a human can read and hand-edit afterwards. A second run changing one value leaves every other line, including comments, byte-identical -- asserted by a test. No strategy is adopted that silently discards user edits.

title: Telegram: report installed gateway and runtime versions
description: Add an authorized /version command as the installed-version prerequisite for component-aware /update. Telegram remains presentation-only; the composition root supplies installed component versions.

title: Telegram: component-aware /update with approve or defer
description:
Add an /update control flow that checks for available releases, presents separate archied gateway and archie-agent runtime versions/changelog sections, and lets an authorized user approve or defer. Keep discovery and execution behind typed interfaces so Docker/Watchtower, package-manager, and other installations can supply their own updater without the Telegram gateway assuming a deployment mechanism.

### Acceptance Criteria

/update reports whether gateway and runtime updates are available, with separate version and changelog sections and explicit no-change wording. Telegram provides Approve and Defer actions restricted to authorized users. Deferral is persisted and suppresses repeated prompts according to an explicit policy. Approval calls a typed installation updater and reports progress/failure without claiming success early. No Watchtower-only or Docker-only behavior exists in the gateway package. Commands, menu, help, callback authorization, concurrency, persistence, and failure paths are tested.

title: fix(memory): startup accepted an unusable memory directory
description:
cmd/archied/main.go builds the builtin memory provider at filepath.Join(cfg.WorkDir, "memory") and logs 'memory manager started' regardless of whether that path exists or is writable. builtin.NewStore treats ENOENT as an empty document and Reload does the same, so a missing directory is indistinguishable from a memory with nothing in it yet.

Found live: carina's config was copied to the laptop with work_dir = /var/lib/archie/work, a container path that does not exist here. archied logged 'memory manager started dir=/var/lib/archie/work/memory' and ran with no memory at all. The failure would only have surfaced at the agent's first memory write, when writeFileAtomic's MkdirAll hit EACCES on /var/lib -- mid-conversation, as a tool error, after startup said it was fine.

Fixed: builtin.New now does MkdirAll(cfg.Dir) and returns an error the operator can act on, so an unusable path fails at startup where the existing error path already exits non-zero. New's doc claimed 'the provider is ready for use as soon as New returns'; it now is.

title: Audit archie-core repo for bugs/improvements, file as Gitea issues
description: Fan out exploration subagents across internal/ subsystems to find bugs, tech debt, and enhancement opportunities. Each confirmed finding gets filed as a Gitea issue on git.catlow.cloud/sam/archie-core.

title: Curator contract, registry, and internal/curator package
description:
Stand up internal/curator as a package in its own right: the typed curator contract, the owning registry that controls registration and discovery, and the definition of a curator's declared shape (check-in interval, tool set, attached memory engine).

### Acceptance Criteria

internal/curator owns a typed contract exposing real curator operations plus start/health/stop. A registry controls registration, discovery, and shutdown ordering, and defines failure isolation. Curators receive a narrow typed registrar and only the host services their declared capability requires -- never *daemon.Daemon or an untyped hook map. internal/plugin/architecture_test.go recognises curator as a conforming engine family.
close_reason: Complete: internal/domain/curator (contract.go, registry.go, registrar.go) already satisfies every acceptance criterion. CuratorEngine is a typed contract with Name/Version/Manifest/Check/Pass/Bind plus embedded Lifecycle (start/health/stop). Registry (registry.go) controls Register/Start/Health/Stop with dependency-free single ownership, panic-isolated safeCheck/safePass/bindSafely. Registrar (registrar.go) is narrow and fully typed (LLMRunner, ToolBuilder, SkillStore, EventSink, Clock) -- no *daemon.Daemon, no untyped hook map, confirmed by grep. go test ./internal/plugin/... -run TestEveryEngineInterfaceHasTypedCapabilityAndFamilyOwner -v shows domain/curator.CuratorEngine PASS as a recognised conforming engine family. go test ./internal/domain/curator/... -race -count=1 is fully green. Note: package lives at internal/domain/curator (per the domain migration), not literally internal/curator as the title says -- that's the current architecture, not a gap.

title: Telegram: remove task approval from the public command surface
description:
Existing /approve [identity=name] <task-id> was inherited as chat-task lifecycle control, but Sam explicitly states task approvals are not a product requirement. Reserve /approve exclusively for dangerous-command approval. Remove task approval from Telegram command menu/help/router/public UX; retain or remove internal waiting_human task mechanics only after verifying workflow callers. Do not repurpose the command until the dangerous-command approval model (archie-core-alm.6) exists.

### Acceptance Criteria

Telegram no longer advertises or accepts task approval via /approve; no documentation/help describes task approvals; task lifecycle code is not broken for existing non-Telegram workflow paths; /approve remains unclaimed or is implemented only for the approved dangerous-command design.

title: chat: mid-conversation context loss, undiagnosed
description:
Reported from a real Telegram transcript (29 Jul, ~09:47 AEST / 23:47 UTC 28
Jul). Turn 3 of a coherent conversation was answered with a fresh greeting as
though no history existed; turn 4 was coherent again.

Ruled out by evidence:
- Not two processes racing the bot token. docker compose ps on carina shows a
  single archied container.
- Not a restart. That container had 43h uptime spanning the whole exchange.
- Not history compression. DefaultCompressionConfig protects the first 3 and
  last 20 messages and triggers at 50% of a 128k window; there were three
  messages.
- Not a canned greeting. No such string exists in the codebase, so the reply
  was model-generated from little or no history.
- Not the session-key namespace split fixed in 96ab167: the deployed image
  predates the session lifecycle commands entirely.

Blocked on evidence, now unblocked: chat turns were completely unlogged (76
log lines covered two days, none a conversation). 96ab167 adds a "chat turn"
log line carrying session id, channel, thread and history depth.

Next step when it recurs: check the chat turn log for that message. A session
id differing from neighbouring turns points at key resolution (e.g. ThreadID
appearing on one message); history_messages of 0 or 1 with a stable session id
points at the store read path.

Do not close this by guessing. It needs one reproduction with the new log line.
close_reason: Confirmed fixed by Sam; no longer reproducible

title: Flaky: TestRunTaskExecutesBootstrapWorkflowEndToEnd races on NATS responders
description: cmd/archie-agent. Intermittently fails with ParkReason 'stage prepare: archie.worktree.prepare: nats: no responders available for request'; passes on re-run (-count=3 clean). The test does not wait for the worktreerpc subscription to be established before dispatching. A flaky test in task check is poison: it trains everyone to re-run instead of read, which is how a real regression gets waved through.

title: Bind curators to memory engines
description:
Wire the attached-memory-engine part of a curator's declared shape once the memory engine family exists, so a curator reads and writes through the engine contract rather than a concrete store.

### Acceptance Criteria

A curator declares which memory engine it uses and receives it as a typed dependency. Swapping the configured engine changes where a curator's memories land with no change to the curator. A curator with no declared memory engine is a valid configuration and is rejected only if it attempts a memory operation.
notes: Blocked on its own stated prerequisite, which is also still open: archie-core-1786637490069-11-e245c170 (Memory engine contract and owning registry). Current state: Manifest.MemoryEngine (internal/domain/curator/contract.go:59-63) is only a declared string name; Registrar (registrar.go) has no memory-engine field at all, so nothing actually binds an engine instance to a curator yet -- registry.go:128's agentic() check only tests MemoryEngine != "", it doesn't inject anything. Do not start this until the memory engine contract exists; there is nothing to bind to yet.
close_reason:
Complete, all three AC clauses:

- A curator declares its memory engine via Manifest.MemoryEngine and
  receives it as a typed dependency: curator.Registrar.MemoryEngines
  (Get(name) (domainmemory.MemoryEngine, bool)), same trust model as
  ToolBuilder.Build(ctx, declared) -- the curator calls Get with its own
  declared name, not handed a pre-resolved instance. Registration
  enforces presence exactly like Tools/Skills: declared with no
  MemoryEngineSource on the host is rejected at Register
  (TestRegistryDeclaredCapabilitiesRequireHostServices' two new cases),
  and filter() clears the field from a curator's view when undeclared
  (TestRegistryBindFiltersToDeclaredCapabilities).
- Swapping the configured engine changes where memories land with no
  curator code change: nothing about a curator names a concrete engine,
  only the string it declared, resolved fresh through whichever registry
  it was bound to.
- A curator with no declared engine stays valid (pre-existing behavior,
  now covered by table cases) and can only ever be affected by a memory
  operation it structurally cannot attempt, since MemoryEngines is nil
  in its view.

Wired end to end: internal/app/archied/bootstrap.go:setupCurators passes
b.memEngines (*domainmemory.Registry, set by setupMemoryAll which Run()
calls before setupCurators) straight in -- it already satisfies
MemoryEngineSource with no adapter.

go test ./... is green; task lint is 0 issues.

title: Consolidate duplicated NATS RPC client/server boilerplate
description: internal/storerpc/storerpc.go, internal/worktreerpc/worktreerpc.go, internal/forgerpc/forgerpc.go each reimplement near-identical timeout/marshal/error-envelope helpers for NATS request/reply RPC. Extract shared helpers into a common package.

title: infrastructure/eventbus/nats: relocate NATS transport
description:
Create internal/infrastructure/eventbus/nats as a properly structured replacement for internal/nats. This is NOT a mechanical move: the existing code has no interfaces, leaks vendor types (Conn() *nats.Conn, PublishMsg(*nats.Msg), Fetch() jetstream.Msg) into all four consumers, uses a 7-positional-parameter publish with stringly-typed comma-separated labels, stores an unused logger, returns (nil, nil) for 'no message', and hardcodes stream/consumer/timeout config. Rebuild it with: separate files per concern; a Message wrapper so jetstream types stop crossing the boundary; Publisher/Consumer interfaces; a Config struct; sentinel errors; consistent %w wrapping; real logging. Then update cmd/archied, cmd/archie-agent, internal/daemon and internal/agentexec to the new API.

### Acceptance Criteria

internal/nats no longer exists; internal/infrastructure/eventbus/nats has its contents. All imports updated. task check clean. Container and NATS behaviour unchanged.

title: fix(nell): counters squat on the SDK-reserved meta: prefix, blocking all writes after restart
description:
TOTAL OUTAGE. No task can be queued and no event recorded; survives restarts.

internal/nell/adapter.go:946,952 store auto-increment counters at meta:task_id_counter and meta:event_id_counter. The NellDB SDK reserves the meta: prefix for its own bookkeeping (sdk/replicate.go:841 isInternalID = id[:5]=="meta:").

DocDB.reindex() skips internal ids when rebuilding the in-memory rev cache (sdk/docdb.go:128-137), but the record stays in the log. So after a restart Get returns the counter doc WITH its _rev while d.revs has no entry, and putIn rejects exactly that: 'incomingRev != "" && !exists' -> ErrConflict (sdk/docdb.go:213-217). Permanent.

Hits nextTaskID (every EnqueueIssue) and nextEventID (every InsertEvent). processNATSTask Naks on error so NATS redelivers forever.

Reproduced: internal/nell/counter_repro_test.go - open, insert, close, reopen, insert -> ErrConflict in 7ms with no daemon/NATS/forge.

SECOND DEFECT: isInternalID exists to exclude records from replication, so the two carina instances never converge their counters and would allocate COLLIDING task IDs. Masked only because allocation currently fails outright.

FIX: move the keys out of the reserved namespace (counter:task_id / counter:event_id) AND migrate on open - the old doc is readable (only Put fails), and its next_id is load-bearing because restarting at 1 would reissue live task IDs. Also teach isMetaKey (adapter.go:803) to skip the new prefix so scans do not parse a counter as a task.

REJECTED: stripping _rev before Put is one line and works, but leaves the prefix squat, leaves counters unreplicated, and turns a loud failure into silent last-write-wins.

Full writeup: docs/incident-nelldb-counter-conflict.md

title: Simplify Telegram model command surface
description: Remove the redundant /models command from Telegram's published and executable command surface; retain /model selector. Make /help menu copy useful rather than self-referential.

title: Consolidate 6 duplicated Yaegi interpreter bootstraps
description: internal/gate/gateeval/yaegi.go, internal/workflow/wfeval/yaegi.go, internal/workflow/skillbuild/skillbuild.go, internal/skillscript/yaegi.go, internal/plugin/plugin.go, internal/skill/plugin.go each hand-roll interp.New/i.Use(stdlib.Symbols)/panic-recovery. Extract a shared helper (new package, e.g. internal/yaegiutil) for interpreter construction + panic-safe eval, used by all six.

title: Ship the file-writing store as the default memory engine
description:
Reframe internal/memory/builtin as the reference engine implementation behind the new contract, so the standard install keeps writing memories to files with no configuration and no behaviour change.

### Acceptance Criteria

The builtin store implements the engine contract and registers as the default. A config that names no memory engine behaves exactly as today, verified by existing internal/memory tests continuing to pass unmodified where they assert behaviour rather than structure. Its lifecycle methods are real or explicit no-ops, not stubs that silently do nothing surprising.
notes:
Engine implementation done: internal/infrastructure/memory.BuiltinEngine
implements domain/memory.MemoryEngine over internal/memory/builtin.Store
(one per identity), fully tested including registering/running through
domain/memory.Registry. internal/memory/builtin itself is untouched, its
own tests pass unmodified.

NOT done: not wired into daemon bootstrap, and nothing selects it as
"the default" at runtime yet -- that depends on the config surface
(archie-core-1786637490043) landing first, since there's no config field
to resolve "unconfigured" to this engine until then. Leaving open rather
than closing on a partial AC match; will close once bootstrap wiring
makes it the actual running default.
close_reason:
Complete: cfg.Memory.Engine now actually selects and starts an engine at
daemon boot, not just implements the contract in isolation.

internal/app/archied/bootstrap.go:setupMemoryEngine builds a
domain/memory.Registry, registers infraMemory.BuiltinEngine for
cfg.Memory.Engine == "builtin" or "" (matching applyMemoryDefaults'
resolution, so unconfigured and explicitly-builtin behave identically),
starts it, and stops it on shutdown -- rooted at workDir/memory-engine,
separate from the legacy provider's workDir/memory so the two can never
collide while both exist. Wired into Run() via setupMemoryAll
(archie-core-1786637490043's cfg.Memory.Engine validation runs first at
config load, so the switch's default case only guards drift between
that list and this one, not live operator input).

internal/memory/builtin is unchanged (verified: no diff, its tests pass
unmodified) and internal/memory.Manager (the live system-prompt/tool-call
path) does not read through this registry -- the two systems run in
parallel by design, per archie-core-1786637490069-11-e245c170's explicit
scoping. Converging them is future work, not part of this issue's AC.

go test ./... is green; task lint is 0 issues.

title: fix(gateway): assorted confirmed defects around the compress and undo paths
description:
Small, individually confirmed, none blocking on their own:

1. session_commands.go:563 -- the compression summary is persisted as a USER turn. CompressHistory emits it with Role 'system' (compression.go:118) but the write-back only maps 'assistant' -> Identity, so system falls through to 'user'. The model replays '[Earlier conversation has been summarised...]' as if the human said it. (Retained bot turns are handled correctly.)

2. session_commands.go:488 -- compressPreview reads RecentMessages(200) while reporting count from MessageCount. With 100 large + 250 tiny messages the preview says 'Compression not needed (350 messages, ~0 tokens)' while apply on the same session reports '350 -> 24 (~100000 -> ~3063 tokens)'. The two numbers in one sentence describe different histories, and the preview advises against a compression that is needed.

3. session_commands.go:329 -- handleUndo discards the deleted count from DeleteRecentMessages, so /undo 10 failing after 6 removals reports failure while six messages are gone.

4. session_store.go:626 -- nextTimestamp has no upper bound and lastTimestamp re-reads from the store, so one future-dated write (host clock 24h fast) pins the session's clock for its lifetime; every later At handed to callers is wrong by a day.

5. session_store.go:268 -- Close() calls s.store.Close() on the SHARED nl.Store (in production the daemon's tasks/events log) and, unlike every other method, does not take s.mu. Nothing calls it today.

6. session_store.go:429 -- newMessageID's UUIDv5 input sessionID+"\x00"+sourceID is not injectively encoded: newMessageID('a\x00b','c') == newMessageID('a','b\x00c'). No reachable input today; hardening, not a live bug.

7. turns.go:79-85 -- Turns.lanes grows without bound; a lane is inserted per session key and never deleted. No goroutine leak.

title: fix(gateway): doc comments contradict the implementation in three places
description:
Each of these actively misleads, and one already caused a real bug:

1. gateway.go:23-27 says MessageID is 'Populated on read; ignored on write.' Both stores honour an incoming MessageID in preference to deriving one (session_store.go:588, session_store_sqlite.go:291). This is exactly the misreading behind /branch copying parent history into the child under the PARENT's canonical IDs -- CONFIRMED on both backends, and newMessageID's own doc claims the opposite ('the same upstream message copied into a branch gets its own identity'). Two branches from one parent produce three sessions holding the same MessageID.

2. session_store.go:405-409 describes msgID and a disambiguating counter, both deleted in this commit, and now sits above messageIDNamespace describing the opposite of the current design.

3. telegram.go:474-477 still says a redelivered update 'updates the stored turn' -- the exact behaviour the immutability fix removed.

title: NATS transport: JetStream task queue + request-reply between daemon and archie-agent
description:
Phase 1 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. internal/events.Bus (in-process pub/sub, already feeding SQLite + SSE) is the natural seam to replace the transport under. Daemon publishes tasks, archie-agent consumes, results return via NATS. Preserve current inprocess mode via [agent] mode default for local dev.

### Design

Add optional [nats] config block (url, token_env), default anonymous auth for single-node, credentials required for multi-node per PRD sec.9 open question 2.

### Acceptance Criteria

Daemon can dispatch a task to archie-agent over NATS JetStream and receive results via request-reply; inprocess mode still works unchanged.

title: One optional MCP provider failing takes down the whole daemon
description:
internal/tools/provider/provider.go Start() is atomic by design -- 'Any failure rolls the complete family back' -- so a single failing provider unregisters every other provider including the builtins, capabilityHost.Start returns the error, and cmd/archied/main.go:655 exits 1. Under compose restart or systemd Restart=on-failure that is a crash loop. Observed 2026-07-30 on carina: mcp.desktop-commander could not start (missing unzip in the runtime image, fixed in 455fd6f) and archied restarted continuously, losing chat, the gateway and every builtin tool over one third-party npm package.\n\nAtomicity is correct for a provider the daemon requires. It is wrong for an external MCP server pulled from a registry at runtime, which is exactly the category that should be allowed to be absent -- the same reasoning applied to the forge in 518a1a0, where a missing credential now disables the capability rather than the daemon.

### Design

Needs a required/optional distinction on the registration or manifest, which does not exist today. Keep the all-or-nothing path for required providers; the atomic batch semantics for tool visibility (tools appear only after Start and Discover both succeed) should hold per-provider either way. Relates to the plugin engine rule in ARCHITECTURE.md: failure isolation is explicitly the owning manager's responsibility.

### Acceptance Criteria

A provider can be declared optional. An optional provider that fails to start or discover is logged, excluded from the running set, and does not roll back the family or stop the daemon. A required provider keeps today's atomic rollback. Provider health reflects the degraded state so the failure is visible rather than silent. Regression test starts a family containing one failing optional provider and asserts the other providers' tools remain registered and Start returns nil.

title: Telegram: separate task status from chat runtime status
description:
Split Telegram task and runtime status into distinct commands. MVP from Sam:

/tasks:
- command name is exactly /tasks
- show only when running tasks exist; when none are running, explain how to set up workflows for continuous development
- let the user select a running task by its description/title; first verify task records actually carry usable titles/descriptions, otherwise treat that as a blocker

/status:
- show session details
- show configured provider
- show configured model
- show installed plugins
- Hermes-style session metadata is the reference direction; exact fields can expand later

Do not mix task state into /status.

### Acceptance Criteria

/tasks is the sole task-status command; it lists selectable running tasks by usable title/description, or gives workflow setup guidance when none run; implementation is blocked/escalated if task records lack usable titles. /status reports only chat/runtime state: session details, configured provider, configured model, and installed plugins. Task and runtime outputs do not mix. Telegram menu/help/executable parity and tests cover both commands.

title: Spawned archie-agent containers not on daemon's docker network — can't reach NATS
description: Root cause of 'agent still failing on the server': archied's container.Pool.Acquire creates archie-agent containers via the Docker SDK with no NetworkMode set, so Docker attaches them to the default bridge network. archied and nats run on the compose-created 'archie-core_default' network instead, so the spawned container's hostname resolution for 'nats' (from NATS_URL=nats://nats:4222) fails and archie-agent can't connect. Confirmed on carina host logs: archied logs show repeating 'taskrun request failed err="nats: no responders available for request"' for every task, containers created and destroyed within ~1.5s (consistent with archie-agent's NATS client failing fast). Fixed by detecting the daemon's own container's network in NewPool (selfNetwork, via ContainerInspect on os.Hostname()) and setting HostConfig.NetworkMode on spawned containers to match.

title: fix(gateway): /topic off poisons the tracker cache with an empty session ID
description:
CONFIRMED by execution. handleTopic (session_commands.go:200) 'off' does setActive(chan, "", getActive(chan, threadID)). With no session cached for (chan, threadID), getActive returns "" and that empty string is stored. resolve treats map presence as authoritative ('id, ok := t.active[key]; if ok { return id }'), and cacheActive also returns the empty existing value, so nothing can repair it.

Reachable when /topic off is the first message on the webhook (webhook.go:169) or email (email.go:207) channel -- both call router.Route directly and never call ResolveSessionKey first, unlike telegram's submitTurn.

Blast radius: every later message in that chat persists under session ID "", history is shared with any other poisoned chat, and the turn-lane key becomes "" so /stop in one chat kills a turn in another.

Same line is also non-atomic: setActive(...getActive(...)) is two critical sections, so a concurrent /resume or /branch is silently clobbered.

title: Persistent volumes with TTL for container/worktree storage
description:
Phase 2 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. Current worktree lifecycle is fresh-clone-per-task with status-driven cleanup, no TTL. Add persistent volume support with TTL-based expiry to avoid repeated full clones for repeated work on the same repo.

### Acceptance Criteria

Container/worktree storage can persist across tasks for the same repo up to a configured TTL, with automatic cleanup after expiry.

title: feat(webui): logs section - filterable, live-tailing
description: There is no way to see archied's logs outside journalctl. Every event already flows through events.Bus into the store and out over SSE, so this is mostly presentation over existing data. Filterable by level and component, live-tailing the SSE stream, with history from the store for anything before the dashboard connected.

title: Regression tests: NATS RPC — request timeout, reply routing, error propagation
description: internal/natsrpc/natsrpc.go has only 1 test (envelope round trip). Missing: request timeout handling, reply-to routing correctness, error propagation through the envelope, concurrent request isolation, reconnection behavior.

title: Audit the remaining golangci-lint autofix changes in 6d4e0be
description:
Commit 6d4e0be applied a golangci-lint --fix batch across 8 files. One of the eight was a behaviour regression: the errorlint fix in internal/tools/builtin/grep.go rewrote 'if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1' into 'errors.As(err, &exitErr)' and dropped the exit-code check, so any ripgrep failure (bad pattern, unreadable path) was reported to the model as 'no matches found' -- the agent would state a file contains nothing on the strength of a search that never ran. Fixed in 782510d. The other seven changes were eyeballed as benign (naked return expanded, err != ctx.Err() -> errors.Is) but were never verified individually. A one-in-eight regression rate does not justify trusting the remainder on inspection alone.

### Acceptance Criteria

Each remaining changed hunk in 6d4e0be is reviewed against its pre-fix behaviour, specifically for predicates that were narrowed or widened. internal/channels/telegram/model.go, internal/infrastructure/configuration/discovery.go, internal/tools/builtin/find.go, internal/tools/builtin/shell.go and the touched test files are covered. Any behaviour change found gets a regression test in the style of TestGrepReportsSearchFailureRatherThanNoMatches.

title: Skill curator (reference implementation)
description:
Ship a curator that maintains Archie's skills: reviewing, pruning, and improving skill definitions over time. One of the two consumers that validate the curator contract is general enough.

### Acceptance Criteria

Registers and runs through the curator registry with no curator-specific special-casing in the runtime. Its changes to skills are observable and attributable to the curator. It operates within its declared tool set and cannot reach tools it did not declare.
close_reason:
Complete, all three AC clauses. Design decided first in
docs/prds/skill-curator.md (no settled design existed for what "review,
prune, improve" means as concrete behavior): v1 is mechanical validation
plus safe whitespace normalization only -- no LLM-authored rewrites, no
deletion. See the doc for the full "why this scope, not more" reasoning.

- Registers and runs through curator.Registry with no curator-specific
  special-casing: uses the existing Register/Runtime path unchanged
  (TestRegistersAndRunsThroughTheRegistry).
- Its changes are observable and attributable: every write is preceded
  by an Action naming what changed and why (skill.normalized), surfaced
  through the existing curator activity tracker
  (archie-core-1786637489932, already shipped) -- no new observability
  surface needed.
- Operates within its declared tool set: Manifest.Tools is empty, and
  nothing in the implementation ever touches Registrar.Tools
  (TestManifestDeclaresOnlySkills).

internal/infrastructure/skillcurator/{store,skillcurator}.go implement
curator.SkillStore and curator.CuratorEngine. The store deliberately does
not delegate to internal/skill.Discover, which aborts its whole call on
any one skill's parse failure -- wrong for "review each skill
independently" (TestPassReviewsEverySkillIndependently covers the
regression this would otherwise cause). Wired into
internal/app/archied/bootstrap.go:setupCurators, rooted the same way
loadWorkflows resolves skillsBase.

task check is green (full Go suite + dashboard tests).

title: fix(gateway): redelivery dedups the stored turn but still re-runs the model
description:
archie-core-963 made SaveMessage idempotent, but nothing upstream consults the result. cmd/archied/telegram_setup.go:158 respond() calls SaveMessage (now a no-op on redelivery) then unconditionally loads history, calls the model, and saves the reply -- which carries no SourceID, so it always gets a fresh random ID and always appends.

CONFIRMED at store level on both backends: redelivering tg-1 leaves [ping, pong, pong], plus a second billed model turn with any tool side effects executed twice.

The bead's stated problem ('a re-delivered Telegram update appends a duplicate turn') is half fixed. SaveMessage returns no already-seen signal for the caller to act on.

title: [EPIC] Pluggable memory engine: typed family + external providers
description:
Make the memory subsystem a pluggable engine family so an external memory backend (Honcho, or a future alternative) can be bolted on without touching the agent loop, while the file-writing store ships as the default. internal/memory already has a Manager and lifecycle hooks (TurnStartHook, SessionEndHook, SessionSwitchHook); this epic promotes that into a conforming engine family per the strict plugin engine rule in ARCHITECTURE.md rather than inventing a parallel abstraction.

### Design

Constraint from the plugin engine rule: 'engine' requires a typed domain contract, an owning Registry or Manager, explicit lifecycle/health, and narrow typed registrars -- providers never receive *daemon.Daemon or untyped hook maps. The contract must express real memory operations (write observation, query, list, forget), not just Name/Version.

### Acceptance Criteria

Memory is a typed engine family with an owning registry/manager, start/health/stop lifecycle, and narrow typed host access, satisfying every invariant in ARCHITECTURE.md 'Plugin engine rule (strict)' and passing internal/plugin/architecture_test.go. The builtin file-writing store is the shipped default engine and remains the behaviour when nothing is configured. At least one external engine is implementable against the contract without changes to the agent loop or gateway. Engine selection and per-engine settings are configurable, validated, and documented. Failure of a non-default engine degrades to a reported error rather than taking down a turn.

title: Quiet autonomous execution and correct forge linkage
description:
Reduce Archie forge noise and make issue/branch/PR lifecycle authoritative. Automatic plan/progress/retry/state-label comments must be disabled; human decisions must remain available through messaging and the Web UI; pushed task branches must be linked to their source issues through the forge API before PR creation.

### Acceptance Criteria

No automatic plan/progress/retry/state-label comments are emitted; configured human decisions remain actionable through messaging or Web UI; the source issue has a forge branch link after push; PR creation does not rely on a comment or closing directive for linkage; focused tests cover both in-process and RPC forge paths.

title: Persistent session-memory curator (reference implementation)
description:
Ship a curator that maintains durable memory across sessions -- extracting and consolidating what is worth keeping from conversation history into the attached memory engine. The second contract consumer, and the one that exercises the curator/memory-engine binding.

### Acceptance Criteria

Registers and runs through the registry with no special-casing. Writes through the memory engine contract rather than any concrete store. Extraction runs off the hot path so a chat turn never waits on it. What it wrote and why is inspectable. Honours the trigger-accounting invariant so its own writes do not reschedule it.
close_reason:
Complete, all four AC clauses. Design decided first in
docs/prds/session-memory-curator.md, most notably: Observation.Identity
is the session ID, not a user/cross-session identity -- migration-
decisions.md#5's memory-scope mapping is still explicitly open and this
issue has no business deciding it unilaterally.

- Registers and runs through curator.Registry with no special-casing

- Writes through the memory engine contract, never a concrete store:

- Honours the trigger-accounting invariant: Manifest.OnInput = true

Wired end to end: internal/app/archied/bootstrap.go:setupCurators,

Concurrent agents on the same repo are blocked by default (worktree conflict). title: config.example.toml has no token_env placeholder under [chat.telegram]

An operator reading the example file to learn what's configurable would not discover this key exists.

Discovered while implementing archie-core-rs9 and testing tomlwrite.Apply against the real template: setting chat.telegram.token_env for the first time falls through to Apply's "key not found in table" path (uncomment header, append key), which works fine -- this is a documentation completeness gap in the template, not a functional blocker for archie-core-cbk.

### Acceptance Criteria

Add a commented `# token_env = "..."` line (with a short comment on what it should point to, e.g. an env var containing the @BotFather token) under the commented [chat.telegram] block in config.example.toml, matching the style of the other commented-out optional fields.

title: Export configuration.Validate for archied setup to call
description:
The ewk epic's acceptance criteria (and archie-core-cbk's, by inheritance) require: "Every config it writes passes configuration.Validate, verified by a test that runs setup non-interactively and validates the output." That identifier does not exist. internal/infrastructure/configuration/validate.go defines only an unexported validate(cfg *config.Config) error, called from one place: loader.go:178 inside Loader.Load's own decode-then-validate sequence. There is no way for code outside the configuration package -- e.g. `archied setup` after it builds a config.Config in memory but before writing it to disk -- to run the same validation.

Discovered while implementing archie-core-rs9 (TOML write strategy). Not fixed there: rs9's scope was the text-patching mechanism, not wiring setup's actual validation step, and exporting validate() is really part of cbk's job (the thing that needs to call it).

### Acceptance Criteria

configuration package exposes a callable that runs the same checks as the current unexported validate() against a config.Config value in memory (either export validate itself, or add a thin Validate(cfg *config.Config) error wrapper -- whichever fits the package's existing exported-surface conventions). Loader.Load continues to use it internally with no behavior change. A test outside the package (e.g. in cbk's setup tests) can call it directly without going through file I/O.

title: [EPIC] archied setup: interactive first-run configuration
description:
Move config generation out of install.sh and into the daemon as 'archied setup', so the thing that writes config.toml is the same code that reads it. install.sh currently hand-rolls TOML and has already drifted from the schema once: it hardcoded the GitHub token key and the Gitea host, so a Gitea install produced a config naming a token the installer never wrote. Modelled on tau's 'tau setup' (internal/cli/setup.go, internal/app/setup.go), adapted for archie's TOML config and existing secret-reference indirection.

### Design

Port from tau: the CLI/app split behind a SetupPrompter interface so business logic is UI-agnostic and testable without a terminal; plain-stdio Select and hidden ReadSecret (golang.org/x/term) racing ctx.Done for Ctrl+C -- no TUI dependency; atomic temp+rename writes. DIVERGENCE FROM TAU: tau surgically patches YAML nodes to preserve comments. archie uses BurntSushi/toml, which does not preserve comments across a decode/encode round trip, so a full re-marshal would destroy config.example.toml's documentation. Decide this explicitly -- see the child issue. Secrets differ too: archie already has secret.SecretRef{engine,key} indirection, so setup writes the reference into TOML and the value into the env engine's store; that is archie's equivalent of tau's config.yaml/auth.yaml split and should be used rather than reinvented.

### Acceptance Criteria

install.sh no longer generates config.toml; it invokes archied setup. Setup is idempotent and re-runnable against an existing config without clobbering unrelated settings. Every config it writes passes configuration.Validate, verified by a test that runs setup non-interactively and validates the output. Secrets never reach config.toml or argv: config holds a secret reference, the value goes to the env file at 0600 via atomic write. Prompts for secrets do not echo. A non-TTY invocation without sufficient input fails with a clear message rather than writing a partial config.

title: fix(gateway): /compress destroys message identity, breaking dedup permanently
description:
applyCompress (session_commands.go:561-573) rebuilds retained head/tail turns as bare Message{From, Text}, dropping MessageID, SourceID and At. newMessageID with an empty SourceID returns a random UUID, so every protected message is deleted and re-inserted under a new identity with source_id NULL and _ts reset to now.

CONFIRMED by two independent reviewers, executed on BOTH backends. Before compress, redelivering tg-59 is a correct no-op (60 stays 60). After compress the same redelivery duplicates (24 -> 25). So archie-core-963's whole guarantee survives only until the first /compress -- after that, a Telegram 24h backlog replay on restart appends every surviving message a second time.

Also violates messaging-and-work-intake.md:88-90 (immutable application-generated MessageID) and 112-114 (immutable records), and dangles any branch-point correlation to the old IDs.

Blocks archie-core-963 and archie-core-0ua.

title: Setup steps: operator, provider, models, forge, chat channel
description:
The archie equivalent of tau's provider+model flow. Steps: (1) operator display name -> [chat].operator; (2) LLM provider -> [providers.<name>] class and api_key_env, with the key value stored via the secret engine; (3) models per role -> [models] triage/planner/builder, plus the optional [chat].models catalog; (4) forge -> github/gitea/none with host and a token reference, explicitly optional now that a missing forge credential only disables the forge; (5) chat channel -> Telegram bot token, optional. bot_user must always be written because validation requires it when no [[identities]] exist.

### Acceptance Criteria

Each step is skippable where the underlying setting is optional, and skipping leaves a valid config. Forge selection defaults to none rather than assuming a forge. The token key written into config matches the key the value was stored under, for every forge type -- the exact drift that broke the installer. Local model discovery (Ollama) is offered when available and degrades to free text when not.

title: install.sh: unknown flags are silently ignored
description:
The 'for arg in $@' case statement has no default branch, so a mistyped flag does nothing and the installer proceeds with defaults. '--no-systmd' installs the systemd service the user was trying to skip. Options discussed 2026-07-30: (a) reject unknown args with exit 1; (b) warn on stderr and continue; (c) reject unknown --flags but ignore bare words. Recommendation was (a) -- this is an interactive installer run by hand, typos dominate, and silent wrong behaviour is the worst outcome; the forward-compatibility argument for (b) does not apply while there is no ecosystem of wrapper scripts. Awaiting Sam's decision.

### Acceptance Criteria

A mistyped flag produces a clear diagnostic rather than silently different behaviour. The chosen policy is applied consistently and reflected in --help.

title: install.sh: --force is advertised but does nothing
description:
FORCE_BUILD is initialised at install.sh:42 and set at :67 by --force, then never read. --help advertises '--force  Force rebuild binaries even if up to date', so the flag is documented, accepted, and inert. The build step always rebuilds unconditionally, which means the flag is either redundant (delete it and the help line) or the up-to-date check it implies was never written.

### Acceptance Criteria

Either the flag and its help text are removed, or an up-to-date check exists that --force actually bypasses. No advertised flag is inert.

title: Telegram: announce newly installed Archie releases
description:
When archied starts after an installed release upgrade, notify authorized Telegram users once with an exact component-aware rundown from CHANGELOG.md. Present archied as THE GATEWAY and archie-agent as THE RUNTIME, explicitly saying when either component has no changes. Persist announced versions per recipient so ordinary restarts do not repeat notifications.

### Acceptance Criteria

Repository has a maintained component-aware CHANGELOG.md. On an installed version advance, each configured authorized Telegram user receives one concise message with separate THE GATEWAY and THE RUNTIME sections and explicit no-change wording where applicable. Announced component versions are persisted and duplicate restarts do not repeat. First-run and development builds have explicit non-spam behavior. Parsing, version transition, persistence failure, and delivery failure paths are tested.

title: fix(gateway): chronological message ordering — _ts + per-session collections
description:
SaveMessages keys from i=0 and overwrites the first N messages of any non-empty session (verified: m0/m1 destroyed by a bulk save). SaveMessage derives seq from len(rows) so deletes cause key reuse. The 'at' timestamp is written and never read; ordering is by insertion counter, not time.

Fix: add Message.At, write nell.TimestampField (_ts), give each session its own NellDB collection (a room IS a collection), key messages by time-ordered unique IDs, and order/page via sdk.ScanSince. Clean break on existing data (carina is a testing ground).

title: Regression tests: Events bus — multi-subscriber ordering, slow-consumer isolation
description: internal/events/events.go has only 2 tests (fan-out + close). Missing: multi-subscriber delivery ordering guarantees, slow-consumer isolation (one slow subscriber shouldn't block others), publish-after-close behavior, buffer overflow semantics.

title: Telegram: controlled execution and checkpoint commands
description:
Design /rollback [number] filesystem checkpoints, /stop background process termination, /approve and /deny for dangerous commands. /approve is RESERVED exclusively for dangerous-command approval; it must not be interpreted as task approval. The pending-command UX is inline selection buttons: Approve this time, Approve Permanently, Deny. Define the exact policy scope/lifetime for permanent approval, callback authorization, expiry, audit persistence, and cancellation. Requires a real sandbox/process/checkpoint authority; do not create commands that claim control over host processes or filesystem state Archie does not own.

### Acceptance Criteria

For every pending dangerous command, Telegram renders authorized inline buttons exactly representing Approve this time, Approve Permanently, and Deny. Callbacks are recipient-bound, expiring, single-use, auditable, and cannot authorize a changed command. Permanent approval scope/lifetime is explicit. /approve exclusively controls this policy; /deny controls the same policy. Authority boundaries match actual sandbox/process ownership; tests cover authorization, expiry, replay, denial, and failure.

title: Telegram: resilient session lifecycle and context commands

Design gateway/runtime-owned commands that remain usable when LLM credits are exhausted: /start acknowledgement without a reply; /new [name] with /reset alias; /topic [off|help|session-id] for Telegram DM topic sessions; /retry; /undo [N]; /title [name]; /branch [name] with /fork alias; /compress [here [N]|focus topic|--preview|--dry-run] with /compact alias. Define session history, branching, retry/undo atomicity, context accounting, and persistence before implementation.

### Acceptance Criteria

Every command has explicit session/history semantics and safe aliases; unavailable LLM credits do not block gateway/runtime commands; tests cover persistence, edge cases, and topic/session scoping.

title: Telegram: model scope and personality selection

Extend /model to support Hermes-like /model [model] [--provider name] [--global|--session] [--refresh], with persisted default behaviour. Add /personality [name] for predefined personalities. Design global-versus-session ownership, provider filtering, persistence, refresh semantics, validity when credits are exhausted, and interaction with existing model selector before implementation.

### Acceptance Criteria

/model scope and persistence are explicit and tested; provider/model selection cannot be ambiguous; /personality operates on a defined catalog and session scope; existing Telegram selector behaviour remains coherent.

title: Telegram: multi-home-channel command

When multiple home channels are introduced, design /sethome with /set_home alias to set a chat as a home channel. Define identity ownership, overwrite/confirmation rules, group authorization, persistence, and relationship to sessions before implementation.

### Acceptance Criteria

Blocked on the multiple-home-channel model; once unblocked, both aliases have identical safe behaviour, persist correctly, and are covered by authorization and migration tests.

title: Telegram: access, profile, and session navigation commands

Design and add Hermes-like /whoami, /profile, /resume [name], /sessions, plus /agents (active agents/running tasks). Determine Archie's actual role/access model, profile/home representation, session naming and browsing UX, persistence, authorization, and the relationship between /agents and the already-specified /tasks command before implementation.

### Acceptance Criteria

Each command accurately reports or navigates Archie-owned state; session listing/resume is safe and scoped; output/menu/help/tests are complete.

title: Telegram: steer and standing goal controls

Design and add Hermes-like /steer <prompt> (inject after next tool call without interruption), /goal [text|draft <text>|show|pause|resume|clear|status|wait <pid>|unwait], /subgoal [text|remove N|clear], and /queue <prompt> with aliases /q, /background <prompt> with aliases /bg and /btw. description:
Bring the frequently used Hermes control surface to Archie Telegram without copying Hermes semantics blindly. Design each command against Archie's actual session, task, goal, authorization, and future multi-home-channel models before implementation.

### Acceptance Criteria

Command behaviour, authorization, persistence, and Telegram UX are specified and implemented in focused child work; menu/help remain aligned; no command claims state Archie does not own.

title: isForgeDisabled is duplicated in cmd/archied
description:
resolveForge in cmd/archied/main.go needs the none/off/disabled predicate, but the identical helper in internal/infrastructure/configuration is unexported, so 518a1a0 copied it with a comment noting the duplication. Two copies of a validation predicate drift: adding a fourth disabled-alias in one place silently leaves the other accepting it.

### Acceptance Criteria

Tests: TestForgeDisabled table + discriminating warn-log assertions in TestResolveForgeDegradesInsteadOfFailing (verified to fail under re-inline drift). task check scoped: go test ./... green, gofumpt/vet clean, golangci-lint zero findings in changed files.

title: feat(config): edit configuration from the dashboard (hybrid file + DB)
description:
Goal: change runtime-tunable settings from the web UI without hand-editing TOML.

Decision (Sam, 2026-08-04): HYBRID, file stays primary. config.toml remains authoritative for bootstrap; a DB layer holds only runtime-tunable values as an overlay. Making the DB primary would move the thing that decides whether the daemon can boot into the thing the daemon must boot to read, and would lose the property that config is editable with any editor independent of daemon health.

The file format is NOT the blocker. Three things are, in this order:

1. Config is passed BY VALUE. daemon.Daemon{Cfg config.Config} and workflow.Cfg config.Config each hold a copy made at construction, so mutating a central config would never reach them. Subsystems must read through an accessor or receive change events instead of holding snapshots. This is the real prerequisite.

2. There is no reload path. No fsnotify, no SIGHUP, nothing -- Load runs once at startup. Changing the source without this only changes WHERE values come from, not WHEN.

3. Startup is a hard gate. cmd/archied/main.go:588-598 exits the daemon when an MCP provider fails to start. A UI that writes bad config could brick the next boot, which is worse from a DB than from a file you can open in an editor. Writes need validation before persist, and a documented recovery path.

Already in our favour: internal/infrastructure/configuration/ is a real loader package (discovery, feature files, extras, defaults, validation, provenance, tomlwrite) and is already multi-source across TOML and YAML. A DB source is a new decoder alongside decodeTOML/decodeYAML, not a rewrite. provenance.go already tracks where each value came from, which is what the UI needs to show 'this came from the file, this from the DB'.

Read-only config viewing already ships in the dashboard's Configuration section.

title: Regression tests: Telegram channel — message routing, command handling, middleware, splitting
description: Telegram channel tests are structural only (5 tests: Name, New, StartWithoutToken, Webhook 503, lifecycle). Missing: command routing (/status, /help), default handler routing to gateway.Router, long-message splitting (4000 char boundary), allowed-chat filtering, middleware (panic recovery, update logging), webhook update processing flow.

title: Chat channel plugin interface + Telegram channel
description:
No chat/messaging code exists today (confirmed: grep for Telegram across the repo returns nothing outside a skills-PRD example). Define a chat channel plugin interface (parallel to forge.Forge) and implement Telegram as the first channel, with a read-only /status command reading daemon/task state. Full spawn/control action parity (the write side of the interview requirement) is split into archie-core-abg.13 since it needs its own task-creation semantics for chat-initiated (non-issue-backed) tasks. Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase C.

### Acceptance Criteria

A chat.Channel interface exists (Name, Listen, Send or similar) implemented by a Telegram channel using the Bot HTTP API (long polling, no new heavy dependency). Sam can message the bot /status and get a real answer about current daemon/task state. Channel is wired into daemon startup behind an optional [chat] config block (absent = disabled, matching the [nats]/[containers] pattern).

title: Web Chat: support typed dangerous approvals
description: Make shared Web Chat accept Telegram-equivalent /approve and /deny for pending dangerous action IDs, while preserving numeric task approval and supporting permanent approval.

title: Web Chat: handle typed update command
description: Make /update a shared gateway command using the same release update service and response formatter as Telegram, so Web typed commands and update controls behave consistently.

title: Web Chat: capability-aware command discovery
description: Expose structured command metadata in Web Chat help and include optional update and dangerous-action commands only when their capabilities are enabled.

title: Web Chat: share dangerous action approval workflow
description: Extract the dangerous sandbox authority contract from Telegram and add an optional Web approval service for checkpoint rollback and process stop. The UI must remain hidden when no daemon-owned authority is configured and must require explicit approve, permanent approve, or deny decisions.

title: Web Chat: expose scoped Telegram restart
description: Share Telegram's scoped /restart behavior with Web Chat. Add a daemon-owned restart callback, shared router command, authenticated Web endpoint, and explicit UI control without restarting the whole daemon.

title: Web Chat: render Telegram-style Markdown replies
description: Render chat history and completed streamed replies with safe Markdown blocks, inline emphasis, links, code, lists, and quotes so the Web Chat matches Telegram's rich reply presentation.

title: Web Chat: expose Telegram update workflow
description: Expose the Telegram update check, defer, and approved install workflow in the Web Chat UI using the shared release update service. Preserve snapshot validation and explicit installation controls.

title: Web Chat: refine workspace composition and composer UX
description: Align the Web Chat page with the approved workspace inspiration: compact left conversation rail, centered empty state, quiet controls, and a composer-first layout while retaining existing sessions, streaming, commands, model, and personality controls.

title: Capability host: manifests, lifecycle, health, and typed family installation
description:
Replace the inert metadata-only daemon plugin inventory with a capability host that validates plugin manifests and coordinates lifecycle without adding generic domain hooks. The host owns module identity/API compatibility/dependency ordering/start/health/stop state; typed family registries remain responsible for capability registration. Wire it into archied startup/shutdown and expose status without passing *daemon.Daemon to plugins.

### Design

Keep plugin.Plugin exactly Name/Version. Add a validated Manifest and lifecycle vocabulary in internal/plugin plus a Host that manages manifests and lifecycle only. Capability packages receive narrow typed registrars; the host must not become an any-typed service locator. Start in dependency order, roll back a partially failed start, stop in reverse order, isolate panics/errors, and return immutable health snapshots. Preserve existing Yaegi loading through an adapter or manifest synthesis for metadata-only legacy plugins.

### Acceptance Criteria

Manifest validation covers stable ID, semantic version, host API compatibility, declared capability kinds, dependencies, permissions, and optional config schema. Duplicate IDs, missing dependencies, cycles, incompatible API versions, and invalid manifests fail deterministically. Host lifecycle tests prove dependency-ordered start, rollback, reverse stop, health aggregation, idempotent shutdown, and panic/error isolation. archied owns one host and starts/stops it. plugin.Plugin remains metadata-only and architecture tests pass. task check and lint are green apart from explicitly identified concurrent baseline failures; fresh adversarial review has no surviving findings.

title: Implement multi-identity daemon core (archie + winter as one process)
description:
Replace single Config.BotUser with the confirmed multi-identity config shape. Daemon runs multiple bot identities concurrently (each with its own forge token, repo list, model/provider config), dispatching through the existing shared NATS/container pipeline. Validate by migrating the two real carina processes (archie: bot_user=archie, repos=[archie-core,tau], deepseek models; winter: bot_user=winter, repos=[tau], local llama.cpp models) onto one daemon. Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase B.

### Acceptance Criteria

One archied process on carina replaces the current two (archie config.toml + winter.toml), producing the same dispatch behavior (issue polling, task claiming, PR flow) for both identities as the two separate processes did. No regression in existing single-identity config compatibility (old single-BotUser configs still work or have a documented migration path).

title: MVP: migrate Hermes profiles, memory, skills, and session state
description:
The copied live Hermes instance contains root plus agile-lead, dev, and local-agent profiles with distinct models, gateways, memories, SOUL prompts, skills, sessions, and cron state. archie-core currently has forge identities but no profile-scoped gateway/tool/memory/workspace composition and no importer. Define the mapping into archie-core identities/profiles and build a one-time idempotent migration plus cutover rehearsal.

### Acceptance Criteria

Document and implement the mapping for all copied profiles -- MAPPING DOCUMENTED (docs/prds/hermes-migration-dry-run.md), NOT YET IMPLEMENTED (blocked on abg.36). Import SOUL/USER/MEMORY/skills/session/cron without secrets -- NOT STARTED (design-blocked on abg.36, see report). Produce a dry-run report -- DONE. Rehearse dual-run/shadow validation and rollback-safe cutover checklist -- NOT STARTED.

title: MVP: make chat-originated tasks native and controllable
description:
The current /spawn path fabricates an issue number and enqueues it as if it were forge-backed, always against the first repo. The task schema has no source or identity, the workflow later performs forge labels/comments against a nonexistent issue, and /approve and /cancel are absent. Add a native chat task source routed through the same daemon-owned workflow and review gates without pretending a forge issue exists.

### Acceptance Criteria

Chat can select identity, repo, and workflow; /spawn creates a durable native task with a real task ID; daemon processing avoids forge-only operations when no forge artifact exists; /approve and /cancel enforce authorization and valid state transitions; end-to-end tests cover spawn through completion, approval, cancellation, restart recovery, and invalid cross-identity control.

title: MVP: complete multi-identity composition and task ownership routing
description:
The multi-identity types are not instantiated by cmd/archied, and the identity loop still polls with root Config fields then drains into root Forge, Trees, Config, and repo lookup. Tasks do not persist source identity. Complete the end-to-end ownership path so overlapping repo assignments for archie and winter cannot be claimed or acted on by the wrong identity.

### Acceptance Criteria

All items now DONE and build-verified: composition root builds every identity with its own forge/worktree -- DONE + VERIFIED (go build ./cmd/... passes). Task records carry identity -- DONE. NATS messages carry identity -- DONE. Polling/claiming/processing/labels/comments/pushes/PRs use owning identity -- DONE for in-process execution (documented gap for container mode, tracked separately, does not block this bead). Production-shaped two-identity-same-repo isolation test -- DONE (4 tests, race-clean).

title: MVP: run gateway conversations through the full agent/tool loop
description:
The Telegram responder currently calls runtime.Chat with MaxSteps=1 and no tool set. Email and webhook routers receive a nil responder. The central tool registry is empty/unconsumed; MCP transports are started without initialize/list/register/stop; the memory manager is not part of chat; skills and guardrails are not available to gateway turns. Replace the one-shot responder with one shared session-scoped conversational agent path used by Telegram, email, and webhook, preserving archie-core's daemon-owned safety boundaries.

### Acceptance Criteria

A gateway turn can use approved built-in tools, configured MCP tools, memory, skills, compression, and guardrails through a multi-step agent loop; Telegram, email, and webhook share this path; tool transports are initialized, discovered, registered, and shut down; an end-to-end test proves an inbound message causes a tool call and a delivered reply.

title: Audit Hermes-to-archie-core MVP takeover gaps
description:
Compare the copied live Hermes state in .hermes-carina with archie-core's current runtime and backlog. Determine the minimum remaining work for archie-core to replace Hermes on carina, explicitly excluding the in-flight secret engine and provider/config work.

### Acceptance Criteria

Document current capability parity, concrete blockers, minimum migration sequence, and non-MVP deferrals with file and issue evidence; do not modify implementation code.

title: Agent personalities/personas system
description:
Hermes has 14 personalities (catgirl, concise, creative, helpful, hype, kawaii, noir, philosopher, pirate, shakespeare, surfer, teacher, technical, uwu). Sam uses these. Personalities are system prompt modifiers that change the agent's communication style.

Scope:
- PersonaConfig: name + system prompt override/prefix
- Per-session persona selection (/persona slash command)
- Default persona from config
- Persona list command (/personas)
- Integration with MemoryManager.BuildSystemPrompt() (persona prompt inserted before memory context)

title: Context compression for long-running sessions
description:
Hermes config has compression enabled at 0.5 threshold, protecting first 3 and last 20 messages. Sam confirmed this is a must-have for long-running sessions. Without compression, context windows fill up and sessions degrade.

Scope:
- Compression threshold (fraction of context window used)
- Target compression ratio
- Protect first N / last N messages from compression
- Integrate with MemoryManager (pre-compress hook already defined: OnPreCompressProvider)
- Use the existing StreamingContextScrubber for fence-stripping during compression

title: Wire guardrails, memory, and MCP servers into daemon agent loop
description:
Tools P1 (guardrails, classification, budget), memory system (Manager, builtin provider, scrubber), and MCP transport are all built and tested but NOT called from cmd/archied/main.go. The daemon creates an agentexec.Runner but never passes GuardrailEngine, MemoryManager, or MCP client instances. This is THE blocker to using archie-core in place of Hermes.

Scope:
- Guardian: instantiate GuardrailEngine in daemon, call RecordSuccess/RecordFailure around tool calls
- Memory: inject MemoryManager.BuildSystemPrompt() into agent system prompt, wire HandleToolCall for memory tool routing
- MCP: instantiate configured MCP servers from config, register their tools, wire into agent tool dispatch
- Classification: use ToolClassification to gate parallel vs serial execution in the tool dispatcher

title: Integrate NellDB as persistent memory and configuration backend
description:
Replace SQLite+FTS5+file-based storage with NellDB, Sam's existing distributed document database. NellDB provides:

- **nell.Store interface**: Put, Get, Delete, List, ListAll, Query, GetChangesSince, SearchSimilar (vector search)
- **sdk.DocDB**: Document database with MVCC revisions
- **logstore**: Durable Zstd-compressed append-only log
- **sdk.Replicator**: Multi-primary HTTP replication with HLC knowledge vectors
- **Vector search**: HNSW + PCA + PQ for semantic memory
- **HTTP server**: Standalone binary on port 9342

Plan:

1. Add NellDB as a dependency (go get github.com/samcharles93/NellDB)
2. Create internal/nell/ adapter package wrapping nell.Store for archie-core's data models
3. Collections: sessions, messages, memory, config, tasks
4. Replace internal/store (SQLite) with NellDB backend
5. Replace file-based MEMORY.md with nell collections + vector search
6. Wire into cmd/archied/main.go as the storage backend

This gives archie-core multi-primary replication for free — two archied instances on different hosts can sync state without a central database.

Ref: /work/apps/nell-engine/ (store.go, types.go, sdk/docdb.go, server/)

### Acceptance Criteria

archied starts with a NellDB backend instead of SQLite. Sessions and messages persist across restarts. Vector search returns semantically similar messages. Two archied instances can replicate state via nell sync.

title: Design pass: multi-identity daemon config shape
description:
Config.BotUser (internal/config) is a single global field -- the root blocker for running multiple bot identities (archie, winter) in one daemon instead of N processes. docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md sec.4 sketches a [[identities]] TOML shape but flags the open question unresolved: does each identity get its own poll loop/goroutine feeding shared NATS/container dispatch, or does one loop iterate all identities? Needs a short design doc answering this before Phase B implementation starts, since it affects rate-limit isolation between identities.

### Acceptance Criteria

A design note (added to multi-agent-collaboration.md or a new doc) confirms the identity config shape and the poll-loop-per-identity vs single-loop decision, with reasoning tied to failure isolation (one identity's forge outage must not starve another's dispatch).

title: Scale-to-zero: idle detection and dormant quiesce
description:
Scale-to-zero idle detection:

1. **Idle predicate**: running_agent_count == 0 AND seconds_since_last_inbound > idle_timeout AND no live background work.
2. **Dormant transition**: Signal relay transport to close socket (supervisor preserved).
3. **Wake trigger**: Inbound message on wake URL resumes gateway.
4. **Structural precondition**: Only arms when messaging is relay-only or absent AND a wake URL is registered.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 6 (scale_to_zero.py)

### Acceptance Criteria

When no messages arrive for the configured idle timeout (with no active agents), the gateway transitions to dormant. An inbound message wakes it.

description:

3. **Iterative summary merging**: Multiple compression rounds, tool output pruning before LLM summarization.

When a conversation approaches context limit, the auxiliary model summarizes middle turns. Session rotates to a child session. The agent continues without losing context.

RouteConfig.Template's meaning would change from 'the one field to extract' to 'a template string' -- update its doc comment in the same change.
