title: WebhookAdapter: HTTP server with per-route HMAC validation
description: Implement WebhookAdapter as an HTTP server supporting per-route HMAC validation: GitHub X-Hub-Signature-256, GitLab X-Gitlab-Token, and a generic V2 timestamp-bound HMAC scheme.
notes: Partially done: internal/channels/webhook/webhook.go:186-196 validateHMAC() implements GitHub-style HMAC-SHA256 (X-Hub-Signature-256/X-Signature-256, sha256= prefix). title: Webhook platform: generic inbound adapter with HMAC + filters + templates
description:
Generic webhook platform adapter:

1. **HTTP server**: Receives POSTs from external services (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, etc.). Per-route configuration.
2. **HMAC validation**: GitHub (X-Hub-Signature-256), GitLab (X-Gitlab-Token), Svix/AgentMail, generic V2 (timestamp-bound replay protection), legacy V1.
3. **Declarative filters**: all/any/not, field resolution (dot-notation), equals/contains/regex, in_file.
4. **Script transforms**: External bash/python scripts per route that transform or filter payloads.
5. **Prompt templates**: Dot-notation template rendering from webhook payloads ({pull_request.title}).
6. **deliver_only mode**: Skip agent, render prompt as deliverable message (push notifications at zero LLM cost).
7. **Idempotency cache**: TTL-based dedup of webhook retries.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md (webhook.py, webhook_filters.py, msgraph_webhook.py)

### Acceptance Criteria

A GitHub webhook lands on /webhooks/github, passes HMAC validation, renders a prompt from the PR payload, and the agent responds. Duplicate deliveries are deduped.

title: Delivery system: router, ledger, dead targets, wake
description:
Outbound message delivery infrastructure built on NATS JetStream (already provides guaranteed delivery, dead-letter queues, ack/nak, dedup — no need for a separate actor engine like Hollywood).

1. **DeliveryTarget**: Parse strings like 'telegram:12345' or 'discord:channel:thread'. Resolve to platform adapter.
2. **DeliveryRouter**: Route content to configured targets, handle truncation, silence-narration filtering.
3. **DeliveryLedger**: JetStream consumer with max-deliver=3, ack-wait configurable per target. Crash recovery via NATS redelivery (no separate SQLite ledger needed).
4. **DeadTargetRegistry**: Persistent JSON tracking of confirmed-dead targets (deleted groups, kicked bots). Self-healing on successful send.
5. **Wake delivery**: Use NATS request/reply for async delivery to push-capable adapters.

### Acceptance Criteria

A cron job can schedule a message for delivery. If the target is unreachable, the ledger retries. If the bot is kicked from a group, the target is registered dead and skipped.

title: Feature-based config: split monolithic config.toml into modular files
description:
Sam's explicit directive: move to feature-based YAML config files in conf.d/ (Linux convention) instead of one monolithic config.toml.

## Design

- ~/.config/archie/config.yaml — daemon-level (work_dir, db_path, poll_interval, max_retries, bot_user, skills_dir, plugin_dir, label, diff_cap_lines, agent, budgets, web, notify, nats, containers, dispatch, forge)
- ~/.config/archie/conf.d/gateway.yaml — chat channels, platform configs
- ~/.config/archie/conf.d/tools.yaml — MCP servers, tool policy
- ~/.config/archie/conf.d/memory.yaml — memory provider config
- ~/.config/archie/conf.d/models.yaml — LLM providers and model role mappings
- ~/.config/archie/conf.d/identities.yaml — identity configs (replaces [[identities]] in TOML)

## Implementation requirements

1. New function: LoadDir(baseDir, overlayDir string) (Config, error)
2. New types on Config: MemoryConfig, ToolsConfig (with MCPServer + ToolPolicy), Extra map[string]any
3. Feature files as top-level YAML keys (memory.yaml has provider, provider_config, session_ttl; tools.yaml has mcp_servers, tool_policy; models.yaml has models, providers, etc.)
4. Legacy support: if config.yaml absent, fall back to config.toml via existing Load function
5. Existing Load() and LoadOverlay() preserved unchanged (they still work with monolithic TOML)
6. Overlay support: overlayDir files merged on top of baseDir files (shallow merge per file, overlay values take precedence, base values inherited for missing keys)
7. Validation: unknown feature files error (prevent typos like config.gaeway.yaml), duplicate feature files error (same name in root and conf.d/), malformed YAML errors
8. Missing feature files mean feature disabled (zero values, no error)
9. YAML parser: gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (already a transitive dependency via NellDB)

## Test contract

28 tests in internal/config/feature_config_test.go define the COMPLETE spec. An implementing agent must:
- NOT modify the test file
- Write implementation that makes all 28 tests pass
- The key signature is: func LoadDir(baseDir, overlayDir string) (Config, error)

## Acceptance
All 28 LoadDir tests pass. Existing Load/LoadOverlay tests pass. go build ./... clean. No config.toml parsing capability is lost.

### Acceptance Criteria

A new feature (e.g. MCP) can be configured by adding one new TOML file. No changes to existing config parsing code are needed. Legacy monolithic config.toml still works.

title: MemoryManager notify_memory_tool_write

After any successful built-in memory tool write, MemoryManager calls external provider's on_memory_write(content) hook

title: MemoryManager prefetch with timeout
description:
Implement prefetch in MemoryManager with an 8-second default timeout. If a provider's prefetch is still running from the previous turn, skip it rather than queue another. This prevents memory lookups from blocking the agent loop.

### Acceptance Criteria

prefetch(ctx, query) accepts a context with configurable timeout (default 8s)
If a provider is still prefetching from the previous turn, the new prefetch is skipped (not queued)
A provider-level mutex or state flag tracks in-flight prefetch operations
Timeout causes context cancellation which the provider should respect
Results from prefetch are stored for retrieval in system_prompt_block()
Metrics/logging track prefetch duration, timeouts, and skips

title: MemoryManager background sync pipeline
description:
Implement a serialized background sync pipeline in MemoryManager using a single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor pattern. All write operations from external providers are serialized through one worker to guarantee write ordering and prevent concurrent mutations.

### Acceptance Criteria

A single-worker goroutine/worker pool processes queued sync operations
Write operations are submitted to the pipeline and processed in FIFO order
Caller receives a channel/future for optional completion notification
Write ordering is guaranteed - operations don't reorder
Pipeline has a configurable buffer size (default 100)
Pipeline drains on shutdown with configurable timeout
Errors from sync operations are logged but don't crash the pipeline

title: MemoryProvider optional methods
description:

MemoryManager checks via type assertion at runtime which optional interfaces a provider implements
Each optional interface has clear doc comments
Default no-op behavior when a provider doesn't implement an optional interface

title: Shutdown drain with timeout and abandoned-write tracking
description:
Implement graceful shutdown drain for MemoryManager with a bounded timeout. In-flight sync operations are given a configurable deadline to complete. Operations that don't finish within the deadline are tracked as abandoned writes for diagnostics.

### Acceptance Criteria

Shutdown(ctx) method on MemoryManager with context-based deadline
In-flight sync pipeline operations are given N seconds (default 10) to complete
Abandoned writes (those exceeding the deadline) are logged with: provider name, operation type, age
shutdown() is called on all active providers in reverse registration order
After shutdown, no new operations are accepted
Provider shutdown respects the same deadline
Abandoned-write counter is accessible for health/status reporting

title: Threat scanning integration for memory content
description:
Integrate threat scanning for all memory content writes. Before persisting any memory content (add/replace/remove), scan the content for potentially dangerous patterns (injection attempts, sensitive data leakage, prompt injection in stored memory).

### Acceptance Criteria

A ScanContent(content string) function or hook is called before every memory write
Scans cover: prompt injection patterns, sensitive data patterns (API keys, passwords, tokens)
Configurable to reject (block the write) or warn (allow with log) on suspicious content
Integration point at the MemoryManager level so it applies to all providers
Results are logged for audit
Config flag to disable scanning for development

title: Frozen snapshot pattern for memory injection
description:
Implement the frozen snapshot pattern: memory content is read at session start and injected into the system prompt as a snapshot. On write, files are updated immediately but the system prompt is NOT changed mid-session. Only the next session picks up the new snapshot.

### Acceptance Criteria

At session start, MEMORY.md and USER.md are read and formatted into a system prompt block
This formatted block becomes part of the session's system prompt (frozen for the session duration)
When a memory write occurs, the files are updated immediately on disk
The in-memory snapshot for the current session is NOT updated
The next session reads the fresh files and creates a new frozen snapshot
Config flag to disable frozen snapshot (always read fresh) for testing

title: Built-in memory tool actions: add, replace, remove
description:
Implement the three core memory tool actions: add (appends new content to a section), replace (replaces content using substring matching to find the target), remove (deletes content using substring matching). These act on the MEMORY.md/USER.md files.

### Acceptance Criteria

Tool exposes three actions: add, replace, remove
add(target_section, content) appends to or creates a named section
replace(target_section, substring, replacement) finds first match of substring in section and replaces it
remove(target_section, substring) removes the matching line/block from the section
Substring matching is exact, case-sensitive by default (configurable)
Actions return clear success/error messages including the affected section and character count
Tool validates section names (alphanumeric + spaces, max 64 chars)
Size bounds are checked before any write (reject if would exceed max file size)

title: Built-in memory tool: file-backed persistent memory
description:
Implement the built-in file-backed memory tool that persists to MEMORY.md and USER.md files. This replaces the current ephemeral memoryNotes system with durable on-disk storage that survives restarts and sessions.

### Acceptance Criteria

Built-in provider lives in internal/memory/builtin package
MEMORY.md stores persistent agent memory (facts, preferences, state across sessions)
USER.md stores user-provided context (background, instructions, preferences)
Both files are bounded (configurable max size, default 100KB per file)
Files are read at provider initialization and written on every mutation
File format is plain markdown with sections
Thread-safe reads and writes (sync.RWMutex)
Files live under the profile's memory directory (e.g., ~/.config/archie/profiles/{profile}/memory/)

title: Tool schema normalization for memory providers
description:
Implement tool schema normalization that handles both bare tools (just Function definition) and wrapped OpenAI-style tool schemas from memory providers. Ensures all provider-exported tools are normalized to a consistent format before being merged into the agent's tool list.

### Acceptance Criteria

Normalizer package detects whether a schema is bare (map with 'name' top-level) or wrapped (map with 'type':'function', 'function':{...})
Converts both formats to a canonical internal representation
Handles edge cases: missing required fields, extra unknown fields
Schema normalization happens at registration time, not per-turn
Errors on truly invalid schemas with clear messages
Round-trips through JSON marshal/unmarshal

title: StreamingContextScrubber
description:
Implement a stateful StreamingContextScrubber that strips <memory-context>...</memory-context> fence spans from streaming text output. Must handle partial chunks that split across fence boundaries, maintain state between chunks, and only emit clean text downstream.

### Acceptance Criteria

Scrubber is in internal/memory/scrubber package
Implements an io.Writer or callback interface for processing streaming chunks
Strips <memory-context> ... </memory-context> fences including the tags themselves
Handles partial chunks where fence tags span chunk boundaries (maintains state)
Handles missing closing tags (closes at end of stream)
Doesn't interfere with non-memory-context content
Zero allocations in the hot path (reuses buffers)
Fully tested with edge cases: partial open/close, nested tags, empty content

title: MemoryProvider interface (abstract)
description:
Define the core MemoryProvider interface with required methods: name(), is_available(), initialize(session_id), get_tool_schemas(). This is the contract that all memory providers (built-in and external/plugin) must implement.

### Acceptance Criteria

MemoryProvider is defined as a Go interface in a new internal/memory/provider package
name() returns a unique human-readable string identifying the provider
is_available() returns true when the provider is ready for use
initialize(session_id) prepares the provider for a given session
get_tool_schemas() returns the tool definitions the provider exports to the agent
Clean godoc comments on all methods

title: [EPIC] Memory: pluggable provider architecture with file-backed persistence
description:
Pluggable memory system to match Hermes parity:

1. **MemoryProvider interface**: Abstract interface with methods for initialize(), get_tool_schemas(), prefetch(), sync_turn(), and optional lifecycle hooks (on_session_end, on_session_switch, on_pre_compress, on_memory_write).

2. **Built-in file-backed memory**: MEMORY.md and USER.md stored per-session/profile. LLM-callable memory tool with add/replace/remove actions. Frozen snapshot at session start (preserves prefix cache), immediate disk write on updates. Section-sign delimited entries with substring matching.

3. **MemoryManager**: Orchestrates built-in + at most one external provider. Background serialized write executor. Prefetch with timeout (8s). Streaming context scrubber that strips injected memory spans from model output.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 4

### Acceptance Criteria

An external memory provider (e.g. Honcho, Mem0) can be plugged in via config. The built-in memory tool persists across sessions. Conversation context is recalled on session resume.

title: Multimodal result envelope handling
description:
Implement a multimodal result envelope type (is_multimodal flag, text summary, subdir hint). When tools return multimodal content (images, audio, video, documents), wrap the result in an envelope that provides a text summary for context-feed while storing the actual media at a hinted subdirectory path.

### Acceptance Criteria

Multimodal result envelope type implemented (tools.MultimodalResult) and wired into the MCP client's tool-call handler with progressive disclosure (text summary always present, media persisted to a hinted subdirectory only when configured) -- DONE. Adversarially reviewed with all findings fixed and regression-tested -- DONE.

title: File checkpointing before mutating operations
description: Implement file checkpointing: before any tool that modifies state (file writes, config changes, etc.) executes, snapshot the relevant files or state sections so they can be rolled back on failure. This provides safety guards for mutating tool operations.

title: Per-turn aggregate budget enforcement (200K char cap)
description: Implement a per-turn aggregate output budget of 200,000 characters. Track cumulative tool result sizes within a turn. When the budget is exceeded, auto-spill the largest results to disk. Enforce a hard stop at the budget limit with clear reporting to the user.

title: Concurrent tool dispatch with execution gating
description: Implement concurrent tool dispatch with execution gating classes: never-parallel (e.g. state mutators), parallel-safe (e.g. read-only tools), and path-scoped (same-path tools are serialized, different paths run in parallel). Use sync primitives and a gating engine to classify and schedule tool invocations correctly.

title: Sequential tool dispatch with per-result previews and error handling
description: Build the sequential tool dispatch pipeline: invoke tools one-at-a-time, capture per-result previews (truncated output for context-feed), and implement error classification with graceful fallback. Each result should produce a short preview snippet for inclusion in the conversation context.

title: feat(gateway): task_list and task_spawn chat tools
description:
/spawn, /approve and /cancel are slash commands only a human types (internal/gateway/gateway.go:299-401), so 'what are you working on?' has no tool path, even though TaskCreator/TaskController (internal/gateway/tasks.go) are one import away.

internal/gateway/tasks.go gains a narrow read interface chatTaskLister (ListChatTasks(ctx, identity, limit) ([]ChatTaskSummary, error)), keeping gateway independent of internal/store; the daemon adapts store.Store.Tasks.

internal/gateway/task_tools.go (new): TaskTools(lister, creator, identity) returning task_list and task_spawn, both bound to the calling gateway's identity so the model never supplies it.

task_approve and task_cancel are deliberately excluded: waiting_human is the one point in the lifecycle where a person must act and /approve is that gate. Chat input is an untrusted path (a forge issue body or inbound email quoted into a turn is model-visible text), so a tool that approves Archie's own work removes the only human checkpoint. Add behind an operator flag defaulting to off if wanted later.

Wired into chatGenerateOptions, merged over the registry-built set.

title: feat(tools): web_fetch tool with dial-time SSRF protection
description:
Archie has no web access of any kind and no MCP server configured to substitute, so it cannot open a URL pasted into chat.

New package internal/tools/webfetch, registered directly in cmd/archied/main.go beside skill_activate.

Schema: url (required), raw (bool, skip HTML extraction).

- http/https scheme allowlist.
- SSRF protection in DialContext, NOT as a pre-flight URL check: resolve the host, reject loopback/private/link-local/unspecified/multicast, then dial the vetted IP. A pre-flight URL check leaves a DNS-rebinding hole, and this daemon runs on a host with the Docker socket and NATS reachable on 172.19.0.1.
- CheckRedirect caps hops and re-applies the scheme check.
- Body capped by io.LimitReader; result then capped by the per-tool limit.
- text/html -> readable text via golang.org/x/net/html; text/*, json, xml as-is; anything else an error naming content type and size.
- Non-2xx returns status plus a short excerpt.

Config [tools.web_fetch]: enabled, timeout, max_bytes, allow_private_networks (default false). Defaults via configuration.applyDefaults.
close_reason: Complete: internal/tools/webfetch (webfetch.go, tool.go) implements every clause. Dial-time SSRF protection via custom DialContext (webfetch.go:66,233,240) that resolves the host and rejects private/loopback before dialing the vetted IP -- not a pre-flight URL check, matching the DNS-rebinding concern the issue calls out explicitly. CheckRedirect present (webfetch.go:74), AllowPrivateNetworks config wired through internal/config/config.go:322-326 (default false) and internal/tools/webfetch/webfetch.go:49-52,256, HTML-to-text via golang.org/x/net/html, and the tool is registered in cmd/archied/main.go:992 beside skill_activate as specified. go test ./internal/tools/webfetch/... -race -count=1 is green.

title: Firecracker substrate for sandboxed MCP code tools
description:
Replace the interim daemon-container code MCP execution path with a real Firecracker boundary. Extend or extract the gorev POC to support a long-lived bidirectional guest process, explicit workspace import/export, per-turn filesystem checkpoints, lifecycle/health, and concurrent-instance-safe networking. Then adapt the MCP provider launcher without changing the chat/tool contract.

### Acceptance Criteria

MCP server code and tool execution occur inside a Firecracker VM; the guest cannot access daemon-host files outside the imported workspace; changes export deterministically; pre-change checkpoints support /restore; lifecycle cleanup survives crashes; tests prove the configured provider cannot silently fall back to host execution.

title: Wire MCP tool servers for the chat agent, sandboxed
description:
The chat agent has only memory_edit and skill_activate, so it cannot act on the codebase. cfg.Tools.MCPServers + the stdio transport are the designed extension point (configuredMCPProvider in cmd/archied/main.go already builds providers from config). Sam's requirement is to expose specific capabilities narrowly rather than granting host access, and he has a Firecracker sandbox POC at /work/clones/gorev (firecracker/sandbox) intended for exactly this.

### Acceptance Criteria

MCP servers are configurable per deployment and discovered into the chat agent tool loop. A narrowly scoped code MCP server runs in the daemon container against an explicitly configured workspace and can make a code change end to end. Firecracker execution remains a requirement tracked separately in archie-core-abg.17.44.

title: wire MCP per-server parallel-tool-calls flag into config and daemon startup
description:
Follow-up to archie-core-abg.17.20, which added mcp.Client.parallelToolCalls + WithParallelToolCalls(bool) at the client-API level (adversarially reviewed, race-clean). Nothing currently sets it: config.MCPServer (internal/config/config.go) has no field for it, and both NewClient call sites (cmd/archied/main.go:510's mcp.NewClient, and internal/tools/provider/mcp/provider.go:85's protocol.NewClient) construct clients without the option -- so the flag has zero effect in production as things stand today.

### Acceptance Criteria

config.MCPServer gains a ParallelToolCalls bool field (default false, matching the client's safe-by-default); both NewClient call sites read it and pass mcp.WithParallelToolCalls(cfg value) accordingly; a config-driven test proves a server configured with parallel_tool_calls=true actually gets a parallel-opted Client.

title: Tool-provider engine: lifecycle registry with MCP and memory providers
description:
Build the typed tool-provider capability family over the central tools registry. Providers declare a plugin manifest, lifecycle/health, and discover executable ToolEntry values. Add adapters for memory.Manager and configured MCP servers, perform MCP initialize/tools-list/tools-call, register handlers atomically with collision rollback, translate available entries to ai-sdk core.ToolSet, and wire consumers so registered tools are actually callable rather than dead daemon fields.

### Design

internal/tools owns Provider and ProviderRegistry; Provider is a typed domain contract and uses the shared plugin manifest/lifecycle vocabulary. The registry owns provider registration and tool indexing while the capability host orchestrates cross-family lifecycle. Memory is adapted without changing internal/memory concurrent work. MCP provider wraps the existing stdio transport without modifying its concurrent implementation, adds protocol client behavior in new files, prefixes/sanitizes server tool names deterministically, and retains original MCP names for calls. Never advertise a tool on an execution path that cannot invoke its handler; explicitly proxy or omit tools across subprocess/NATS boundaries.

### Acceptance Criteria

Provider registration is atomic and rejects duplicate provider/tool IDs without partial state. Start/discovery failure rolls back tools and lifecycle; stop removes availability and shuts providers down in reverse order. Memory provider tools appear in the central registry and execute through memory.Manager. A fake MCP server proves initialize, initialized notification where supported, tools/list discovery, tools/call execution, JSON-RPC errors, shutdown, and name mapping. Available tools convert to valid ai-sdk core.ToolSet and are used by the gateway conversational loop and supported agent execution paths; unsupported remote paths do not advertise unusable handlers. Configuration creates providers through typed factories. Focused/race tests, lint, task check, and fresh adversarial review pass subject only to documented concurrent baseline failures.

title: MCP client: per-server parallel tool call opt-in flag
description: Add a per-server configuration flag to opt-in to parallel tool calls in the MCP client. When enabled, the client may dispatch multiple tool calls to the same MCP server concurrently. When disabled, all calls to that server are serialized. This respects server-side concurrency limitations.

title: Central tool registry singleton with Register() + discovery
description: Implement a global tool registry singleton with a Register() method. Add file-system discovery that scans tools/*.go for registry.Register calls to auto-register tools at startup. This is the core infrastructure that all tool registration and lookup depends on.

title: MCP client: server-initiated sampling
description: Implement MCP server-initiated sampling support: when the MCP server sends a sampling request, route it to the LLM and return the sampled response. This enables MCP servers to request LLM completions as part of tool execution (e.g. for sub-agent delegation within a tool).

title: MCP client: SSE transport
description: Implement MCP SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport: establish SSE connection to MCP servers, handle event stream parsing, manage reconnection with backoff, and translate SSE events to the unified MCP transport interface. This enables real-time streaming from MCP servers.

title: MCP client: HTTP/StreamableHTTP transport
description: Implement MCP HTTP/StreamableHTTP transport: make JSON-RPC requests over HTTP/HTTPS with support for streamable HTTP responses. Handle connection lifecycle, keep-alive, reconnection, and error classification for remote MCP servers accessed via HTTP.

title: MCP client: stdio transport (subprocess management)
description: Implement the MCP stdio transport: spawn and manage MCP server subprocesses, handle stdin/stdout JSON-RPC message framing, subprocess lifecycle (start/stop/restart), and auto-restart with exponential backoff. This is the foundational MCP transport that most local MCP servers use.

title: Context-pressure threshold gating
description: Implement context-pressure threshold gating: when the combined size of tool schemas exceeds a configurable percentage of the LLM context window, automatically switch to progressive tool disclosure mode (bridge tools). Monitor context usage and toggle between full disclosure and bridge-tool mode dynamically.

title: Progressive tool disclosure (bridge tools)
description: Implement the progressive tool disclosure pattern with three bridge tools: tool_search (search available tools by keyword), tool_describe (return full schema for one tool), and tool_call (invoke a tool by name after discovery). This keeps the LLM's tool schema footprint small while providing full access to the tool arsenal on demand.

title: Guardrail decision engine: warning vs hard-stop
description: Implement the guardrail decision engine that uses ToolCallGuardrailConfig thresholds to decide between sending a warning to the LLM or issuing a hard-stop (aborting the tool loop). Considers exact_failure_warn_after, same_tool_failure_warn_after, and no_progress_warn_after. Must track per-session and per-turn counters.

title: Mutating tool classification set
description: Define and maintain a classification set of mutating (mutation-capable) tools. These tools can modify state and require serialization, checkpointing, and stricter guardrail monitoring. The set should be extensible via registration metadata and feed into dispatch gating and checkpointing decisions.

title: Idempotent tool classification set
description: Define and maintain a classification set of idempotent (read-only) tools. These tools can be safely retried and run in parallel. The set should be extensible via registration metadata. Classification feeds into dispatch gating, guardrail decisions, and budget enforcement.

title: Tool guardrails: ToolCallGuardrailConfig
description: Implement the ToolCallGuardrailConfig struct with thresholds: exact_failure_warn_after (how many exact same failures before warning), same_tool_failure_warn_after (same-tool consecutive failures), and no_progress_warn_after (total tool calls without completing the turn goal). This is the configuration layer for the guardrail decision engine.

title: ToolEntry data type definition
description: Design and implement the ToolEntry data type carrying: name, toolset (which tool group this belongs to), schema (JSON Schema for invocation), handler (function ref), check_fn (availability predicate), requires_env (env vars needed), is_async (async/sync distinction), description, emoji, max_result_size_chars (per-tool result cap), and dynamic_schema_overrides (runtime schema mutations). This is the foundational type that everything in the tools subsystem builds upon.

title: [EPIC] Tools: central registry, MCP client, guardrails
description:
Central tool infrastructure to match Hermes parity:

1. **Tool registry**: A central registry where tool modules register themselves with name, schema, handler, toolset membership, and availability check. Dynamic discovery of built-in tools. This replaces the current pattern of manually constructing core.ToolSet maps per invocation.

2. **MCP client**: Connect to external MCP servers via stdio, HTTP/StreamableHTTP, or SSE transport. Discover their tools and register them into the tool registry. Support automatic reconnection with backoff, configurable timeouts, per-server parallel tool call opt-in.

3. **Guardrails**: Tool-call loop detection (repeated calls, repeated failures, no-progress loops). Idempotent/mutating tool classification. Warning vs hard-stop decisions.

4. **Progressive disclosure**: When tool schemas exceed a context-window threshold, replace them with bridge tools (tool_search/tool_describe/tool_call) and surface on demand. Core tools are always visible.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 3

### Acceptance Criteria

MCP servers can be configured with a TOML block and their tools appear alongside built-ins. The agent loop is protected against tool-call loops. Tool schemas stay within context budget.

title: SessionSource struct for platform identity
Platform capability flags for adapters
description:
A capability-flag mechanism so callers can ask an adapter which optional features it supports (typing indicator, edit, delete, media send, clarify/approval/picker UI) instead of discovering support by a failed type assertion or a runtime error.

### Context for implementers

This depends on the optional-method interfaces this issue is meant to describe: `archie-core-1786637493329-136-49b39c78` (typing/edit/delete/media) and `archie-core-1786637493357-137-35af7083` (clarify/approval/pickers). Implement after (or in close coordination with) those two, since the flag set should mirror whatever optional interfaces they land — don't invent a flag taxonomy ahead of the methods it describes.

### Acceptance Criteria

`BasePlatformAdapter` (`internal/gateway/adapter.go`) or a wrapping type exposes a capability query (e.g. `Capabilities() AdapterCapabilities`) that reports which optional methods an adapter implements. Every existing adapter's reported capabilities match its actual method set (a regression test should fail if an adapter claims a capability it doesn't implement, or vice versa).
notes: Partial: the mechanism itself (gateway.CapabilityReporter, CapabilitiesOf, AdapterCapabilities) is built and covered by a regression test, scoped to Media only -- see archie-core-1786637493329-136-49b39c78 (closed, media portion). Still blocked on archie-core-1786637493357-137-35af7083 (clarify/approval/pickers) since AdapterCapabilities needs those flags added too before this is fully done.

title: BasePlatformAdapter interactive UX methods (clarify, approval, pickers)
description:
Add adapter-facing methods for interactive UX: presenting a clarifying question, an approval prompt, and a picker (multi-choice selection) natively on the platform, rather than as plain text the user has to reply to by hand.

### Context for implementers

The approval *decision* plumbing already exists — `internal/tools/approval.go`, re-exported through `internal/gateway/approval.go` (`ApprovalRequester`, `ApprovalDecision`, `WithApprovalRequester`/`ApprovalFromContext`). What's missing is the adapter-side rendering: `BasePlatformAdapter` (`internal/gateway/adapter.go`) has no method for an adapter to display an approval/clarify/picker UI and report back a decision through that existing plumbing. This issue wires a new adapter method (or interface) into the existing `ApprovalRequester` flow — it should not duplicate or replace the decision model in `internal/tools/approval.go`. Sibling of `archie-core-1786637493329-136-49b39c78` (typing/edit/delete/media) — same "optional adapter capability" shape, different capability set.

### Acceptance Criteria

An adapter can render a clarify/approval/picker prompt and the user's response is delivered back through the existing `ApprovalRequester`/`ApprovalDecision` flow in `internal/tools/approval.go`, not a parallel mechanism. Platforms without native UI (e.g. plain text-only channels) degrade to a text-based fallback rather than failing. Covered by a test double adapter, not a live platform.

title: BasePlatformAdapter optional methods (typing, edit, delete, media)
description:
Extend adapter capability beyond the four required `BasePlatformAdapter` methods with optional per-platform methods: typing indicator, message edit, message delete, and media-specific send.

### Context for implementers

`internal/gateway/adapter.go` today defines `BasePlatformAdapter` with exactly four methods: `Connect`, `Disconnect`, `Send`, `ChatInfo` (see full listing — the file is 80 lines). Not every platform supports typing/edit/delete/media uniformly, so these should be a separate optional interface(s) that callers type-assert for, not additions to the required interface (that would break every existing adapter implementation). Pairs with `archie-core-1786637493387-138-cad8e7a7` (platform capability flags) — callers need a way to know *ahead of a type assertion* whether an adapter supports a given optional method, rather than probing via failed assertions at call time.

### Acceptance Criteria

Optional methods are defined on a separate interface (or interfaces) from `BasePlatformAdapter`, so existing adapters keep compiling unchanged. At least one adapter implementation exercises each optional method in a test. Callers that invoke an optional method on an adapter that doesn't implement it get a defined, non-panicking behavior.

title: BasePlatformAdapter interface with required methods
EphemeralReply type with auto-delete TTL
description:
An `EphemeralReply` type for messages the gateway sends that should self-delete after a TTL — status/progress placeholders ("thinking…", "running tool X…") that shouldn't linger in the chat history once superseded.

### Context for implementers

No ephemeral-reply file exists yet in `internal/gateway`. Deletion requires adapter support: `BasePlatformAdapter` (`internal/gateway/adapter.go`) currently exposes only `Connect`/`Disconnect`/`Send`/`ChatInfo` — no delete method. This depends on (or should land alongside) `archie-core-1786637493329-136-49b39c78` (BasePlatformAdapter optional methods, which includes delete) — an adapter without a delete method can't honor the TTL.

### Acceptance Criteria

An `EphemeralReply` carries a TTL after which the gateway issues a delete against the originating adapter. Adapters without delete support degrade gracefully (e.g. leave the message, log once) rather than erroring the turn. TTL firing is covered by a test using an injected clock, not a real sleep.

title: Telegram: interactive /model selector
description:
When /model is invoked without an argument, present Telegram-native interactive controls rather than only plain text usage. Use the pinned go-telegram/bot SDK inline keyboard and callback query APIs; preserve /model provider/model for typed selection and enforce the existing sender allowlist on callbacks.

### Acceptance Criteria

An allowlisted user invoking /model receives an inline keyboard of configured models with the active model marked; tapping a model switches it through gateway.ModelManager, acknowledges the callback, and updates the message; unauthorized or malformed callbacks cannot switch models; empty model catalogs degrade safely.

title: Telegram: comprehensive truthful /help output
description:
The live /help response lists only /status and /help and still says LLM chat is not wired, despite the gateway supporting model, task, restart, and free-text chat paths. Replace the stale hardcoded copy with a complete, maintainable command guide that matches the registered menu and actual router behavior.

### Acceptance Criteria

/help describes every published command with accurate usage, includes free-text chat behavior, no longer claims chat is unwired, and a regression test fails if the published command menu and help surface drift.

title: Telegram: /restore to revert the last change
description:
Operator escape hatch requested alongside /restart: revert the last change from chat when an agent-authored change breaks something, without needing shell access to the host. Gateway-scoped.

### Acceptance Criteria

Admin-only (allowlisted sender). Reverts the last change and reports what was reverted. Safe to run when there is nothing to revert.

title: Telegram: /restart command to reload gateway config
description:
Operator escape hatch: restart the chat gateway from chat to pick up config changes (notably the allowlist) or recover from a wedged adapter, without shell access to the host.

### Acceptance Criteria

/restart is admin-only (allowlisted sender). Re-reads config and restarts the gateway. Replies with the outcome. In-flight agent tasks are not killed.

title: Telegram: register command menu via SetMyCommands
description:
The bot never calls SetMyCommands, so Telegram shows no command menu and the commands the Router implements (/status, /help, /models, /model, /spawn, /approve, /cancel) are undiscoverable. Asking the bot for /commands makes the LLM answer that it has none, which is wrong.

### Acceptance Criteria

SetMyCommands is called at startup with the commands the Router actually handles. Failure is logged, not fatal.

title: Telegram: allowlist senders, fail closed when unset
description:
telegram.New is called with a nil allowlist and isChatAllowed returns true when the allowlist is empty, so any Telegram user who finds the bot can talk to it. AllowedChatIDs is not plumbed into config at all. This gates exposing any real tools to the chat agent: with an MCP shell/filesystem server wired, allow-all becomes RCE for arbitrary senders.

### Acceptance Criteria

Allowlist is configurable via config.toml. Unset means deny, not allow. Sender identity (user id) is checked, not just chat id, so a group chat cannot be used to bypass it. Rejections are logged with the sender id. Startup logs loudly when the chat gateway is enabled with an empty allowlist.

title: Telegram: stream LLM replies via sendMessageDraft
description:
Chat replies currently block for the whole LLM turn, then arrive as one message. The typing indicator masks the wait but shows no progress. go-telegram/bot exposes SendMessageDraft (see examples/streaming_draft) and ai-sdk's runtime.ChatStream already returns core.StreamResult with a TextStream <-chan string, so both halves exist -- only the gateway seam is missing, since gateway.LLMResponder is func(ctx, Message) (string, error) and cannot emit partial output.

### Acceptance Criteria

Gateway exposes an optional streaming responder; Router falls back to the blocking path when unset. Telegram adapter streams deltas into a draft, then finalises with a formatted SendMessage. Draft updates are throttled to respect Telegram rate limits. Streaming failure falls back to a normal send rather than losing the reply.

title: Media utilities: cache, validate, deliver images/audio/video/documents
description:
Shared media utilities for handling images/audio/video/documents across platform adapters: download from the platform, validate (MIME type, size ceiling), cache to avoid re-fetching, and hand back a normalized reference the gateway can attach to a `MessageEvent` or deliver outbound.

### Context for implementers

No media file exists yet in `internal/gateway`. `MessageEvent` (`internal/gateway/messageevent.go`) is the shared event model this should plug into — check its current field set before adding a parallel media type. This is infrastructure other Gateway epic items depend on conceptually (any adapter method that sends/receives media, e.g. `archie-core-1786637493329-136-49b39c78` BasePlatformAdapter optional methods) but there is no formal `bd dep` between them yet.

### Acceptance Criteria

A shared utility validates MIME type and size before accepting media, caches downloaded media keyed by platform + media ID with TTL/size-bounded eviction, and exposes a normalized reference type usable from any adapter. Oversized or disallowed-MIME media is rejected with a caller-visible error, not silently dropped.

title: Code-fence-aware message truncation
description:
Truncate outbound messages to a platform's length limit (e.g. Telegram's 4096 chars) without ever cutting inside a ``` code fence — a truncation mid-fence leaves the rest of the message rendered as broken/unclosed markdown on the client.

### Context for implementers

No truncation helper exists yet in `internal/gateway`. This is distinct from the Markdown→HTML conversion trap documented in `CLAUDE.md` ("`EscapeMarkdown` does the *inverse* of formatting" / `go-telegram/bot`'s `SendRichMessage`) — that trap is about format conversion, this issue is about length-based cropping. Keep the two concerns separate: this helper should decide *where* to cut; rendering is a separate step.

### Acceptance Criteria

A message longer than the platform limit is truncated at a safe boundary: never inside an open code fence, preferring a paragraph/sentence boundary before the limit. If truncation would land inside a fence, the cut point backs up to before the fence opens (or the fence is closed and reopened on continuation, if multi-part delivery is in scope — confirm with the maintainer which behavior is wanted before implementing). Covered by a table-driven test with fenced and unfenced inputs at/over the limit.

title: TextBatchAggregator for rapid-fire text events
description:
Batch rapid-fire inbound text events from the same sender/channel into a single dispatch instead of invoking the agent loop once per fragment. Chat clients (Telegram in particular) often split a user's thought across several quick messages; dispatching each separately wastes a full agent turn per fragment and can interleave responses oddly.

### Context for implementers

No aggregator exists yet in `internal/gateway`. This sits upstream of the agent-loop dispatch, after platform adapters normalize events into `MessageEvent` (`internal/gateway/messageevent.go`) but before a turn is started (see `internal/gateway/turn.go`, `turns.go`).

### Acceptance Criteria

Text events from the same channel arriving within a short configurable window are coalesced into one aggregated event before dispatch. A single non-batched message is not delayed by more than the window. Aggregation window is configurable, not hardcoded. Covered by a test using an injected clock.

title: MessageDeduplicator with TTL-based dedup cache
description:
Prevent duplicate processing of the same platform message. At-least-once delivery (webhook retries, Telegram long-poll re-fetch after a slow ack, forge redelivery) can hand the gateway the same `MessageEvent` more than once; without a dedup layer it gets answered twice.

### Context for implementers

`internal/gateway/messageevent.go` already carries a platform-assigned `ID` field (`MessageEvent.ID`, see line ~59) suitable as a dedup key alongside `ChannelID`/`Platform`. There is currently no dedup file in `internal/gateway` — this is new code, not a rename. Related but distinct: `archie-core-ippu` (gateway: replay and redelivery lose tool activity) covers a different symptom — a replayed *turn* losing its tool-call history in the transcript, not a duplicate inbound message being processed twice. Fix this one first; it may reduce (but won't eliminate) triggers for the other.

### Acceptance Criteria

A `MessageDeduplicator` (or equivalent) keyed on platform + channel + message ID rejects a second delivery of the same message within a configurable TTL window. TTL expiry is covered by a test using an injected clock, not a real sleep. Memory use is bounded (LRU or TTL sweep), not an unbounded map.

title: SessionStore interface and implementation

MessageType enum for gateway messages
[EPIC] Gateway: rich message model, adapter lifecycle, session management
description:
Foundational gateway infrastructure to match Hermes parity. Three interdependent pieces:

1. **Message model**: Replace the 3-field Message struct with a rich MessageEvent (MessageType enum: text/photo/video/audio/voice/document/sticker/command, media_urls, reply_to context, metadata dict, source). This is the wire type every adapter produces.

2. **Adapter lifecycle**: Replace the 3-method Gateway interface with a BasePlatformAdapter interface: connect()/disconnect()/send() as required methods, plus optional overrides for typing indicators, edit/delete, image/voice/video/document send, interactive UX (clarify buttons, approval dialogs). Capability flags (supports_code_blocks, splits_long_messages, supports_async_delivery).

3. **Session management**: SessionSource struct (platform, chat_id, chat_type, user_id, thread_id, guild_id, profile), AsyncSessionStore for persistent session storage, SessionContext for system prompt injection.

All three blocks together enable adding new platforms as plugins without touching core gateway code.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md sections 1-2

### Acceptance Criteria

New adapters can be added by implementing a Go interface with connect/disconnect/send + optional media methods. Messages carry full metadata through the pipeline. Sessions persist across gateway restarts.
