title: Multi-agent collaboration: many agents working together
description:
Support multiple agents working in combination — not just one agent per task in isolation, but agents coordinating with each other (e.g. on the same repo, the same task, or a decomposed set of related tasks). Scope, coordination model, and conflict-avoidance strategy are all undefined — this is exploratory. No implementation approach has been decided yet.

### Acceptance Criteria

A PRD exists (docs/prds/) covering: what 'multiple agents working in combination' means concretely for archie-core, how agents discover/hand off work to each other, how conflicts (same repo, same worktree, shared state) are avoided or resolved, and what changes to daemon/workflow/dispatch are implied. No code changes required to close this epic — the PRD is the deliverable.

title: Evaluate internal/workflow architecture and APIs
description:
Perform a read-only, repository-grounded evaluation of internal/workflow. Identify correctness, definition clarity, reuse, interface ownership, coupling, testability, and maintainability improvements, with concrete evidence and prioritized recommendations.

### Acceptance Criteria

Assessment covers package definitions, consumers, subpackages, tests, and architecture invariants; findings are prioritized with file references and actionable recommendations; no code or git changes are made.

title: Regression tests: internal/gate — GateContext, Finding types, Yaegi evaluation
description: internal/gate/gate.go has zero tests. GateContext and Finding are the runtime types that custom gate scripts receive. The Yaegi evaluation path (gateeval) has tests, but the gate package itself has none. Add tests for type construction, finding validation, and integration with the gate evaluation pipeline.

title: Honcho memory engine as the external-provider proof
description:
Implement an engine backed by Honcho (plastic-labs/honcho, cloned at /work/clones/honcho) to prove the seam holds for a real external backend. Honcho's model is Workspace -> Peer -> Session -> Message with asynchronously derived conclusions queried back as representations; its dual-peer convention has the assistant observe others without self-modelling. Treat this as validation of the contract, not as a dependency of the default install.

### Acceptance Criteria

The engine satisfies the contract with no changes to the agent loop or gateway. Archie runs unchanged when it is not configured. Its network calls carry timeouts and its failures degrade to reported errors rather than failing a turn. Any mapping decision between Archie sessions/identities and Honcho peers/sessions is documented. Unit tests use httptest and never require a live Honcho instance, per the repo testing rule.
close_reason: Deprioritized by Sam (2026-09-02): not a current priority. Re-open when there's actual appetite to build against a live Honcho instance -- the engine contract it would implement against (domain/memory.MemoryEngine) is done and stable, so this is unblocked whenever picked back up, not superseded by anything.

title: feat(gateway): durable message deduplication via upstream IDs
description: gateway.Message carries no upstream/channel-native message ID, so a re-delivered Telegram update appends a duplicate turn. Add Message.ID and derive the NellDB document ID from it (time-prefixed to preserve the ScanSince ID tie-break), making redelivery an idempotent LWW upsert.

title: feat(gateway): version the SQLite session schema before cutover
description:
OpenSQLiteSessionStore currently runs CREATE IF NOT EXISTS statements with no schema version or transactional migration record. Before production wiring, add the smallest deterministic schema-version mechanism so future upgrades cannot silently leave a partially evolved database.

### Acceptance Criteria

A fresh database records the current schema version; opening a supported older fixture migrates transactionally and preserves data; unsupported newer versions fail with an actionable error; migration failure leaves the prior schema/data usable; schema initialization and upgrades are covered by file-backed tests.

title: test(gateway): pin SQLite FTS lifecycle and literal-query semantics
description:
Trigger-driven FTS synchronization and hostile-query escaping were manually verified but are not retained by the trimmed SQLite-specific test suite. Preserve these SQLite-specific guarantees without duplicating the shared SessionStore contract.

### Acceptance Criteria

Table-driven tests show FTS search/count remains correct after message deletion, ReplaceMessages, and session deletion with no cross-session leak; hostile inputs including column syntax, unmatched quotes, NEAR, wildcard, and boolean operators return literal-match behavior without syntax errors; multi-term queries pin AND semantics; tests stay SQLite-specific and focused.

title: fix(gateway): round-trip SourceID through every SessionStore backend
description:
SQLite persists and returns Message.SourceID, but the NellDB adapter derives MessageID from SourceID and then discards SourceID from the stored document. External correlation metadata therefore changes across backend selection and cannot be exported from NellDB during migration.

### Acceptance Criteria

The shared conformance suite requires SourceID to round-trip without becoming the canonical MessageID; NellDB persists and reads source_id with empty-field compatibility for older records; SQLite remains conformant; redelivery deduplication and immutable content semantics remain unchanged.

title: fix(gateway): align newest-session ordering across SessionStore backends
description:
SQLite List/GetByChannel order by created_at, while NellDB orders by latest document write/HLC. Touching or re-saving a session can therefore select a different active session after a backend cutover even though both pass the shared suite. Pin one observable newest-session contract and make both adapters satisfy it.

### Acceptance Criteria

The shared conformance suite covers multiple sessions with distinct CreatedAt and LastActiveAt values plus Touch/re-save; List and GetByChannel return the same deterministic order on NellDB and SQLite; restart-style resolution selects the same session on both backends; indexes support the chosen SQLite ordering.

title: test(gateway): prove SQLite session rollback and reopen durability
description:
The SQLite SessionStore uses real transactions and WAL, but current tests only verify successful operations through the same open handle. Add adversarial file-backed tests that prove persisted session/message state survives close+reopen and that injected failures during Delete and ReplaceMessages roll the transaction and FTS index back to the original state.

### Acceptance Criteria

A file-backed store is closed and reopened with sessions, canonical MessageID, SourceID, text, sender, and timestamps intact; PRAGMA quick_check returns ok; deterministic abort triggers force mid-Delete and mid-ReplaceMessages failures; after each failure the original session, history, counts, and search results remain unchanged; focused and race tests pass.

title: feat(gateway): migrate canonical session/message store to SQLite
description:
docs/architecture/messaging-and-work-intake.md:107 requires the canonical session and message implementation to supply durable SQLite round trips. The current store is NellDB-backed.

Scope is the SETTLED parts of the messaging architecture only:
- SQLite persistence (modernc.org/sqlite; FTS5 verified available at 3.53.3, no CGo)
- application-generated canonical MessageID, platform IDs as correlation only (doc 88-90)
- immutable message records (doc 112-114)
- append-only linear sequence per conversation (doc 128)
- real transactions for ReplaceMessages and Delete

Explicitly OUT of scope: the rich typed-content / tool-call / tool-result model and delivery-attempt semantics. docs/architecture/messaging-and-work-intake.md:273-284 lists the canonical inbound message model, source-correlation model, and outbound delivery/retry/dedup semantics as DECISIONS STILL REQUIRED, so they are not specified enough to implement. That work belongs to archie-core-abg.16.

Decision by Sam 2026-08-03 after the third review surfaced that the NellDB-vs-SQLite question was already settled by the architecture docs.

title: fix(gateway): /compress argument dispatch is wrong in three ways
description:
session_commands.go:460-478, all CONFIRMED by execution:

1. Bare /compress can never apply. isPreview is 'len(fields) == 0 || --preview || --dry-run', so /compress with no arguments takes the preview branch -- and compressPreview ends with 'Run /compress to apply'. The command tells the user to run a command that does nothing, forever. The failure-safe ReplaceMessages path added by archie-core-0ua is unreachable via the documented command; only '/compress here <N>' reaches it.

2. /compress focus <topic> silently ignores the topic. focus is validated for arity only; cfg is never modified, so it runs a full default compression and reports success. Irreversible history rewrite from a command the user believes does something narrower.

3. /compress here (no N) and any unrecognised argument (/compress asdf) fall through to a full default compression rather than printing usage, unlike the sibling focus branch.

title: Curator runtime: persistent loop with idle cooldown
description:
Implement the loop that runs a registered curator: continuous operation while work is available, backing off to a configured cooldown when there is nothing to do, waking on new input, and honouring per-curator check-in intervals.

### Acceptance Criteria

A curator with pending input runs without waiting for its next interval; an idle curator consumes no meaningful CPU and wakes on new input. Cooldown and check-in interval are configurable per curator. Loop timing is tested with a fake clock, not wall-clock sleeps. Shutdown is clean and bounded: an in-flight curator pass is cancelled via context and the daemon does not block indefinitely on it. A panicking curator is recovered and isolated from other curators and from the agent loop.
close_reason: Complete: internal/domain/curator/runtime.go implements exactly this. Verified against every acceptance-criteria clause: pending-input curators run without waiting for the interval (TestRuntimeWakeRunsPendingPassImmediately), idle curators sleep until interval (TestRuntimeIdleCuratorSleepsUntilInterval) with a configurable per-curator cooldown (TestRuntimeCooldownAfterIdlePass, TestRuntimeNextCheckInOverride), all timed via an injected fake clock not wall-clock sleep, shutdown is context-bounded (TestRuntimeShutdownCancelsInFlightPass, TestRuntimeShutdownBoundedDespiteStuckPass), and panics are recovered and isolated (TestRuntimeCheckPanicRecovered, TestRuntimePassPanicRecovered). go test ./internal/domain/curator/... -race -count=1 is fully green.

title: test(gateway): the conformance suite does not pin what it claims, and the backends already drift
description:
The commit message for 3eb00db claims the shared suite means NellDB and SQLite 'cannot drift'. Two confirmed divergences it does not catch:

1. testReplaceMessagesIsFailureSafe (sessionstore_conformance_test.go:769) never induces a failure -- four happy-path cases asserting the post-condition of a SUCCESSFUL call. Swapping the write and delete loops in session_store.go:696-708 would leave it green. Only SQLite has a real abort test, and it pins rollback, the opposite failure mode. The backends genuinely differ here: SQLite is atomic (failure -> clean rollback), NellDB is not (failure -> duplicates). SQLite's semantics are better; the point is the suite does not know.

2. NellDB's lastTS cache is never invalidated by deletes; SQLite recomputes MAX(ts). Save at 13:00, delete it, save with At=12:00 -> NellDB persists 13:00:00.001Z, SQLite persists 12:00:00Z. Both pass the suite.

3. GetByChannel ordering differs between backends and is unpinned (see the newest-first bead).

4. applyCompress has zero test coverage: no test in the package calls it, none of its three error returns is exercised, and fakeSessionStore.ReplaceMessages is a slice assignment that cannot observe ordering or identity.

title: fix(gateway): session resolution is not newest-first, so restart resumes a stale session
description:
Found independently by two reviewers, CONFIRMED by execution.

sessionTracker.resolve (session_commands.go:54-59) comments 'Find the most recent session matching this thread and bot' but returns the first element GetByChannel yields. The wired-up NellDB store returns document-ID order (listAllLocked reverses AllDocs, which sorts by document ID), i.e. UUID-lexicographic -- effectively random. LastActiveAt is populated on every record and never consulted.

Scenario: user runs /new 'old', chats, runs /new 'current'; daemon restarts (the tracker cache is in-memory only); the next message resolves to whichever session sorts first. Probed over 10 runs: 4 landed in the OLDER session, answering against pre-/new history. This is the user-visible lost-context class.

Also a silent backend divergence: SQLite's GetByChannel orders created_at DESC, NellDB does not, and the shared conformance suite does not pin it. Separately, SessionStore.List's doc comment (session_store.go:34-36) promises newest-first and does not deliver: saving zzz-oldest, aaa-middle, mmm-newest returns [zzz-oldest mmm-newest aaa-middle].

Blocks archie-core-b4i and archie-core-gih.

title: Daemon: every task/event write fails with 'sdk: revision conflict' after NellDB v0.3.0 bump — counter RMW permanently broken
description:
## Symptom (observed 2026-08-05, task dev session)

- Every 1m poll logs `issue queued` for the same open issue (sam/archie-core#8) again.
- Every attempt logs `event sink insert failed: err="sdk: revision conflict"` (cmd/archied/main.go:373, the event-sink goroutine calling st.InsertEvent).
- The daemon's own task consumer logs `nats enqueue failed: err="sdk: revision conflict"` (internal/daemon/daemon.go:599, calling Store.EnqueueIssue) and NAKs; JetStream redelivers to max-deliver 3 (triples of errors every ~2 min in the log).
- The task doc is never persisted, so the enqueue dedup check always passes and the poll re-queues forever. Work never reaches the agent; dashboard shows a stuck/no-op task.

## Exact cause

Commit 44f914c bumped github.com/samcharles93/NellDB v0.2.5 -> v0.3.0 touching only go.mod/go.sum. v0.3.0 changed the DocDB rev-cache rebuild:

- v0.2.5 sdk/docdb.go reindex() indexed EVERY record by rec.ID, including Archie's meta:task_id_counter / meta:event_id_counter docs.
- v0.3.0 sdk/docdb.go reindex() skips any id where isInternalID() is true (sdk/replicate.go:841: id[:5] == "meta:"), intended only for the SDK's own meta:clock/meta:vector bookkeeping but prefix-matching Archie's counter docs too.
- v0.3.0 putIn (sdk/docdb.go:208-216) keeps the same conflict rule as v0.2.5: incomingRev != "" && !exists -> sdk.ErrConflict.

Archie's Adapter.nextCounter (internal/nell/adapter.go:957) is a Get -> mutate -> Put RMW that supplies the _rev returned by Get (joinDoc copies the payload, which putIn re-stamps with _rev). After any restart the counter docs are present in the log but absent from the rev cache, so exists=false and every counter Put conflicts. The counter doc can never be written again, so the cache is never repopulated — the failure is permanent for the lifetime of the DB, every process run, from the first poll.

Repro (standalone, module cache, v0.3.0): open log, Put meta:task_id_counter, close, reopen, Get (rev e.g. "1-69bfa51d..."), Put with that rev -> "sdk: revision conflict". First run of a fresh DB succeeds (empty-rev init Put is allowed); every subsequent process restart fails.

Why tests are green: OpenMemory/fresh-log tests initialize the counter via empty-rev Put within the same process; TestPersistenceAcrossRestart reopens a real log but only reads (TaskByIssue) and never exercises the counter RMW after reopen. The production path (restart an existing log, then enqueue) is untested.

## Evidence

- go.mod: github.com/samcharles93/NellDB v0.3.0 (no replace).
- git show 44f914c --stat: go.mod, go.sum, .gitignore only; internal/nell/ untouched since.
- Module cache diff !nell!d!b@v0.2.5 vs @v0.3.0: sdk/docdb.go reindex()/putIn(), sdk/replicate.go isInternalID.
- /tmp/nell-repro: deterministic ErrConflict on counter RMW after reopen.

## Fix direction

Options, in order of preference: (1) pin back to v0.2.5 (verified-2026-07-28 semantics) until adapter is migrated; (2) stop supplying _rev in nextCounter (drop rev from the RMW doc before Put — v0.3.0 continues the chain from the cached rev when incomingRev == ""), but that breaks the MVCC chain for the counter when the cache lacks it; (3) upstream: isInternalID should match exact SDK ids (meta:clock, meta:vector), not the meta: prefix, or reindex should index meta docs. Any fix must add a red test: open persisted log, EnqueueIssue, reopen, EnqueueIssue again -> no conflict.

title: Restore a clean repository-wide golangci-lint baseline
description:
Repository-wide golangci-lint currently reports 39 pre-existing findings (32 errcheck and 7 staticcheck) across NATS/RPC/container code and older tests. Remediate the findings without weakening lint configuration so golangci-lint run ./... is a reliable required gate.

### Acceptance Criteria

golangci-lint run ./... exits successfully with no findings; affected cleanup/error paths handle or explicitly document ignored errors; existing race tests remain green.

title: Remove source-project references from Archie
description:
Remove every tau reference outside the explicitly preserved Beads data and docs-2/README.md. Delete copied product-specific documentation and accompanied rationale rather than mechanically renaming it. Retain reusable documentation-generation and VitePress scaffolding only after removing source-specific coupling. Update code, tests, archives, and architecture documents so archie-core contains no unauthorized tau references.

### Acceptance Criteria

rg 'tau' -ow excluding .beads/** and docs-2/README.md returns zero; retained tools and documentation scaffolding contain no source-project imports, paths, product claims, or rationale; relevant validation passes.

title: Telegram rejects model confirmation when clearing inline keyboard
description:
Selecting a model calls editMessageText with a typed nil reply_markup; Telegram rejects it as object expected, leaving the picker visible. Omit reply_markup when no keyboard is required and cover the request shape.

### Acceptance Criteria

Selecting any model replaces the picker with metadata confirmation and the Telegram edit request omits reply_markup when clearing controls.

title: fix(gateway): a message arriving mid-/compress is destroyed
description:
applyCompress reads MessageCount then RecentMessages, and ReplaceMessages later removes everything outside the replacement set. A chat turn that lands between the read and the replace is deleted, never summarised.

CONFIRMED executed on both backends: 'nell: mid-compress inbound message destroyed (stored=24)', 'sqlite: ... (stored=24)'. NellDB deletes it via the AllDocs snapshot; SQLite via DELETE ... WHERE message_id NOT IN (survivors), a survivor-complement.

archie-core-0ua's guarantee (worst case is recoverable duplicates) does not cover this: it is unrecoverable loss, and the store-level fix cannot address it because the window is in the caller. Nothing serialises /compress against an inbound turn.

title: config.docker.toml missing required fields, no overlay merge implemented
description: config.docker.toml was rewritten to be a docs-as-overlay file (comment says base+overlay merge) but internal/config.Load has no merge logic and docker-compose.yml mounts only config.docker.toml at /etc/archie/config.toml. It is missing bot_user, [forge], [dispatch], [models], [providers], [budgets] which Load requires -> daemon fails to start in docker as currently configured. Implement real base+overlay config loading (or restore a full standalone docker config) so there is one source of truth.

title: Seed a default SOUL without clobbering user edits
description:
Write a starter SOUL on first run and allow upgrading untouched scaffolding in place, following Hermes' is_legacy_template_soul approach: compare normalised content against known-shipped templates, which carry zero user intent, and only replace on an exact match.

### Acceptance Criteria

First run seeds a documented starter SOUL. A SOUL matching a known shipped template can be upgraded in place. A SOUL the user has edited in any way is never modified. Comparison normalises line endings and trailing whitespace so a CRLF checkout does not defeat it.

title: Register storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc servers in archied startup
description:
Depends on the TaskContext interface refactor. cmd/archied/main.go builds the Daemon with Store/Forge/Trees but never registers the storerpc.Server/forgerpc.Server/worktreerpc.Server handlers, so archie-agent's RPC calls currently have no responder in production. Wire all three Register(nc) calls into archied's startup when cfg.NATS is configured, alongside the existing NATS client connect.

### Acceptance Criteria

When [nats] is configured, archied subscribes to all storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc subjects at startup; an archie-agent container can successfully call Store/Forge/worktree operations against a running archied.

title: daemon.go: hand off whole task to archie-agent in sandboxed NATS+container mode
description:
Depends on the archie-agent full-task handler existing. internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() currently always calls workflow.Route/workflow.Run itself, dispatching per-stage LLM calls to d.Agent (NATSRunner does this over NATS today). When d.Nats != nil && d.ContainerPool != nil (the sandboxed path this whole PRD phase targets), process() should instead publish one 'run whole task' message to archie-agent and await its completion report, skipping local workflow.Route/workflow.Run entirely. inprocess/subprocess modes (no container pool) keep calling workflow.Run in the daemon exactly as today — this only changes behavior for the fully-sandboxed path.

### Acceptance Criteria

With containers enabled, daemon.process() delegates the entire task to archie-agent in one round trip; without containers, behavior is unchanged (verified by existing daemon tests continuing to pass).

title: archie-agent: run full task (workflow.Route + workflow.Run) via RPC-backed TaskContext
description:
The actual stage-loop move for archie-core-5zh, depending on the TaskConfig payload and TaskContext interface refactor. cmd/archie-agent gains a handler for a new 'run whole task' NATS message (task summary + TaskConfig + repo config, no secrets). On receipt it: builds its own workflow.Registry via skillbuild.BuildRegistry against its mounted worktree (/data/worktree — same pattern the daemon already uses, no registry needs to cross the wire); calls workflow.Route itself; builds a TaskContext using storerpc.Client (Store), forgerpc.Client (Forge), and a hybrid Trees (worktreerpc.Client for Prepare/Push, a local *worktree.Manager with no token for CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines against the bind-mounted dir); calls workflow.Run; reports completion once instead of round-tripping per stage.

### Acceptance Criteria

When agent.mode=nats and containers are enabled, archie-agent runs an entire task's workflow (all stages) per invocation, not one stage per round trip; inprocess/subprocess modes are unaffected.

title: TaskContext interface refactor: Forge/Store/Trees as trimmed interfaces
description:
Groundwork for archie-core-5zh.4. workflow.TaskContext currently types Forge/Store/Trees as concrete daemon types (forge.Forge interface already, *store.Store, *worktree.Manager). Define trimmed interfaces in internal/workflow scoped to exactly the methods stages call (Forge: Comment/CloseIssue/CreatePR/SetStateLabel; Store: Update/Transition; Trees: Prepare/CommitAll/Push/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines) so storerpc.Client, forgerpc.Client, and a worktreerpc-backed implementation can satisfy them from inside archie-agent, while *store.Store/*worktree.Manager and the real forge.Forge implementations keep satisfying them unchanged for the daemon's existing inprocess/subprocess paths.

### Acceptance Criteria

TaskContext.Forge/Store/Trees are interface-typed; daemon.go compiles and all existing tests pass unchanged (concrete types satisfy the new interfaces structurally); no behavior change for inprocess/subprocess modes.

title: Curated TaskConfig payload for archie-agent (no secrets)
description:
Groundwork for archie-core-5zh.4. workflow.TaskContext.Cfg (config.Config) is read throughout stages (Models, Budgets, Dispatch incl. label mapping, DiffCapLines, Notify.Webhook, Forge.Host) but the full Config also carries forge/NATS credentials that must never enter the agent container. Add a config.TaskConfig struct — same field names/shapes as the subset config.Config exposes (Models, Budgets, Dispatch, DiffCapLines, Notify, Forge) — with json tags, plus a constructor (e.g. config.Config.ForTask()) that builds it from the daemon's live config. Add json tags to config.Repo's remaining fields (only AllowConcurrent has them today) since tc.Repo also needs to cross the wire.

### Acceptance Criteria

config.TaskConfig marshals/unmarshals via JSON and carries exactly the fields workflow stages read; no token/credential field is reachable from it; config.Repo fully round-trips through JSON.

title: Move workflow.Route/workflow.Run stage loop into archie-agent
description:
Final step of archie-core-5zh, depends on the Store/Forge/push RPC proxies existing. Move workflow.Route + workflow.Run's stage-loop execution from internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() into cmd/archie-agent, using the RPC proxies for Store/Forge/push and reimplementing CustomStages discovery (wfeval.Discover) agent-side against the already-mounted worktree. daemon.process() keeps worktree prepare + container acquire/release, then hands off the whole task to archie-agent in one NATS round trip instead of one round trip per stage.

### Acceptance Criteria

workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied, when agent.mode=nats; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation; inprocess/subprocess modes keep working unchanged.

title: Move workflow.Route/workflow.Run stage loop into archie-agent
description:
Final step of archie-core-5zh, depends on the Store/Forge/push RPC proxies existing. Move workflow.Route + workflow.Run's stage-loop execution from internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() into cmd/archie-agent, using the RPC proxies for Store/Forge/push and reimplementing CustomStages discovery (wfeval.Discover) agent-side against the already-mounted worktree. daemon.process() keeps worktree prepare + container acquire/release, then hands off the whole task to archie-agent in one NATS round trip instead of one round trip per stage.

### Acceptance Criteria

workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied, when agent.mode=nats; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation; inprocess/subprocess modes keep working unchanged.
close_reason: Stale/duplicate: exact duplicate of already-closed archie-core-1786637491429-62-088b752f (GH #83, created 3 min later, closed within 2s — accidental double-create). Also independently verified complete: internal/daemon/daemon.go:882-893 already hands sandboxed tasks to archie-agent in one NATS round trip via runViaAgent instead of a per-stage loop, and internal/app/agentworker/task_execution.go:85,143,146 calls workflow.Route/workflow.Run with wfeval.Discover agent-side, matching the acceptance criteria verbatim. inprocess/subprocess path (daemon.go:894+) is untouched, as required.

title: Worktree push RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for git push
description:
Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. worktree.Manager.Push needs the forge HTTPS push token (held daemon-side, used via an askpass helper). Trees.Prepare/CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines are local git operations against the already-mounted worktree and can run agent-side unchanged (containers already bind-mount /data/worktree) — only Push needs to be proxied back to the daemon, which holds the credential.

### Acceptance Criteria

archie-agent can request a git push over NATS; archied performs the authenticated push using its held token and replies with success/failure; the push token is never sent to or stored in the agent container.

title: Forge RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for forge API calls
description:
Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. Stages call Forge.SetStateLabel/Comment/CreatePR/CloseIssue/CreateIssue/React/RepliesAfter mid-workflow. Forge holds live API tokens (Gitea/GitHub) that must stay daemon-side per the PRD's 'daemon never runs untrusted code, owns all secrets' boundary. Once workflow.Run moves into archie-agent, these calls need to become NATS request/reply RPCs to the daemon rather than shipping forge credentials into the agent container.

### Acceptance Criteria

archie-agent can invoke the forge.Forge interface methods used by workflow stages over NATS; archied executes them against the real forge client and replies; no forge API tokens are present in the agent container.

title: Store RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for task state mutations
description:
Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. workflow.Run calls tc.Store.Update every stage and tc.Store.Transition on terminal outcomes — Store wraps a direct SQLite *sql.DB handle that only the daemon owns. Once workflow.Run moves into archie-agent, these calls need to become NATS request/reply RPCs to the daemon (the sole DB owner), reusing the existing AgentRequestMessage/reply-inbox plumbing pattern (internal/agentexec/nats.go) rather than giving the agent container direct DB access.

### Acceptance Criteria

archie-agent can call Store.Update and Store.Transition equivalents over NATS; archied executes them against SQLite and replies; no direct DB access from the agent container.

title: Promote archie-agent to per-task process; move workflow routing out of archied
description:
cmd/archie-agent exists but only executes one workflow stage per invocation over the internal/agentexec stdin/stdout JSON protocol (v1). Phase 1 of the PRD requires promoting it to the PRD's per-task process model, moving workflow.Route/workflow.Run out of archied and into archie-agent.

### Acceptance Criteria

workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation.

title: Disable automatic forge comments and state labels
description: Remove automatic plan/progress/retry/dead/state-label noise from normal execution. Preserve internal logs/events and retain only comments explicitly required by an operator decision flow, exposed through messaging or Web UI.

title: Document Hermes capabilities missing from Archie
description: Investigate Hermes' available features and commands, compare them with Archie, and publish a simple Markdown TODO checklist excluding Kanban.

title: Configuration boundary and ownership review
description:
Run the first focused architecture campaign for the configuration refactor. Trace the current TOML/YAML loaders, defaults, validation, overlays, secret references, identity/repository settings, worker snapshots, container/NATS passthrough, and every production consumer. Produce a field-level current-to-target ownership ledger and decide the smallest behavior-preserving migration slice. Do not edit runtime code until ownership, input DTO boundaries, provenance requirements, schema generation boundary, compatibility semantics, and deletion criteria are recorded.

### Acceptance Criteria

A reproducible current-state trace covers entrypoints, loaders, consumers, process boundaries, tests, deployment passthrough, and decoded-but-unwired fields; every in-scope setting has one current owner, target owner, scope, validation/provenance behavior, and migration disposition; base/overlay and secret compatibility semantics are explicit; the first implementation slice has an observable outcome, bounded change cone, parity tests, rollback, and deletion criterion; no unresolved semantic decision is left for the implementer to invent.

title: Docsgen: emit deterministic contract data JSON
description:
Begin the generated-documentation implementation with the smallest vertical slice: normalize the existing Archie contract schemas into deterministic JSON under docs-2/data/generated for VitePress consumption, without generating Markdown pages. Preserve the nested tools module and existing source-of-truth imports.

### Acceptance Criteria

A failing test first proves docsgen emits valid generated JSON at the data path; repeated generation is byte-identical; tools tests and vet pass; generated-documentation.md reflects the agreed data-loader architecture.

title: Define target project organisation and restructuring rules
description:
Run a package-by-package architecture grilling session, establish the target DDD and semi-microservice organisation, record strict restructuring requirements and package destinations, and produce docs/prds/01-project-management.md as the durable handoff.

### Acceptance Criteria

The PRD records agreed project-wide organisation rules, bounded-context and service/plugin boundaries, dependency constraints, migration principles, and the destination of each reviewed package. Decisions are confirmed one at a time with the user before the document is finalized.

title: install.sh delegates config generation to archied setup
description:
Remove the TOML-generating branches from install.sh and call the binary it just built. Ends the class of bug where the installer's idea of the config schema drifts from the daemon's.

### Acceptance Criteria

install.sh contains no TOML templates and no sed-patching of config files. It invokes archied setup for a fresh install and skips it when a config already exists. A non-interactive install still produces a valid config or fails loudly. The forge_block helper and its awk splice are deleted.

title: Enforce typed plugin engine architecture rule
description:
Cement the repository invariant that a plugin engine is a typed capability family with an owning registry/manager and lifecycle semantics, never a generic daemon hook. Add one canonical architecture rule referenced by both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, record it in Beads memory, and add an executable architecture test that prevents drift without touching the concurrently edited secret/config packages.

### Acceptance Criteria

A canonical rule defines typed domain contract, owning registry/manager, lifecycle and health expectations, narrow host access, and trust boundaries; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md both surface the rule through their shared source; an architecture test fails for generic plugin-hook expansion or an engine interface without a family manager; focused tests and task check pass; fresh adversarial review has no surviving findings.

title: Port tau internal/indexing (codesearch) into archie-core
description:
First slice of the tau cherry-pick strategy. Copy-and-mutate (NOT extract to pkg/ - Sam's decision: exporting would force designing metrics/session/logger seams upfront before archie-core knows which it wants differently).

tau/internal/indexing is the cheapest high-value lift: 512 LoC, one file, and its only tau coupling is 3 calls to config.WorkspaceIndexDir()/WorkspaceIndexDBPath(). Nothing else in tau imports it.

Mutations: replace the global config path helpers with explicit constructor params (archie-core passes config, no globals); add the workspace-codesearch helper subcommand to archied since the manager deliberately runs google/codesearch in a child process (upstream fatal exits + mmap leaks must not kill the daemon).

Each lifted file carries a provenance header (source path + tau commit) so a future refresh is a diff, not archaeology.

title: Gateway: unknown slash commands must not reach the LLM
description:
Unknown slash commands currently fall through to free-text LLM chat, causing fabricated command behavior such as /memories claims and false statements about files or model identity. Make slash command recognition deterministic and answer unknown commands locally with guidance to /help, while preserving free-text chat and supported Telegram bootstrap commands.

### Acceptance Criteria

Any unrecognized leading slash command is answered locally and never invokes or streams from the LLM. The reply identifies the command as unknown and points to /help. Recognized commands and ordinary free text retain existing behavior. Telegram /start has an explicit deterministic behavior. Tests cover unknown commands with arguments and @gateway mentions, streaming routing, /start, and LLM non-invocation.
close_reason: Verified against current main: Route/RouteStream reject unrecognized slash commands before any LLM call (gateway.go:299-318, 449-462), /start is deterministic in both gateway and Telegram handlers, and full test matrix from acceptance criteria exists (gateway_test.go:106-133, gateway_stream_test.go:54-88, telegram_test.go:135-157). Confirmed by fresh code-tracing pass, not just prior user experience.

title: [EPIC] SOUL file: user-authored agent identity
description:
Move Archie's identity and tone out of compiled Go constants and into a user-editable SOUL file. Root cause of a real defect on 2026-07-29: heyarchie answered 'Hey are you there?' with 'I'm here. What do you need?', which reads as demanding the user justify getting in touch. The fix required editing DefaultPersonas() in internal/gateway/persona.go and rebuilding -- personality is not tunable without a compile. Modelled on Hermes (SOUL.md occupies the identity slot in the stable tier, DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY is the fallback when absent, re-read per message so no restart is needed) and openclaw, which injects SOUL.md alongside AGENTS.md.

### Design

THE BOUNDARY IS THE POINT. The existing layering rule (recorded in the chat-system-prompt-design memory) is that PersonaRegistry is the style layer only and rules live in the template, so switching persona cannot strip the agent's rules or tool inventory. SOUL inherits exactly that constraint: it owns identity, name, register and warmth, and must not be able to touch core_rules -- otherwise 'be terse' in a SOUL silently disarms the no-fabrication rules. Steal from Hermes: is_legacy_template_soul upgrades untouched scaffolding in place but never overwrites a SOUL the user actually edited. This is the first of the three identity layers agreed with Sam on 2026-07-30: invariants (template, nobody edits at runtime) / SOUL (user-authored) / representation (curator-derived, proposes only).

### Acceptance Criteria

A user can name their agent and define its personality by editing a file, with no rebuild and no restart. An absent or empty SOUL falls back to the shipped default identity. SOUL cannot weaken the invariants: <instruction_precedence>, <core_rules>, the <tools> block and <env> stay in the template and remain unreachable from SOUL, enforced by a test. A SOUL the user has customised is never overwritten by an upgrade.

title: Make Archie the user-facing identity
description:
Remove internal gateway terminology from Telegram replies and establish an Archie default system prompt so chat does not drift into generic assistant identity.

### Acceptance Criteria

Telegram help and restart copy call the assistant Archie; default chat persona identifies Archie and forbids unverified claims or vendor impersonation; tests and task check pass.

title: worktree.Manager gets an empty token when the forge degrades
description:
Since 518a1a0 a missing forge credential disables the forge instead of stopping archied. resolveForge returns an empty token in that case and cmd/archied/main.go still hands it to worktree.Manager{Token: token}. If repos are configured while the forge is disabled, clone/push fails at push time rather than at startup. This is the intended trade -- a deferred error beats a crash loop -- but the failure is currently discovered late and its message will not explain that the cause is an unconfigured forge.

### Acceptance Criteria

A worktree operation attempted with no forge credential fails with a message naming the missing forge configuration as the cause, rather than a bare git transport error. Alternatively the manager refuses the operation up front. Either way the operator can tell why from the error alone.

title: Expose quiet execution and decision controls in messaging and Web UI
description: Make the no-comment/no-label behavior and human approval or retry decisions controllable through existing messaging channels and the Web UI. Do not reintroduce issue comments as the control plane; show the same persisted task state and actions in both surfaces.

title: MCP servers are re-fetched from npm on every daemon start
description:
config.docker.toml launches desktop-commander with 'npx -y @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander@0.2.46'. The container has no persistent npm cache, so every restart re-resolves and re-downloads the package and its puppeteer browser payload. That is slow, makes startup depend on npm registry availability, and turns a registry outage or a yanked version into a daemon outage. It also amplified the crash loop observed on 2026-07-30, since each restart repeated the whole download.

### Acceptance Criteria

Daemon startup does not depend on reaching the npm registry. Either the MCP servers are installed into the image at build time and invoked directly, or the npm cache is persisted across restarts. Startup time no longer scales with the size of the server's dependency tree.
notes: Not fixed in code, but operationally contained: CLAUDE.md now states 'No npx-launched servers are configured in production anyway -- the builtin tools (read, write, edit, find, grep, shell) and web_fetch.' Confirmed no persistent-cache or build-time-install mechanism exists in internal/tools/provider/provider.go. If an operator adds an npx-based MCP server back, this bug reproduces exactly as described. Fix is still the structural one (build-time install or persisted cache), not just avoiding the config -- don't close this on the operational workaround alone.
close_reason: Fixed: configuredMCPProvider (cmd/archied/main.go) now sets NPM_CONFIG_CACHE under the daemon's persistent work_dir and NPM_CONFIG_PREFER_OFFLINE=true for any npx-launched MCP server (matched by base name so an absolute-path npx still qualifies), so a daemon restart reuses a warm npm cache instead of re-resolving/re-downloading from the registry every time -- the amplifier behind the 2026-07-30 crash loop. Guards an empty workDir explicitly (unreachable in production since config defaulting runs first, but matches memoryProvider's existing precedent for the same defense). Adversarially reviewed by a fresh subagent; findings addressed: narrowed an overclaim that this also covers a package's own separate downloads (e.g. Playwright/Puppeteer fetching browser binaries via CDN, which NPM_CONFIG_CACHE does not touch), and closed the absolute-path-command gap. Full task check clean. The identical, arguably-worse instance in internal/app/agentworker/mcp_providers.go (every per-task ephemeral container, not just daemon restarts) needs real new infra -- a persistent Docker volume bind-mounted into task containers, which doesn't exist yet -- so it's filed separately as archie-core-qk8m rather than folded into this scoped fix.

title: Web Chat: expose provider-aware active model and personality selectors
description:
Make the Web Chat selector state match Telegram: expose the active model/provider and the active personality for the current Web session, group models by provider when the manager supports it, and render those states in the UI. Preserve graceful fallback for managers without provider metadata.

### Design

Use the existing ModelManager, ProviderModelManager, and PersonaRegistry contracts. Keep the existing models/personas fields backward compatible while adding structured provider/active fields.

### Acceptance Criteria

Sessions API returns active model/provider data and current-session personality state; provider-aware model options are grouped and selectable; selecting a provider/model/personality updates the shared gateway state; focused Go and UI/browser tests cover active and fallback states.

title: Make activity and task context navigable
description: The dashboard's live activity entries are not clickable, task detail does not provide a source-task/forge link, and the Tasks KPI strip sits directly against the table. Make activity events navigate to the relevant dashboard area, expose a clear source task action that opens the task's forge page when available, and restore visual separation between KPI cards and the task table. Add focused UI/runtime tests.

title: Discover user-installed global skills alongside project skills
description: The Web UI currently scans only the daemon work directory, so skills installed under the user's global ~/.agents/skills are invisible. Add global-skill discovery alongside project skills, preserve deterministic precedence for duplicate names, expose source/path in the API/UI, and keep workflow activation using the same merged catalogue. Add tests for configured and default roots.

title: Restore compliance with the approved Archie visual design
description: The current dashboard does not follow the supplied reference design. Rework the shell and page composition around the reference: a framed rounded workspace, compact top navigation, prominent welcome/header area, adjacent primary actions, getting-started panel, prominent status/compliance visualization, compact KPI strip with trend marks, forecast/projection panel, and live-runs table. Match the reference visual treatment: layered rounded surfaces, soft translucent panels, luminous abstract background treatment, compact information-dense cards, restrained status colours, and consistent icon/action placement. Do not reinterpret this as a generic dark admin console or as a light editorial marketing page. Capture desktop and narrow-viewport visual evidence before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add accessible interaction semantics across the dashboard
description: Source review found navigation icons and a theme toggle that depend on visual glyphs or title text, and task rows are clickable table rows without keyboard semantics or an explicit expandable control. Audit the main pages for labels, focus visibility, keyboard operation, semantic headings and table behavior, status announcements, and sufficient non-color cues. Add automated DOM/accessibility-oriented regression tests for the critical controls.

title: Improve operator orientation and safe refresh behavior
description: The current shell has a minimal brand/sidebar, repeated bare  actions, and limited indication of data freshness or which filters are active. Define a small consistent page-toolbar pattern with last-updated/loading/error states, clearer action labels, and preserved filter/navigation state across refresh and route changes. Keep the visual system lightweight and consistent with the existing dark/light themes.

title: Make dense dashboard views usable on narrow screens
description: The responsive layout collapses the sidebar at 860px, but the dashboard relies on dense tables and multi-control filter rows without a documented table overflow/stacking treatment. Exercise dashboard, tasks, logs, workflows, settings, and channels at narrow viewport widths; fix clipping, horizontal scrolling ownership, control wrapping, and touch target sizing while preserving desktop density.

title: Replace Skills with a bundled Extensions center
description:
Build an Extensions center with typed Skills, Workflows, Tools/MCP, Plugins, and Integrations inventories. Add a compiled bundled catalog whose optional capabilities are disabled by default, required core capabilities are non-disableable, configuration-backed enablement requires restart, and runtime state distinguishes available, enabled, active, degraded, skipped, and pending restart. Keep plugin.Plugin metadata-only and use family-owned controllers.

### Acceptance Criteria

Extensions inventories reconcile configured, bundled, discovered, and active state truthfully. Optional bundled capabilities can be enabled or disabled through safe configuration saves; core capabilities cannot. Provider failures and capability health are visible, integrations link to Configuration, and no remote/arbitrary-URL installation path exists. Architecture guard, tests, UI build, task check, viewport inspection, and fresh adversarial review pass.

title: Add safe structured configuration and truthful channel state
description:
Select TOML files, YAML files, or configuration directories through one production format-neutral resolver while retaining the TOML default; expose secret-free effective configuration, schemas, provenance, revision, pending/restart state; validate and atomically patch the owning highest-precedence source with comment preservation and backups; move memory status into Configuration; and report channel lifecycle and supported reload actions through a typed manager.

### Acceptance Criteria

Production composition accepts TOML, YAML, and directory sources with exact precedence/provenance. Candidate validation and optimistic saves handle invalid input, stale/concurrent revisions, permissions and write failures without secret disclosure or running-config mutation. Comments and untouched fields survive. Memory redirects into Configuration. Channels distinguish configured from running health and only supported reloads are actionable. Tests, UI build, task check, viewport inspection, and fresh adversarial review pass.

title: Separate daemon logs and activity and expose executable workflows
description:
Provide a logging-owned bounded daemon slog feed with live stream and optional durable history, keep lifecycle activity on the existing events stream, make selectors truthful, preserve live entries across history refresh, expose the executable workflow registry including zero-run definitions and statistics, and admit Start work requests through normal work intake. Include audit activity for work requests.

### Acceptance Criteria

Live daemon logs continue when durable file history is disabled and the UI explains that limitation. History refresh does not clear or duplicate live entries. Activity remains separate. Workflow inventory includes installed zero-run workflows and ordered stages. Start work validates identity, repository, workflow, title, and instructions and produces an ordinary admitted queued task. Tests, UI build, task check, viewport inspection, and fresh adversarial review pass.

title: Make navigation and task controls operational
description:
Deliver the immediate operator UX slice: always-labelled responsive navigation with compact Jump to search; direct dashboard attention/running links; versioned Setup complete dismissal; lifecycle-safe task controls in expanded and responsive surfaces; and shared taskstate validation for cancel, stop, approve, reject, retry, abandon, PR links, and per-task archive. Preserve same-origin authenticated JSON mutations and emit activity events.

### Acceptance Criteria

Navigation labels and Jump to remain keyboard and screen-reader usable at wide, constrained, 899px, and mobile widths. Dashboard links focus the correct task/filter. Setup dismissal resets when setup becomes incomplete. Every task state exposes only its valid actions and backend optimistic-state checks reject stale or illegal actions. Relevant tests, UI build, task check, live viewport inspection, and fresh adversarial review pass.

title: Keep streamed local-command replies visible in Web chat
description:
The Web chat receives a successful SSE done response for local commands such as /status, renders it, then immediately calls selectSession, which clears the transcript and reloads persisted messages. Local-command exchanges are not persisted, so the command and response disappear. Preserve the live transcript after a successful send while still refreshing session metadata.

### Acceptance Criteria

Sending /status in the Web chat leaves both the user command and returned status visible; normal streamed replies remain visible; session catalogue metadata still refreshes; focused frontend tests and the repository quality gate pass.

title: Fix Web Chat nil update service panic
description: Fix the typed-nil *releaseupdate.Service injected into ChatUpdateService when update checking is unconfigured. Make the Web Chat update endpoints return a controlled not-configured response and add service nil-receiver safety as needed. Preserve the regression test in archie-core-3cf.19 and run focused tests plus task check.

title: Make dashboard authentication and connectivity failures actionable
description: Opening the bare dashboard hash URL returns a raw 401 text response telling the operator to find the startup URL; the authenticated dashboard also showed reconnecting while activity rows were visible. Provide a browser-facing auth recovery state or clear redirect guidance, distinguish initial load failure from SSE reconnecting, and expose a retry path without requiring source or log knowledge. Cover token, API, SSE, and daemon-unavailable states.

title: Add regression test for nil Web Chat update service
description: The Web Chat update endpoint receives a typed-nil *releaseupdate.Service through ChatUpdateService when update checking is unconfigured. Add a regression test proving the endpoint returns a controlled not-configured response instead of panicking. Do not implement the fix in this task.

title: Web Chat: render rich Markdown during streamed replies
description: Telegram drafts render Markdown while a turn is streaming. Web Chat currently appends deltas as plain text and only renders rich output after completion. Keep the live assistant bubble semantically rich throughout SSE updates, including safe handling of partial Markdown.

title: Web Chat: split component markup and presentation files
description:
Refactor the Web Chat out of a large JavaScript-built markup blob. Keep HTML structure in a dedicated template, CSS in dedicated chat styles, Markdown rendering in its own module, and interaction/rendering behavior in focused modules while preserving current API behavior.

### Acceptance Criteria

Chat has dedicated HTML, CSS, Markdown, view, catalog, panel, render, and state modules; chat.js contains only chat-specific coordination and event wiring with no static markup blob; npm tests/build and task check pass; Playwright confirms chat interactions and Markdown rendering.

title: Web Chat: restore Telegram-compatible Markdown rendering
description:
Ensure assistant history and streamed replies render Markdown consistently in the split Web Chat component, matching Telegram-visible formatting. The renderer must remain a dedicated module and be covered by UI and Playwright tests.

### Acceptance Criteria

History and streamed assistant bubbles use the same dedicated safe Markdown renderer; supported Markdown constructs render as semantic HTML; raw markup is not shown for supported constructs; unsafe links remain inert; tests and task check pass.

title: Web Chat: cancel server-side turns from Stop
description: Make the Web Chat Stop action cancel the server-side gateway turn lane and discard queued turns, matching Telegram behavior. Add an authenticated cancel endpoint, wire the shared ChatService to gateway.Turns, and cover API/UI behavior.

title: Chat parity: align shared and Telegram command catalogs
description:
Align command discovery with the commands actually handled by the shared gateway and Telegram adapter while preserving Telegram’s intentional hidden dangerous approval commands.

### Design

Keep command execution unchanged. Extend the existing catalog entries with accurate descriptions and preserve the existing dangerous-command hiding rule; do not duplicate dispatch logic.

### Acceptance Criteria

The shared gateway catalog includes /start and Telegram publishes /start; Telegram’s intentionally hidden /approve and /deny remain executable but undiscoverable; capability-specific dangerous commands remain correctly gated in Web; tests assert the published Telegram menu covers the non-hidden executable command surface.

title: Web Chat: add contextual session lifecycle controls
description:
Expose Telegram session lifecycle actions directly in the Web Chat workspace while continuing to route them through the shared gateway.

### Design

Use a native details popover in the workspace header, prompt only for title/branch names, and keep compression destructive work behind the existing gateway preview command. Do not add Web-only session semantics or duplicate command implementations.

### Acceptance Criteria

An active Web session exposes retry, undo, title, branch, and compression preview actions; actions use shared commands, refresh the selected session/history, handle missing sessions and failures visibly, and remain keyboard accessible. Browser verification covers command dispatch and session refresh.

title: Web Chat: revalidate update snapshot before installation
description:
Make the Web update approval path match Telegram by requiring the displayed snapshot and rechecking available component versions immediately before installation.

### Design

Export the existing releaseupdate available-version comparison instead of duplicating it. Keep the existing in-progress mutex and progress response.

### Acceptance Criteria

Web install requests include the displayed snapshot; the server rejects changed or missing snapshots without installing; unchanged snapshots install once; the shared comparison logic is tested and used by Telegram and Web.

title: Web Chat: render Telegram-style Markdown tables
description:
Extend the Web Chat Markdown renderer to preserve table structure and strikethrough formatting supported by Telegram rich replies.

### Design

Keep the existing dependency-free renderer. Recognize a table only when a header row is immediately followed by a Markdown separator row, parse cells without innerHTML, and reuse inlineMarkdown for cell content.

### Acceptance Criteria

Pipe-delimited Markdown tables render as semantic table/thead/tbody elements with inline formatting; strikethrough renders as del; malformed pipe text remains ordinary text; safe DOM construction is preserved and Playwright verifies the rendered structure.

title: Web Chat: add Telegram-parity slash command palette
description:
Make the Web Chat composer discoverable like Telegram command entry: when the operator types /, show the available shared command catalog, filter it as they type, and allow keyboard or pointer selection to insert a command without submitting it.

### Design

Keep the gateway as the command source of truth. Implement the palette in the vanilla chat composer with role=listbox/option semantics, bounded results, and no new backend endpoint.

### Acceptance Criteria

Typing / opens an accessible command list; filtering matches command names and descriptions; ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter/Escape and pointer selection work; selected commands retain the existing command semantics; the palette uses the capability-aware command catalog returned by the sessions API and is verified in browser.

title: Fix dashboard KPI tiles rendering blank values
description: Authenticated runtime inspection of the supplied dashboard URL showed the first three dashboard stat tiles visually rendered with empty headline values while their comparison text was present; the Tokens used tile rendered 0. Trace the stat tile/render/update path and make every KPI display a stable value during initial load, loading, zero-data, and API-error states. Add focused regression coverage and verify against the live dashboard.
notes: The Tokens-used/Token-outlook portion of this is now tracked in far more depth by archie-core-1786748942590-20-c21c728b (Dashboard: Token outlook is blank because token usage is not reaching daily accounting), which traces the root cause to missing agent_finish event rows (internal/store/events.go:231-251) rather than a rendering bug. If you pick this up, check whether the other KPI tiles (non-token) are still blank independently of that root cause before assuming this issue is just a duplicate of #20 -- the original report named 'the first three dashboard stat tiles', which may be broader than tokens alone.
close_reason: Already fixed by 170fe02 (2026-08-05), predating this bead's 2026-08-08 runtime inspection -- the inspected deployment was serving a stale build. el() in ui/src/base/dom.js was treating a falsy scalar first child (0, '', false) as a missing attrs object and dropping it, so any stat tile whose value was 0 (Working now, Needs you, Tokens used before any usage) rendered a blank headline. Fixed with dedicated regression coverage in ui/test/dom.test.js (el renders a falsy numeric value instead of dropping it, statTile renders a zero headline value, etc.) -- all 9 tests pass. Verified ui/dist rebuilds byte-identical to the committed tree, so the fix ships in the current binary. The token-outlook-specific root cause (missing agent_finish event rows) is tracked separately in archie-core-1786748942590-20-c21c728b per this bead's own notes and is out of scope here.

title: [EPIC] Web UI polish and enhancements
description:
Polish and extend the Archie dashboard against the supplied reference design. Keep the UI a trustworthy operator control room: show real state, explain auth/connectivity failures, remain usable on narrow screens, make interactions accessible, and follow the reference composition and visual system. Existing feature issues for dashboard chat, configuration editing, and logs remain separate unless a child below explicitly coordinates with them.

### Acceptance Criteria

Authenticated dashboard renders meaningful KPI values; unauthorised access has a clear recovery path; core navigation, tables, controls, and task interactions are keyboard/screen-reader usable; dense views remain usable on narrow viewports; the dashboard follows the supplied reference composition and visual treatment; each child has focused UI tests or runtime verification.

title: ContainerRunner: implement agentexec.Runner against Docker for sandboxed execution
description:
Phase 2 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. agentexec.Runner (InProcessRunner/SubprocessRunner) is an interface deliberately designed to be swapped for a container-backed runner without touching workflow orchestration. internal/container/pool.go already handles Docker lifecycle (pull, create, start, release, orphan recovery). Implement ContainerRunner against the existing Runner interface.

### Design

Do not redesign the execution boundary — implement strictly against the existing Runner interface per its doc comments.

### Acceptance Criteria

ContainerRunner implements agentexec.Runner, runs tasks in ephemeral Docker containers with workspace bind-mounted, and is selectable via [agent] mode = "nats" + containers.enabled = true.

title: Eliminate intermittent JetStream TempDir teardown race
description:
An intermittent full-suite race failure shows TestConnectAndPublish cleaning its testing.TempDir while JetStream is still removing the ARCHIE_TASKS msgs directory. The package subsequently passed five race iterations, so the timing window is narrow.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run: go test -race -count=1 ./...
2. Repeat until internal/nats TestConnectAndPublish fails during TempDir RemoveAll with: unlinkat .../jetstream/$G/streams/ARCHIE_TASKS/msgs: directory not empty.
3. Compare with: go test -race -count=5 ./internal/nats.

Make embedded NATS shutdown and storage cleanup deterministic before TempDir cleanup.

### Acceptance Criteria

Repeated race runs of internal/nats and the full repository do not race TempDir cleanup against JetStream file removal; the test explicitly waits for server/storage shutdown.

title: Fix chat command palette keyboard interaction
description:
The chat slash-command palette remains open after the slash is removed or Escape is pressed, and its results cannot be navigated with ArrowUp/ArrowDown. Add regression tests and restore expected keyboard behavior.

### Acceptance Criteria

Backspace/removing the slash closes the palette; Escape closes it; ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the active option; Enter activates the highlighted option; the focused option is exposed accessibly; UI tests and project quality gates pass.

title: Trim the remaining agent skills to factual reference
description:
The .agents/skills/ library is 4283 lines across 12 skills. An audit found most carry useful facts buried in process ceremony. Five worst offenders were already parked at /work/apps/archie-skills-parked. Trim what remains to roughly 2200 lines total. KEEP: concrete commands, package anchors, config wiring tables, NellDB shapes, symptom-to-diagnostic indexes, known regressions, domain glossary, operational hazards, false-confidence warnings. CUT: mandated N-step procedures, handoff templates, evidence packets, acceptance checklists, ownership/deletion/rollback field lists, sibling-skill routing prose, repeated 'reject unless' instructions, dated tool snapshots. Preserve every skill's YAML frontmatter name and description. Do not delete any skill file outright.

### Acceptance Criteria

Total line count of .agents/skills/*/*.md is between 1900 and 2500. All 12 skills still exist with valid frontmatter. No factual command, path, or table was lost - only procedure and ceremony. go build ./... still clean.

title: SOUL cannot override the prompt invariants
description:
Enforce the boundary that makes SOUL safe to hand to users: it supplies identity and style, and cannot reach the instruction hierarchy, core rules, tool inventory or env block.

### Acceptance Criteria

A test renders a hostile SOUL that attempts to countermand core_rules and asserts the invariant sections are still present and intact. The boundary is documented where the layering rule already lives so the next person editing the template does not quietly relax it.
close_reason: Wrapped SOUL/Persona in an XML-escaped, trust=data <soul> block rendered before the invariant tags; added TestBuildSystemPromptSoulCannotOverrideInvariants; documented the enforcement in identity.md

title: Memory engine contract and owning registry
description:
Define the typed memory engine interface and the registry that owns provider registration, discovery, and lifecycle. This is the load-bearing design step: everything else in the epic is written against this contract.

### Acceptance Criteria

A typed interface exposes real memory operations beyond identity metadata. An owning Registry/Manager controls registration, init, start, health, and stop, and defines failure isolation and shutdown ordering. Providers receive only a typed registrar and the host services their capability declares. internal/plugin/architecture_test.go passes with memory recognised as a conforming engine family. Stateless providers may declare explicit no-op lifecycle.
notes: Not started as a conforming engine family. The existing internal/memory package (provider.go, lifecycle.go, backup.go, etc.) predates the domain migration: it has an ad-hoc MemoryProvider interface plus several optional hook interfaces (TurnStartHook, SessionEndHook, ...), but no owning Registry/Manager, no narrow typed registrar, and no Manifest-style declared shape -- it does not follow the strict plugin engine rule that internal/domain/curator (archie-core-1786637499933-386-83646cce, now closed) already demonstrates as the reference implementation. Confirmed via go test ./internal/plugin/... -run TestEveryEngineInterfaceHasTypedCapabilityAndFamilyOwner -v: only domain/curator.CuratorEngine, secret.Engine, and tools/provider.Engine are currently recognised conforming families -- no memory family. Use internal/domain/curator's contract.go/registry.go/registrar.go split as the template; do not extend internal/memory's MemoryProvider in place.
close_reason:
Complete: internal/domain/memory/{contract,registrar,registry}.go stands up
memory as a conforming engine family, mirroring internal/domain/curator's
split exactly per this issue's own notes.

MemoryEngine (contract.go) embeds Lifecycle (Start/Health/Stop) and Store
(Write/Query/List/Forget -- real operations, not identity metadata) plus
Name/Version/Manifest/Bind. Store is split out as its own embedded
interface so MemoryEngine stays under golangci-lint's interfacebloat
threshold, same mechanism as curator's embedded Lifecycle.

Registry (registry.go) owns Register/Get/Names/Start/Health/Stop with
duplicate/nil-engine/panic-in-Bind rejection, per-engine Start failure
isolation (one engine's failed Start does not block the others, and is
reported via Health), ctx-bounded Stop, and reverse-registration-order
shutdown -- all verified by registry_test.go, mirroring curator's test
suite. go test ./internal/domain/memory/... -race -count=1 is green;
task lint is 0 issues.
