title: Config surface for memory engine selection and settings
description:
Add validated configuration for choosing a memory engine and supplying its per-engine settings, following the existing config conventions in internal/config and internal/infrastructure/configuration.

### Acceptance Criteria

Engine choice and per-engine settings are expressible in config.toml with toml/yaml/json tags matching repo convention. Validation rejects an unknown engine name with a clear error naming the valid set, in the style of the existing forge.type validation. Defaults resolve so an absent section keeps the builtin engine. config.example.toml documents the section.
close_reason:
Complete, all four AC clauses:

- config.MemoryConfig.Engine field added with toml/yaml/json tags;
  Provider/ProviderConfig/SessionTTL also gained the toml tags they were
  missing (repo convention, config.toml is the primary format).
- validateMemory (internal/infrastructure/configuration/validate.go)
  rejects an engine name outside memoryEngines with
  "%w: memory.engine %q (want %s)", the same named-constant-list +
  oneOf/list shape forge.type already uses. TestValidateMemoryNames
  TheValidSet pins the exact message.
- applyMemoryDefaults resolves an absent engine to "builtin"
  (memoryEngineBuiltin), verified by
  TestApplyMemoryDefaultsFillsAbsentEngineWithBuiltin, and an explicit
  value is left alone (TestApplyMemoryDefaultsLeavesExplicitValuesAlone).
- config.example.toml documents [memory] engine alongside the existing
  provider field, distinguishing the two mechanisms.

Since closing this, archie-core-1786637499480 (ship builtin as default)
landed the bootstrap wiring that actually consumes cfg.Memory.Engine, so
the field is not just parsed and validated but live end to end.

title: Telegram: provider selector filters model choices
description:
Add an authorized native /provider inline selector. The selected provider scopes /model so only configured model references belonging to that provider are shown; e.g. openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6 must not appear under provider openai. Selecting a provider establishes a valid active model for that provider when necessary, and /status reports active provider and model.

### Acceptance Criteria

/provider displays configured providers as an inline keyboard and marks the active provider. Authorized callbacks switch provider; unauthorized, malformed, stale, and duplicate callbacks fail safely. /model shows only models whose first reference segment matches the selected provider and uses unambiguous labels. Switching provider leaves the chat responder on a valid model from that provider. /status includes active provider and full model reference. Menu/help/executable parity and concurrent access are tested.
close_reason: Superseded: confirmed by Sam that there is no longer a separate /provider command -- grepped the codebase and no '/provider' command exists in internal/gateway or internal/channels/telegram. /model now handles provider scoping directly.

title: Document the memory engine family in ARCHITECTURE.md
description:
Record the memory engine family alongside the existing engine documentation so the contract, its lifecycle guarantees, and the trust boundary for third-party memory backends are written down where the plugin engine rule already lives.

### Acceptance Criteria

ARCHITECTURE.md describes the memory engine contract, its owning manager, lifecycle and failure isolation, and states the trust boundary for an out-of-process or third-party memory backend. The shared CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md source is updated if the rule surface changes.
close_reason: Documented the memory engine contract, owning manager, lifecycle/failure isolation, and third-party trust boundary in ARCHITECTURE.md; focused memory tests pass.

title: fix(telegram): honour retry_after on 429 instead of the library's fixed backoff
description:
go-telegram/bot v1.22.0 get_updates.go discards TooManyRequestsError.RetryAfter and applies its own 100ms-doubling backoff capped at 5s. Against retry_after:5 that is ~12 further requests inside the silence window, which escalated a brief 429 on carina into sustained 429s, 502s and request timeouts over several minutes.

Fixed in internal/channels/telegram/ratelimit.go: WithErrorsHandler is invoked synchronously from the polling loop before the library applies its own backoff, so blocking there honours the interval without patching the dependency. errors.As unwraps the library's fmt.Errorf wrap; capped at maxRetryAfter=60s; releases immediately on context cancellation so /restart during a 429 does not block.

Upstream report drafted for https://github.com/go-telegram/bot/issues -- suggested fix is to prefer RetryAfter over incErrTimeout in the error branch.

title: Curator observability surface
description:
Give curator activity visibility: which curators are registered, when each last ran, what it changed, and why. Background agents mutating memory unobserved is the failure mode this epic most needs to avoid.

### Acceptance Criteria

Registered curators, their schedule state, and their recent activity are inspectable at runtime. Each recorded action carries enough context to answer why it happened. Surfaced through the existing observability paths rather than a bespoke channel.
notes: Half-built: the data this needs already exists but nothing surfaces it. internal/domain/curator/registry.go has Health(ctx) map[string]Health and Names() []string; every pass emits an Action (At/Type/Detail/Reason) and a run event through the curator's EventSink. daemon.Daemon.Curators *curator.Registry (internal/daemon/daemon.go:107-110) holds the live registry. But grep confirms no webui/API/dashboard code reads any of it -- internal/webui has zero curator-aware endpoints, ui/src has no curator surface. This issue is 'wire the existing Registry.Health/Names + action history into the existing observability paths (health endpoint / dashboard)', not 'build the data model from scratch'.
close_reason: Wired GET /api/curators (names, health, last-run, recent actions) backed by a new bounded in-memory activity tracker in internal/domain/curator, plus a Curators dashboard page at ui/src/curators/.

title: CLI: technical design interview and PRD for command surface
description:
Run a technical design interview with Sam before making any CLI implementation decisions. Produce a reviewed PRD/specification for the user-facing archie CLI: goals, personas, installation/distribution, configuration and state model, commands/subcommands/flags, output and machine-readable contracts, auth/host targeting, update lifecycle, error semantics, compatibility/migration, and acceptance tests. The eventual implementation must use urfave/cli/v3; do not use or introduce urfave/cli/v2. No CLI code is in scope until Sam approves the resulting PRD.

### Acceptance Criteria

Interview captures Sam's intended CLI workflows and non-goals; PRD defines the complete command surface and state/transport ownership without assumptions; PRD specifies urfave/cli/v3; Sam explicitly approves the PRD before implementation work is created.

title: feat(config): optional file logging
description: archied writes slog JSON to stdout only; under systemd journald is the sole copy, and running by hand leaves nothing. Add a log_file config field so there is a durable copy independent of journald. Prerequisite for the webui logs view showing anything from before the dashboard connected.

title: fix(gateway): make /compress failure-safe
description: applyCompress swallows MessageCount and DeleteRecentMessages errors (allCount, _ := and _, _ =) then deletes all messages BEFORE saving the compressed replacement. A crash or error between the two loses the session's entire history unrecoverably. Add a store-level ReplaceMessages that saves first and deletes the previously-listed IDs after, so the failure mode is recoverable duplicates rather than total loss.

title: [BUG] /model <name> asked the router for a doubled model name
description:
The nestif extraction in 651de0a pulled --provider parsing out of parseModelRest into extractProviderFlag, which took the modelParts slice by pointer and appended every non-provider field to it. The caller's own loop then appended the same fields again, so every field of the model name was duplicated: '/model gpt-5.6' resolved to 'gpt-5.6 gpt-5.6' and SetActiveModel rejected it as an unknown model. '/model gpt-5.6 --provider openai' was worse -- the space-separated provider value was no longer consumed with its flag, giving 'gpt-5.6 gpt-5.6 openai'. Direct model switching over Telegram was broken for anything but a bare --refresh or a provider-only switch. Found while auditing 6d4e0be for archie-core-ifi: the naked return in the same function could not be regression-tested until the function produced correct values.

### Design

Two ways to fix the double append were available. Rejected: keep the helper
signature and delete the caller's default-branch append. That restores correct
output but leaves the shape intact -- a helper holding a pointer to the
caller's accumulator, with two loops over the same fields -- so the next person
who adds a field type has the same trap waiting. It also does not fix the
space-separated provider value, because the helper returns early on the first
--provider and never sees the fields after it.

Chosen: splitProviderFlag returns (provider, remaining) and is the sole
accumulator. One loop owns the fields, and there is no shared slice to append
to twice. The index loop is kept deliberately -- i++ after reading a
space-separated value is what removes it with its flag, and converting that to
a range loop is precisely what 651de0a did wrong.

Last --provider wins if repeated, matching the pre-651de0a behaviour rather
than the buggy helper's first-wins. Not worth a flag: /model does not document
repeating it.

### Acceptance Criteria

parseModelRest returns the model name exactly once for bare names, scope flags, and both --provider spellings, with a regression test asserting field count rather than string equality.

title: Trigger accounting: curator output must not feed its own trigger
description:
Establish the invariant that work a curator produces does not count toward the condition that schedules the next curator run. The scheduler must explicitly exclude derived curator output from the observation threshold: counting it would inflate the threshold and create a feedback loop, so a curator that writes memories must not thereby schedule itself again.

### Acceptance Criteria

Derived curator output is distinguishable from primary input at the point the trigger is evaluated. A curator that writes memories does not thereby schedule itself again. There is a regression test that would fail if derived output were counted, with the feedback-loop rationale recorded in the test so the guard is not removed as redundant.
close_reason: Complete: internal/domain/curator/wake.go WakeOnPrimaryInput forwards only explicitly-passed inputKinds; curator-produced kinds (curator_run, curator_action, curator_error) are structurally excluded, per its own doc comment naming this exact invariant. internal/domain/curator/wake_test.go:11-21 TestWakeOnPrimaryInputForwardsOnlyPrimaryKinds carries the required feedback-loop rationale verbatim ('if derived curator output counted... a curator that writes memories would schedule itself again... This test fails if a derived kind is added to the forwarded set or the filter is removed as redundant') and asserts passCalls/checkCalls stay at 1 after publishing derived-kind events. All three acceptance-criteria clauses satisfied exactly.

title: ui: extract duplicated Pill component to ui/src/base/
description: organisation.md's frontend rule says extract to ui/src/base/ on the second distinct consumer. Pill (a 3-line status-badge component) is already independently duplicated verbatim across 11 files: tasks.jsx, logs.jsx, mapping-editor.jsx, capture-row.jsx, settings.jsx, update-status.jsx, skills.jsx, dashboard.jsx, memory.jsx, channels.jsx, curators.jsx. Pre-existing debt, not introduced by any single feature -- found while building the bindings UI (archie-core-t2db.8), which would have been a 12th copy.
design: Extract to ui/src/base/pill.jsx, export Pill, update all 11+ call sites to import from there instead of defining locally. Mechanical refactor -- no behavior change, verify with task test:ui.
acceptance_criteria: ui/src/base/pill.jsx exists and exports Pill; all prior local definitions removed, all call sites import the shared one; task test:ui passes unchanged.
close_reason: Extracted to ui/src/base/pill.jsx, all 12 call sites updated (11 pre-existing + bindings). Verified via task test:ui (120/120) and real browser re-check across all pages given this touches the same rendering path as the earlier Preact regression fix. Commit 2abccf3.

title: skillcurator: nilerr finding at skillcurator.go:110 (pre-existing, unrelated to EDA work)
description: task check's newly-added lint step (chore(taskfile) 60dde24) surfaced internal/infrastructure/skillcurator/skillcurator.go:110 -- returns nil despite a non-nil error at line 108 (nilerr). This is pre-existing debt, unrelated to any EDA/playbook engine work this session -- different subsystem entirely. Filed separately per this session's established pattern (see archie-core-e7bo) of not drive-by fixing unrelated findings inside an in-progress feature's tickets.
design: Read the actual code at skillcurator.go:108-110 before fixing -- determine whether swallowing the error there was ever intentional (check git blame/history) or a genuine bug, and fix at the producer per AGENTS.md's Root-Cause Fixes rule rather than just propagating the error blindly if the surrounding contract expects a specific degrade-gracefully shape.
acceptance_criteria: golangci-lint run ./... reports zero nilerr findings in internal/infrastructure/skillcurator/. Existing skillcurator tests pass; add a test covering the error path if none currently exercises it. task check passes.
close_reason: Investigated per design notes: intentional behavior, not a bug -- confirmed against existing test coverage (skillcurator_test.go's parse-failure-doesn't-abort-batch test). Documented with a scoped nolint explaining why, not a behavior change. Commit pushed to main.

title: Adapt internal/tools/minimax to ai-sdk's video.Provider interface
description:
internal/tools/minimax (the generate_video tool) is a hand-rolled HTTP client (Config/Client/GenerateAndWait against MiniMax's video-generation API) that duplicates functionality ai-sdk already provides generically: video.Provider (Name/GenerateVideo(ctx,req)(resp,error)), core.GenerateVideo, and registry.RegisterVideo/.Video(name) -- the same registration shape chat models and the new image capability use. MiniMax's async submit-then-poll GenerateAndWait fits behind video.Provider's single blocking call fine; nothing about the interface forces synchronous-only backends.

Currently: not extensible (a second video backend would have to duplicate all the HTTP/poll scaffolding instead of just implementing video.Provider) and not reusable (can't be registered/discovered alongside a future video provider the way chat models and image providers can).

Fix: wrap minimax.Client behind an adapter implementing ai-sdk's video.Provider, register it via registry.RegisterVideo instead of the tool holding a bespoke *minimax.Client directly. Keep minimax.Client itself as the low-level HTTP/poll implementation -- only the tool-facing seam changes.
design: Mirrors the note left on archie-core-1786748942169-3-ae7cfaea for the hosted image provider: adapt ai-sdk's existing provider-agnostic facility instead of a bespoke client. Adapter should preserve GenerateAndWait's polling behavior internally -- video.Provider's synchronous call shape does not require changing MiniMax's async job semantics, only where the polling loop is invoked from.
acceptance_criteria: minimax.Client (or a thin adapter) implements ai-sdk/video.Provider; the generate_video tool obtains it through the ai-sdk provider registry, not a bespoke config-to-client wiring; existing tests (minimax_test.go, tool_test.go) still pass or are updated for the new seam; task check passes.

title: send_file confinement is symlink-blind and re-opens the file after checking it
description:
internal/tools/builtin/confinement.go ResolveReadable applies exactly the read tool's policy (resolvePath + isReadConfined), which is purely lexical: filepath.Abs/Rel, never EvalSymlinks. A symlink inside the workspace pointing at /etc/shadow passes the check, and the telegram sender then opens att.Path with no confinement check of its own, in a different goroutine after the turn. There is also a real TOCTOU window -- prepare stats/opens/closes, SendMedia re-stats and re-opens later.

The policy is unchanged from the read tool, so this is not a new hole; what changed is the consequence. The read tool caps at 5MB into the operator's own context; send_file ships up to 50MB OUT to a chat. The shell tool has never been confined either, so a model that wants the bytes already has them.

Decide: either resolve symlinks in ResolveReadable (which changes read-tool behaviour too, and may break legitimate symlinked workspaces), or document the caveat explicitly and stop claiming 'sending cannot reach what reading cannot' without it.

Found by adversarial review of 9a45fbb.

## Acceptance Criteria
Either the symlink case is closed at the resolver, or the limitation is written down where the claim is made (confinement.go doc comment and sendfile package doc).

title: Honor cancellation before local worktree commits
description:
CommitAll discards its context and can stage and commit after task cancellation.

Confirmed still present on main: `Manager.CommitAll` (internal/worktree/worktree.go:387) takes `_ context.Context` and never reads it. Between entry and `wt.Commit` it performs `AddWithOptions{All: true}` and `wt.Commit`, neither of which is context-aware in go-git, so a task cancelled just before the call still mutates the index and HEAD.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Prepare a task worktree with uncommitted changes.
2. Create an already-cancelled context: `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel()`.
3. Call `Manager.CommitAll(ctx, dir, "msg")`.
4. Observe it returns `(true, nil)`: the index was staged and a new commit is on HEAD despite the context being cancelled before the call.
5. In production this leaves a commit on the task branch for work the operator cancelled, which the subsequent push/PR path can then publish.

## Acceptance Criteria

A pre-canceled context causes no index or HEAD mutation; cancellation is checked between non-context-aware go-git phases where possible, with regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: A pre-canceled context causes no index or HEAD mutation; cancellation is checked between non-context-aware go-git phases where possible, with regression tests.
close_reason: Fixed: CommitAll now takes a live context and checks ctx.Err() before open, worktree, staging, status and commit (worktree.go:398-430), so a pre-cancelled context mutates neither index nor HEAD. Proven red against pre-fix code: 'CommitAll() error = nil, want context canceled' for both a cancelled context and an expired deadline. task check green; fresh adversarial review zero findings.

title: agent: markWorktreeSafe checks existence, not mount-ness, so a stale dir writes to the operator's gitconfig
description:
markWorktreeSafe gates on os.Stat (existence and dir-ness), not mount-ness, despite the doc comment claiming a 'mount' check so host-mode agents don't write to the operator's own ~/.gitconfig for a path that was never mounted (commit 6b46ea1's stated purpose). A directory that merely exists at /data/worktree (a stale leftover) satisfies the guard and appends safe.directory=/data/worktree to the operator's gitconfig. Low severity — the entry is inert unless a repo exists at that exact path — but the guard's behavior does not match its documented contract, and the exists-but-not-a-mount case is untested.

Failure: a host-mode agent (local-ollama-standalone.toml) on a machine with a leftover /data directory: an extra safe.directory line appears in the operator's ~/.gitconfig, exactly what the guard claims to prevent.
design: Either implement a real mount check (e.g. /proc/self/mountinfo on Linux) or correct the doc comment to say the guard is existence-based and accept the (inert) entry. Decide which contract is intended.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior matches the documented contract; the exists-but-not-mounted case is covered by a test, or the doc is corrected.
close_reason: Corrected markSafe's doc comment to match its actual existence-based (not mount-based) check; pinned the exists-but-unmounted case with a new test rather than adding platform-specific mount detection for an inert failure mode. Committed f1d74ab.

title: Concurrent send_file uploads in one turn are uncapped
description:
liveReply.Media starts an unbounded mediaWg.Go per attachment. Not a leak (each is bounded by a 30s ctx) and not a memory problem (go-telegram streams via io.Pipe, nothing is buffered), but N send_file calls in one turn start N concurrent multipart uploads against a rate-limited API.

Also noted: send_file is ClassIdempotent, which makes it ExecParallelSafe. Defensible since the tool only validates and never sends, but minimax is ClassMutating for an equivalent 'produces an outbound artifact' tool -- worth deciding deliberately rather than by accident.

Found by adversarial review of 9a45fbb. internal/channels/telegram/live.go:386.

## Acceptance Criteria
Either a bound on concurrent media sends per reply, or a recorded decision that the 30s timeout plus Telegram's own rate limiting is sufficient.

title: telegram: the live-edit answer keeps its turn-start timestamp and can sort before the conversation
description:
The final reply is delivered by editing the message created at the first streamed frame, and editMessageText does not change the message date — so a long tool-using turn's answer is timestamped at turn start, can predate messages sent during the turn, and sorts before the conversation that produced it. Cosmetic and inherent to the watch-the-answer-being-written design (delete-and-resend would flicker and reorder), but it is a visible consequence nothing documents or tests.

Failure: a turn with a two-minute tool phase produces an answer whose timestamp precedes a follow-up user message that references it; chat history ordering places the answer before the conversation that produced it.
design: Either accept and document the limitation (a comment on liveReply/finalize), or investigate a delete-and-resend on finalize for turns that cross a meaningful time gap. Low priority; a documentation note may be the right fix.
acceptance_criteria: The timestamp behavior is at least documented (or changed and tested), so it is a known trade-off rather than a surprise.
close_reason: Documented the accepted trade-off on liveReply's doc comment per the design note's preferred option; no behavior change. Committed ed18bfb.
